# Markandeya-purana

## Chapter 1

## ārambhamaṅgalam

*yadyogibhirbhavabhayārtivināśayogyam*  
*āsādya vanditamatīva vivaktacittaiḥ*  
*tadvaḥ punātu haripādasarojayugmam*  
*avirbhavatkramavilaṅghitabhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*

*pāyāt sa vaḥ sakalakalmaṣabhedadakṣaḥ kṣīrodakukṣiphaṇibhoganiviṣṭamūrtiḥ śvāsāvadhūtasalilotkaṇikākarālaḥ*  
*sindhuḥ pranṛtyamiva yasya karoti saṅgāt*

*nārāyaṇaṃ samaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam \|*  
*devīṃ sarasvatīṃ vyāsaṃ tato jayamudīrayet*

MayVishnu's lotus-feet, which power have To dissipate the woes wrought by the fear Of existence, and which are lauded high By ascetics, assiduous, whose minds From all things else are rapt - may those same feet, Whose steps the earth, the sky, and heaven o'erpassed, To sight appearing, purify your souls!

May He protect you, who is skilled to save In every kind of sin impure; whose form Within the bosom of the sea of milk Upon the hooded snake reclines; and at Whose touch the sea grows mountainous, its spray Up-tossing from its waters by his breath Disturbed, and into seeming dancing breaks!

Jaimini applies to Márkandeya for instruction regarding certain difficulties in the Mahábhárata -Márkandeya refers him to four learned Birds, the sons of Drona, and narrates their history -Their mother Vapu, and Apsaras, was condemned by the Muni Durvásas to become a bird for tempting him.

Having adored Náráyana, and Nara the best of men, the goddess Sarasvatí, and then Vyása, let him utter the verse of Victory!

## Chapter 2

## \|\| 2.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ariṣṭanemiputro 'bhūd garuḍo nāma pakṣirāṭ \|*  
*garuḍasyābhavat putraḥ sampātiriti viśrutaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The story of the Birds continued -Kandhara, king of the birds killed a Rákhasa Vidyud-rúpa for killing his brother, and, marrying the Rákhasa's wife, had a daughter by her named Tárkshí who was the Apsaras Vapu -She married Drona -When pregnant by him she was killed at the battle of the Kauravas and Pándavas, and there laid four eggs from which the four Birds were born -The Birds were nourished by the Muni S'amika.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. The king of the birds, Garuda by name, was the son of

## Chapter 3

## \|\| 3.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ahanyahani viprendra sa teṣāṃ munisattamaḥ \|*  
*cakārāhārapayasā tathā guptyā ca poṣaṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Story of the Birds continued -The Birds, when fullgrown, were endowed with speech, and explained that wonder to the Muni Samika -They were the four sons of a Rishi Sukrisha -Indra appeared to the Rishi in the form of an aged bird, and asked for human flesh -The Rishi ordered his four sons to sacrifice themselves - They refused, and he cursed them to be born in the brute creation, but, moved with compassion at their entreaty, bestowed on them perfect knowledge -Hence they were born as birds.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Thus he, the most virtuous Muni, O princely brahman, nourished them day by day with food and water, and in safety.

## \|\| 3.2 \|\|

*māsamātreṇa jagmuste bhānoḥ syandanavartmani \|*

2\. After a month they resorted to the sun's chariot-road, being gazed at by the Munis' sons, whose eyes were tremulous

## \|\| 3.3 \|\|

3\. with curiosity.After seeing the earth, with its cities, and with its ocean and noble rivers, which appeared of the size

## \|\| 3.4 \|\|

## Chapter 8

## \|\| 8.1 \|\|

*jaiminiruvāca*  
*bhavadbhiridamākhyātaṃ yathāpraśnamanukramāt \|*  
*mahat kautūhalaṃ me 'sti hariścandra kathāṃ prati \|\| 1 \|\|*

Visvámitra not satisfied demands further fees, and Haris-c'andra in desperation sells his wife and his son to a brahman and himself to a c'andála, and gives Visvámitra all the price -Haris-c'andra earns his livelihood as the c'andála's servant at a burning-ground in the most abject state for a year -Then he sees a vision of his future transmigrations with a promise of happiness ultimately -His son is bitten by a snake, and the queen brings the corpse to the burning-ground - They recognise each other and bewail their misfortunes -Both resolve to immolate themselves on their son's funeral pile; but the gods interpose and restore his son to life -Dharma explains that he had personated the c'andála -Indra calls the king to Svarga, but he refuses to go without his faithful people -He, and his queen and people ascend to Svarga in perfect bliss.

Jaimini spoke:

1\. Ye have declared this in order according to my questions: great is my curiosity regarding the story of Haris-c'andra.

## \|\| 8.2 \|\|

*aho mahātmanā tena prāptaṃ kṛcchramanuttamam \|*  
*kaccit sukhamanuprāptaṃ tādṛgeva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Ah! passing great was the woe incurred by that magnanimous king; I trust he obtained a happiness fully commensurate, O brahmans!

The birds spoke:

## \|\| 8.3 \|\|

*pakṣiṇa ūcuḥ*

*vasānisyandasaṃśuṣka-mahīpuṭakamaṇḍite \|*

206\. remains of sacrificial ceremonies and strings; where the cavities of the dry ground are bedecked with oily exudations; which is dreadful by reason of the mixing of the marrow and half-burnt bones with the ashes and charcoal; where the

## \|\| 8.207 \|\|

*gṛdhra-gomāyunādārtanaṣṭakṣudravihaṅgame \|*  
*citādhūmātatirucā nīlīkṛtadigantare \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. small birds have been scared away by the cries of the vultures and jackals; which has spread gloom over the regions of the sky with the colour of the trails of smoke from

208\. the funeral piles; where the night-roaming demons are joyful through the delight of tasting carrion."

## \|\| 8.209 \|\|

*evamuktvā samāśliṣya kaṇṭhaṃ rājño nṛpātmajā \|*  
*kaṣṭaśokaśatādhārā vilalāpārtayā girā \|\| 209 \|\|*

209.Thus having spoken the princess embraced the king's neck and, bearing hundreds of woes and griefs, lamented with sorrowful voice, -

The queen spoke:

## \|\| 8.210 \|\|

*rājapatnyuvāca*  
*rājan ! svapno 'tha tathyaṃ vā yadetanmanyate bhavān \|*  
*tat kathyatāṃ mahābhāga mano vai muhyate mama \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. "O king, is it sleep or waking truth? Tell me Sir, this that thou art thinking of: my mind is bewildered indeed.

## \|\| 8.211 \|\|

*yadyetadevaṃ dharmajña nāsti dharme sahāyatā \|*  
*tathaiva vipradevādipūjane pālane bhuvaḥ \|\| 211 \|\|*

*nāsti dharmaḥ kutaḥ satyamārjavaṃ cānṛśaṃsatā \|*

212\. and others, nor in protecting the world; there is no such thing as righteousness. Whence are there truth, and candour, and meekness, in that thou, the devotee of righteousness, hast been ousted from thy kingdom?"

## \|\| 8.213 \|\|

*iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā niśvasyoṣṇaṃ sagadgadam \|*

213\. Hearing this her speech, sighing deeply he related in faltering accents to the slender-limbed lady, how he had

*ruditvā sāpi suciraṃ niśvasyoṣṇañca duḥ khitā \|*

The king spoke:

215\. "My darling, I choose not to undergo affliction for a long time, nor is my soul docile, O slender-limbed lady. Behold

*caṇḍālenānanujñātaḥ pravekṣye jvalanaṃ yadi \|*

216\. my ill-fortune. If I shall enter the fire, with the permission of the c'andála, I shall in another birth go again into

217\. bondage to c'andálas. I shall fall into Naraka, as a wormeating insect; into Vaitariní which is slimy with much pus,

## \|\| 8.218 \|\|

*asipatravane prāpya chedaṃ prāpsyāmi dāruṇam \|*

218\. fat, blood, and sinews. Reaching the Asi-patra wood, I shall be frightfully cut to pieces; or reaching Mahá-raurava

*magnasya duḥ khajaladhau pāraḥ prāṇaviyojanam \|*

219\. and Raurava I shall be burnt. Surrender of life is the shore for one sunk in the ocean of grief. I had just one son, who

220\. was this boy, to continue my family. He too has sunk through the violence of the waters of my Fate, which are very strong. How shall I resign my life? I am dependent

221\. on others, and in a strait. Or, does not a man afflicted with pain regard evil?There is no such suffering in the brute

*vaitaraṇyāṅkutastādṛg yādṛśaṃ putraviplave \|*

222\. creation, nor in theAsi-patra forest. Whence is there such suffering inVaitariní as in the bereavement of a son? I will

223\. fall then with my son's body into the blazing fire, O slender-limbed! Thou must pardon my ill-deeds; and do thou who hast my permission go to the brahman's house, O bright

248\. "O king of the gods, adoration to thee! hearken also to this my speech, that, filled with affection, I speak to thee whose

*macchokamagnamanasaḥ kośalānagare janāḥ \|*

*brahmahatyā gurorghāto govadhaḥ strīvadhastathā \|*

The birds spoke:

## \|\| 8.269 \|\|

*pakṣiṇa ūcuḥ*  
*etat te sarvamākhyātaṃ hariścandraviceṣṭitam \|*

*vipāko rājasūyasya pṛthivīkṣayakāraṇam \|*  
*tadvipākanimittañca yuddhamāḍibakaṃ mahat \|\| 270 \|\|*

270\. O best of Munis! the outcome of the Rája-súya sacrifice, which was the cause of the decay of the earth, and the cause of that outcome, viz. the great battle of the Mainá and Heron.

## Chapter 9

## \|\| 9.1 \|\|

*pakṣiṇa ūcuḥ*  
*rājyacyute hariścandre gate ca tridaśālayam \|*  
*niścakrāma mahātejā jalavāsāt purohitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vasistha, enraged with Visvámitra for his cruelty to Haris-c'andra, cursed him to become a heron, and Visvámitra cursed Vasistha to become a mainá -Both Munis as gigantic birds have a terrible fight, and are at length pacified by Brahmá.

The birds spoke:

## Chapter 10

## \|\| 10.1 \|\|

*jaiminiruvāca*

Jaimini asks the Birds for instruction how living beings come into existence and die, and how the foetus lives and develops -The Birds repeat the explanation that a wise young brahman Sumati, who was nick-named Jada because of his apparent stupidity, but who remembered his former existences, gave his father -He explains how death occurs, and describes the after-existences through which a living being passes according as it has lived well or ill -He describes incidentally the hell Raurava.

1\. Declare my doubt, when I enquire, O powerful bráhmans, wherein the appearance and disappearance of living beings

*bhakṣyāṇi yatra no janturjoryate kathamalpakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. him? Why does the foetus not become digested there in the stomach, as if it were converted into a morsel of food? In the female's belly, where the various foods consumed are digested although highly indigestible, how is it that the little animal

*tadetat parama guhyaṃ yatra muhyanti jantavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

Yama's officer tells king Vipas-c'it why he was condemned to hell -He explains to him the nature and results of good and evil deeds generally, and mentions at great length the punishments awarded to various special sins.

*vipracittimukhairdevā dānavaiste parājitāḥ \|*

*garga uvāca*  
*hantu śaktā na sandeho dactatreyaprasādataḥ \|*

142\. "Thus exhorted the gods then went to Dattátreya's hermitage, and they beheld the high-souled Muni, attended by

## \|\| 16.144-146 \|\|

*te tasya gatvā praṇatimavadan sādhyasādhanam \|*

And the heaven-dwellers lauded him; they offered him food, viands, garlands and other presents; when he stood, they stood near; when he moved, they moved; when he reposed on his seat, they worshipped him with heads down-bent. Dattátreya addressed the prostrate gods, 'What desire ye of me, that ye do me this obeisance?'

The gods spoke:

## \|\| 16.147 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*dānavairmuniśārdūla jambhādyairbhūrbhuvādikam \|*

147\. 'The Dánavas, headed by Jambha, have attacked and seized upon the earth the atmosphere and the third world, O tiger

*tadvadhe kuru buddhiṃ tvaṃ paritrāṇāya no 'nagha \|*

Dattátreya spoke:

## \|\| 16.149 \|\|

*dattātreya uvāca*  
*madyāsakto 'hamucchiṣṭo na caivāhaṃ jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*kathamicchatha matto 'pi devāḥ śatruparābhavam \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. 'I am drinking strong drink, I have remnants of food in my mouth, nor have I subdued my senses. How is it, O gods, ye seek for victory over your enemies even from me?'

150\. 'Thou art sinless, O lord of the world; no stain hast thou, into whose heart, purified by the ablution of learning, has entered the light of knowledge.'

Dattátreya spoke:

## \|\| 16.151 \|\|

*dattātreya uvāca*  
*satyametat surā vidyā mamāsti samadarśinaḥ \|*  
*asyāstu yoṣitaḥ saṅgādahamucchiṣṭatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. 'True is this, O gods! all learning have I, who am impartial in view: but by reason of association with this woman I

## \|\| 16.152 \|\|

*strīsambhogo hi doṣāya sātatyenopasevitaḥ \|*  
*evamuktāstato devāḥ punarvacanamabruvan \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. am now impure after eating. For commerce with women when continually pursued tends to depravity.' Thus addressed, the gods then spoke again.

The gods spoke:

## \|\| 16.153-154 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*anagheyaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha jaganmātā na duṣyate \|*  
*yāsā vidyā tava vibho sarvajñasya hadi sthitā \|\| 153 \|\|*

*yathāṃśumālā sūryasya dvija-cāṇḍālasaṅginī \|*

Garga spoke:

155\. "Thus accosted by the gods, Dattátreya then with a smile spoke thus to all the thirty gods; - 'If this be your opinion,

157\. and bring them here before my view -delay ye not -in order that the glory of their strength may be consumed by the fire of my glance, and that they may all perish from my sight.'

## \|\| 16.158 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devairdaityā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*āhavāya samāhūtā jagmurdevagaṇān ruṣā \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. "The valiant Daityas, summoned to battle by the gods in compliance with that his advice, advanced with fury against

*te hanyamānā daiteyairdevā śīghraṃ bhayāturāḥ \|*

159\. the troops of the gods. The gods being slaughtered by the Daityas were quickly demoralised by fear; they fled in a

160\. body, seeking protection, to Dattátreya's hermitage. Even there the Daityas penetrated, driving forward the heavendwellers, and saw the high-souled mighty Dattátreya; and

161\. seated at his left side his wife, Lakshmí, loved by all the worlds, beauteous, her shape most graceful, her countenance

*nīlotpalābhanayanāṃ pīnaśroṇipayodharām \|*

162\. like the moon, her eyes lustrous as the blue water-lily, her hips large and breasts full, uttering melodious speech, adorned

## \|\| 16.163 \|\|

*te tāṃ dṛṣṭvāgrato daityāḥ sābhilāṣā manobhavam \|*

163\. with every womanly virtue. Seeing her before them, the Daityas, seized with longing, could not bear the intense love

## \|\| 16.164 \|\|

*tyaktvā devān striyaṃ tāṃ tu hartukāmā hataujasaḥ \|*

164\. with fortitude; and pined in mind to carry her off. Desisting from the gods, but desirous of seizing the lady, they were shattered in vigour, being bewitched by that sin. Then compact

165\. together they spoke -'If only this jewel of womankind in the three worlds might be our prize, successful then should

## \|\| 16.166 \|\|

*tasmāt sarve samutkṣipya śivikāyāṃ surārdanāḥ \|*

*garga uvāca*  
*sānurāgāstataste tu proktāścettthaṃ parasparam \|*

167\. "Thereupon possessed with longing and thus mutually exhorted, afflicted by love, the united Daityas and Dánavas

## \|\| 16.168 \|\|

*śivikāyāṃ samāropya sahitā daityadānavāḥ \|*

## \|\| 16.169 \|\|

*dattātreyastato devān vihasyedamathābravīt \|*

169\. Thereon Dattátreya smiling Spoke thus to the gods ' Bravo! ye prosper! Here is Lakshmí borne on the heads of the Daityas. She has passed beyond the seven stations, she will reach another, a new one.'

The gods spoke:

*devā ūcuḥ*

170\. 'Say, O lord of the world, in what stations has she her abode; and what result of a man's does she bestow or destroy?'

Dattátreya spoke:

## \|\| 16.171 \|\|

*dattātreya uvāca*  
*nṛṇāṃ pade sthitā lakṣmīrnilayaṃ samprayacchati \|*

171\. 'When stationed on the foot of men, Lakshmí bestows a habitation; and when stationed on the thigh, clothing and

## \|\| 16.172 \|\|

*kalātrañca guhyasaṃsthā kroḍasthāpatyadāyinī \|*  
*manorathān pūrayati puruṣāṇāṃ hṛdi sthitā \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. manifold wealth; and when taking her position in the pudenda, a wife; when resting in the bosom, she grants offspring; when stationed in the heart, she fulfils the thoughts

## \|\| 16.173 \|\|

*lakṣmīrlakṣmīvatāṃ śreṣṭhā kaṇṭhasthā kaṇṭhabhūṣaṇam \|*

173\. of men. Lakshmí, is the best fortune of fortunate men. When resting on the neck, she adorns the neck with loved relatives and wives, and close contact with those who are absent.

## \|\| 16.174-175 \|\|

*sṛṣṭānuvākyalāvaṇyamājñāmavitathāṃ tathā \|*

*śirogatā santyajati tato 'nyaṃ yāti cāśrayam \|*

174-175. When abiding in the countenance, the sea-born goddess bestows beauty fashioned according to her word, real command also, and poetic fire. When mounted on the head, she forsakes the man and thence resorts to another abode. And here, mounted on their head, she will now desert these Daityas.

## \|\| 16.176-177 \|\|

*pragṛhyāstrāṇi badhyantāṃ tasmādete surārayaḥ \|*  
*na bhetavyaṃ bhṛśañcaite mayā nistejasaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 176 \|\|*

*paradārāvamarṣācca dagdhapuṇyā hataujasaḥ \|*  
*tasmādete'bhihanyantāṃ bhavaddhiraviśaṃkitai \|\| 177 \|\|*

176-177. Therefore seize your arms and slay these foes of the gods; nor fear them greatly; I have rendered them impotent; and through touching another's wife their merit is consumed, their might is broken.

Garga spoke:

## \|\| 16.178-182 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*tataste vividhairastrairvadhyamānāḥ surārayaḥ \|*

*lakṣmīścītpatya samprāptā dattātreyaṃ mahāmunim \|*

*praṇipatya tato devā dattātreyaṃ manīṣiṇam \|*  
*jaya kṛṣṇa jagannātha daityāntaka haraprabho \|\| 180 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇācyutānanta vāsudevākṣayājara\|*  
*tvatmasādātsukhaṃ lmī rājyaṃ sampajjanārdana \|\| 181 \|\|*

*śardathanvaṃśkrapāṇe bhaktānāṃ nityavatsala \|*  
*iti stutvā nākapṛṣṭhaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ gatāḥ surāḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

178-182. "Thereupon those enemies of the gods, being slain by divers weapons and their heads being assailed by Lakshmí, perished - thus have we heard. And Lakshmí, flying up, reached the great Muni Dattátreya, being hymned by all the gods who were filled with joy at the slaughter of the Daityas. Thereupon the gods, prostrating themselves before the wise Dattátreya, gained as before the uppermost heaven, being freed from affliction.

## \|\| 16.183 \|\|

*tathā tvamapi rojendra ! yadīcchasi yathepsitam \|*

183\. Likewise do thou also, O king! if thou wishest to obtain matchless sovereignty according to thy desire, straightway propitiate him."

## Chapter 17

## \|\| 17.1-3 \|\|

*putra uvāca*  
*ityṛṣervacanaṃ śrutvā kārtavīryo nareśvaraḥ \|*  
*dattātreyāśramaṃ gattvā taṃ bhaktyā samapūjayat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pādasaṃvāhanādyena madhvādyāharaṇena ca \|*  
*strakcandanādigandhāmbu-phalādyanayanena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tathānnasādhanaistasya ucchiṣṭāpohanena ca \|*  
*parituṣṭo munirbhūtaṃ tamuvāca tathaiva saḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

King Arjuna, taking Garga's advice, propitiates Dattátreya, who grants him the boon that he should reign righteously, prosperously and gloriously -Arjuna is then installed in his kingdom, and his reign is described -The blessedness of worshipping Vishnu, who is Dattátreya, expounded -The story of Alarka is then begun.

The son spoke:

1-3. Having heard the Rishi speak thus, king Arjuna, Kritavírya's son, proceeded to Dattátreya's hermitage and worshipped him with faith; by kneading his feet and other services, and by offering honey and other delicacies, and by bringing garlands, sandal, and other perfumes, water, fruit, also with preparations of rice, and by removing the Rishi's fragments of food. Pleased therewith the Muni addressed the

## \|\| 17.4 \|\|

*yathaivoktāḥ purā devā madyabhogādikutsanam \|*  
*strī ceyaṃ mama pārśvasthetyetadbhogācca kutsitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. king in the very same way, as he had formerly addressed the gods. "Ever indeed am I an object of reproach for my enjoyment of spirituous liquor and other bodily pleasures, and an object of reproach for this enjoyment in that I have my

## \|\| 17.5 \|\|

*sadaivāhaṃ na māmevamuparoddhuṃ tvamarhasi \|*  
*aśaktamupakārāya śaktamārādhayasva bhoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. wife here by my side. Deign thou not thus to obstruct me who am unable to benefit thee; O conciliate one who is able."

## \|\| 17.6 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*tenaivamukto muninā smṛtvā gargavacaśca tat \|*  
*pratyuvāca praṇamyainaṃ sārtavīryārjunastadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thus the Muni addressed him; and Arjuna Kártavírya, recalling that speech of Garga's, replied then, bowing before him.

Arjuna spoke:

## \|\| 17.7 \|\|

*arjuna uvāca*  
*kiṃ māṃ mohayase deva ! svāṃ māyāṃ samupāśritaḥ \|*  
*anaghastvaṃ tathaiveyaṃ devī sarvabhavāraṇiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. "Why dost thou beguile me, my lord, resorting to thy illusory devices. Sinless thou art, and this bráhman lady is the path of all existence."

## \|\| 17.8 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ prītimān devastatastaṃ pratyuvāca ha \|*  
*kārtavīryaṃ mahābhāgaṃ vaśīkṛtamahītalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thus invoked, the benign bráhman answered him the illustrious Kártavírya, the subduer of the earth.

## \|\| 17.9 \|\|

*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva guhyaṃ me yat tvayā samudīritam \|*  
*tena tuṣṭiḥ parā jātā tvayyadya mama pārthiva \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. "Choose thou a boon; since thou hast declared my secret, I have felt thereby intense gratification in thee to-day, O

## \|\| 17.10 \|\|

*ye ca māṃ pūjayiṣyanti gandhamālyādibhirnarāḥ \|*  
*māṃsamadyopahāraiśca miṣṭānnaiścājyasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. king. And the men who shall worship me with perfumes, garlands and such like, with offerings also of meat and strong drink, and with sweetmeats accompanied with clarified butter,

## \|\| 17.11 \|\|

*lakṣmīsametaṃ gītaiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ tathārccanaiḥ \|*  
*vādyairmanoramairvoṇā-veṇu-śaṅkādibhistathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. -and who shall worship me and Lakshmí with songs also and the worship of brahmans, and with lute, flute, conchs and other

## \|\| 17.12 \|\|

*teṣāmahaṃ parāṃ tuṣṭiṃ putradāradhanādikam \|*  
*pradāsyāmyavaghātañca haniṣyāmyavamanyatām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. gladsome musical instruments; -to them I will give supreme gratification, children, wives, wealth and other blessings, and I

## \|\| 17.13 \|\|

*prasādasumukhaste 'haṃ guhyanāmaprakīrtanāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. will ward off the violent blows of scorners. Do thou then choose the choice boon that thy mind desires: my face is very gracious to thee through thy declaration of my secret name."

Kártavírya spoke:

*kārtavīrya uvāca*  
*yadi deva prasannastvaṃ tat prayacchardhimuttamām \|*

14\. "If my lord thou art gracious, then grant me supreme prosperity, whereby I may protect my people and may not incur

## \|\| 17.15 \|\|

*parānusaraṇe jñānamapratidvandvatāṃ raṇe \|*

## \|\| 17.16 \|\|

*asaṅgā gatayaḥ santu śailākāśāmbu-bhūmiṣu \|*

16\. May my paths be unimpeded on hill, in air, in water, and on land, and in all the hells!And may my death come from a

## \|\| 17.17 \|\|

*tathonmārgapravṛttasya cāstu sanmārgadeśakaḥ \|*

17\. superior man! And let me have moreover a guide to the right path when I stray from the path: and may my guests be worthy of praise in the imperishable bestowal of wealth!

## \|\| 17.18 \|\|

*anaṣṭadravyatā rāṣṭre mamānusmaraṇena ca \|*  
*tvayi bhaktirmamaivāstu nityamavyabhicāriṇī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. And let there be freedom from impoverishment in my country with repeated recollection of me! May my faith in thee be ever in truth unwavering!"

Dattátreya spoke:

## \|\| 17.19 \|\|

*dattātreya uvāca*  
*yatra te kīrtitāḥ sarve tān varān samavāpsyasi \|*  
*matprasādācca bhavitā cakravarto tvamīśvaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. "Thou shalt receive all those boons in the matters that thou hast specified; and through my favour thou shalt become a universal monarch."

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 17.20 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*praṇipatya tatastasmai dattātreyāya so 'rjunaḥ \|*

*āghoṣayāmāsa tadā sthito rājye sa haihayaḥ \|*

*adyaprabhṛti yaḥ śastraṃ māmṛte 'nyo grahīṣyati \|*  
*hantavyaḥ sa mayā dasyuḥ parihaṃsārato 'pi vā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. exceeding power, made proclamation; -'Henceforth whoever besides me shall lay hold of a weapon, I shall put him to death

## \|\| 17.23 \|\|

*ityājñaptena tadrāṣṭre kaścidāyudhadhṛṅnaraḥ \|*  
*tamṛte puruṣavyāghraṃ babhūvoruparākramaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. as a robber or as one bent on injuring others.' After this order had been issued, there was no man that bore arms in

## \|\| 17.24 \|\|

*sa eva grāmapālo 'bhūt paśupālaḥ sa eva ca \|*  
*kṣetrapālaḥ sa evāsīd dvijātīnāñca rakṣitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. that country, except that valiant tiger-warrior. He it was who was the guardian of the villages, and he the guardian of the cattle. He it was who was the guardian of the

## \|\| 17.25 \|\|

*tapasvināṃ pālayitā sārthapālastu so 'bhavat \|*  
*dsyu-vyālāgri-śastrādi-bhayeṣvabdhau nimajjatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. fields and the protector of the dvijas. He also was the guardian of ascetics, and the guardian of caravans; the guardian of those who were sinking amid the fears of robbers,

## \|\| 17.26 \|\|

*anyāsu caiva magrānāmāpatsu paravīrahā \|*  
*sa eva saṃsmṛtaḥ sadyaḥ samuddhartābhavannṛṇām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. rogues, fire, arms and so forth, as in the sea, and of those who were involved in other calamities; he was the destroyer of hostile warriors. He it was who was ever remembered as

## \|\| 17.27 \|\|

*anaṣṭadravyatā cāsīt tasmin śāsati pārthive \|*  
*teneṣṭaṃ bahubhiryajñaiḥ samāptavaradakṣiṇaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. the upholder of mankind. And there was exemption from impoverishment, while he ruled as king. He offered many

## \|\| 17.28 \|\|

*tenaiva ca tapastaptaṃ saṃgrāmeṣvabhiceṣṭitam \|*  
*tasyārdhimatimānañca dṛṣṭvā prāhāṅgirā muniḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. sacrifices, complete with gifts and fees. He also practised austerities. He performed exploits in battles. Having seen his prosperity and exceeding honour, the Muni Angiras spoke.

## \|\| 17.29 \|\|

*na nūnaṃ kārtavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti pārthivāḥ \|*  
*yajñairdānaistapobhirvā saṃgrāme cāticeṣcitaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. "Assuredly kings will not follow in Kártavírya's steps, either with sacrifices, alms-giving, or austerities, or with high exploits in battle."

## \|\| 17.30 \|\|

*dattātreyāddin yasmin sa prāpardhi nareśvaraḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃstasmin dine yāgaṃ dattātreyasya so 'karot \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On the very day when the king received prosperity from

## \|\| 17.31 \|\|

*tatraiva ca prajāḥ sarvāstasminnahani bhūpateḥ \|*  
*tasyardhi paramāṃ dṛṣṭvā yāgaṃ cakruḥ samādhinā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Dattátreya, he performed sacrifice to Dattátreya. And there all his subjects having seen the king's supreme prosperity that day offered up sacrifices with devout attention.

## \|\| 17.32 \|\|

*ityetat tasya māhātmyaṃ dattātreyasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*viṣṇoścarācaraguroranantasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Such is this magnanimity of the wise Dattátreya, who is Vishnu, the guru of all things movable and immovable,

## \|\| 17.33 \|\|

*prādurbhāvāḥ purāṇeṣu kathyante śārḍgadhanvinaḥ \|*  
*anantasyāprameyasya śaṅkha-cakra-gadābhṛtaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. endless, high-souled. In the Puránas are narrated the manifestations of the bearer of the bow S'árnga, who is endless,

## \|\| 17.34 \|\|

*etasya paramaṃ rūpaṃ yaścintayati mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa sukhī sa ca saṃsārāt samuttīrṇo 'cirādbhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. inscrutable, the bearer of the conch discus and club. Whatever man ponders on his highest form, happy is he, and he

## \|\| 17.35 \|\|

*sadaiva vaiṣṇavānāñca bhaktyāhaṃ sulabho 'smi bhoḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ yasya vai vācastaṃ kathaṃ nāśrayejjanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. may soon pass over mundane existence. 'Ho! I am ever in truth easy of reach by faith even to Vaishnavas,' -how is it that a man should not have recourse to him, whose are these

## \|\| 17.36 \|\|

*adharmasya vināśāya dharmācārārthameva ca \|*  
*anādinidhano devaḥ karoti sthiti-pālanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. very words? For the destruction of unrighteousness, and for the practice of righteousness, the god, who is without beginning and without end, preserves the stability of nature.

## \|\| 17.37 \|\|

*tathaiva janma cākhyātamalarkaṃ kathayāmi te \|*  
*tathā ca yogaḥ kathito dattātreyeṇa tasya vai \|*  
*pitṛbhaktasya rājarṣeralarkasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Moreover I tell thee of Alarka also, the famous birth. And thus has been related the union between the high-souled RájarshiAlarka, who was faithful to his father, and Dattátreya.

## Chapter 18

## \|\| 18.1 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*prāgbabhūva mahāvīryaḥ śatrujinnāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tutoṣa yasya yajñeṣu somāvāptyā purandaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

King S'atru-jit's son Rita-dhvaja receives into intimate friendship two Nága princes in the guise of bráhmans - They live with him by day, and spend the nights in Rasátala -They extol him to their father, and relate his story as follows -Rita-dhvaja sets out to succour the bráhman Gálava against a Daitya Pátála-ketu, with the aid of a wondrous horse named Kuvalaya.

Jada spoke:

1\. There was formerly a valorous king named Satru-jit, in whose sacrifices Indra was pleased by receiving the soma

## \|\| 18.2 \|\|

*tasyātmajo mahāvīryo babhūvārividāraṇaḥ \|*  
*buddhi-vikrama-lāvaṇyairguruśakrāśvibhiḥ samaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. juice. His son was a valiant destroyer of his foes; the peer of Vrihaspati, Indra and theAsvins in intellect, prowess and

## \|\| 18.3 \|\|

*sa samānavayo-buddhi-sattva-vikrama-ceṣṭitaiḥ \|*  
*nṛpaputro nṛpasutairnityamāste samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. beauty. The king's son was continually surrounded by young princes, who were his equals in age, intellect, virtue, prowess

## \|\| 18.4 \|\|

*kadācicchāstrasambhāra-vivekakṛtaniścayaḥ \|*  
*kadācit kāvyasaṃlāpa-gīta-nāṭakasambhavaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. and behaviour. He was sometimes resolved on investigating the whole Sástra literature; at other times engrossed with

## \|\| 18.5 \|\|

*tathaivākṣavinodaiśca śastrāstravinayeṣu ca \|*  
*yogyāni yuddhanāgāśva-syandanābhyāsatatparaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. poetry, dialogue, singing and the drama. Moreover he enjoyed himself both with gambling pastimes, and in the discipline of all kinds of weapons: he was intent on the study of elephants,

## \|\| 18.6 \|\|

*reme narendraputro 'sau narendratanayaiḥ saha \|*  
*yathaiva hi divā tadvadrātravapi mudā yutaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. horses, and chariots suitable for war. The king's son enjoyed himself in company with the young princes, being

## \|\| 18.7 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu krīḍatāṃ tatra dvija-bhūpa-viśāṃ sutāḥ \|*  
*samānavayasaḥ prītyā rantumāyāntyanekaśaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. absorbed in pleasure by day and night alike. But while they sported there, numbers of young bráhmans, young princes and young vaisyas of the same age came to enjoy themselves affectionately.

## \|\| 18.8 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya nāgalokānmahītalam \|*  
*kumārāvāgatau nāgau putrāvaśvatarasya tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Now after a time two young Nágas, the sons of Asvatara,

## \|\| 18.9 \|\|

*brahmarūpapraticchannau taruṇau priyadarśanau \|*  
*tau tairnṛpasutaiḥ sārdhaṃ tathaivānyairdvijanmabhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. visited the surface of the earth from the Nága-world. Disguised in form as bráhmans, youthful, handsome, those two, in company with the young princes and the other dvijas,

## \|\| 18.10 \|\|

*vinodairvividhaistatra tasthatuḥ prītisaṃyutau \|*  
*sarva ca te nṛpasutāste ca brahmaviśāṃ sutāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. remained there linked in friendship, occupied with various amusements. And all those young princes and the young

## \|\| 18.11 \|\|

*nāgarājātmajau tau ca strānasaṃvāhanādikam \|*

11\. bráhmans and vaisyas, and those two young Nága princes engaged in bathing, kneading the limbs &c., adorned themselves with garments and perfumes, and occupied themselves

12\. with the business of kings. As day after day went by, the two young Nágas enjoyed themselves, being bound by affection

16\. "With whom do ye both, my sons, find supreme affection in the mortal-world?" thus inquired their father of both

17\. those young Nágas. "Whilst I have seen you both many day s here in Pátála, I ever behold you both with kindly countenances by day and night."

Jada spoke:

19\. "It is the son of Satru-jit, dear father, famed by name as Rita-dhvaja, shapely, upright in conduct, a hero, proud, kind

*anāpṛṣṭakatho vāggmī vidvān maitro guṇākaraḥ \|*

20\. of speech, no sneaking tale-bearer, eloquent, learned, friendly, a mine of excellencies, an honourer of the honour

The father spoke:

*pitovāca*

23\. He is the happy son of a holy father, whose excellencies such accomplished persons as ye are thus celebrate even in his

*santi śāstravido 'śīlāḥ santi mūrkhāḥ suśīlinaḥ \|*

24\. absence. There are evil-dispositioned men learned in the Sástras; there are good-dispositioned men who are fools: but I esteem him, my sons, the happier who equally possesses

25\. knowledge of Sástras and a good disposition. A father has indeed a son in that son, whose friends always declare his friendly qualities, and whose enemies his valour, among the

*kiñcinniṣpāditaṃ vatsau paritoṣāya cetasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. good. Perchance ye have preferred a request to him as a benefactor: he has done something to satisfy your mind, my

27\. children. Happy is he! The life of each high-born one has been well lived, when petitioners to him turn not away, and the

\- men wish him prosperity." The sons spoke:

32\. of all their desires. The jewels that are in his house, whence can we have them in Pátála?And whence his animals for

*tantu śatrujitaṃ tāta pūrvaṃ kaścididvajottamaḥ \|*

46\. obstacles so that my mind wavers. Thou art able instantly to burn him with the fire of thy anger, but not we. Do I desire that austerities arduously acquired should be squandered,

52\. name Kuvalaya. And the base sinful Dánava, who day and night torments thee, him shall slay, O bráhman, the king named

## \|\| 18.56 \|\|

*sa tasya vacanādrājā taṃ vai putramṛtadhvajam \|*  
*tamaśvaratnamāropya kṛtakautukamaṅgalam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*apreṣayata dharmātmā gālavena samaṃ tadā \|*

## Chapter 19

## \|\| 19.1 \|\|

*pitovāca*  
*gālavena samaṃ gatvā nṛpaputreṇa tena yat \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tat kathyatāṃ putrau vicitrā yuvayoḥ kathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Rita-dhvaja, called also Kuvalayásva, wounds and pursues the Daitya Pátála-ketu. -In the pursuit he falls through a chasm into Pátála and reaches the city Purandara-pura -There he meets Madálasá, (daughter of the Gandharva king Visvávasu,) whom Pátála-ketu had carried off -He marries her with the help of her companion Kundalá, who then admonishes them on the blessings of marriage -He kills the Daityas who oppose him, and brings her home to his father, who praises and blesses him.

The father spoke:

1\. "Relate my sons what the king's son did after he departed in company with Gálava; your story is a surprising one."

The sons spoke:

Pátála-ketu's brother Tála-ketu, in the guise of a Muni dwelling on the bank of the Yamuná, induces Kuvalayásva to guard his hermitage, on the pretext that he had certain ceremonies to perform in the water - Disappearing within the water he goes to the palace and reports that Kuvalayásva had died in battle with the Daityas -Madálasá dies through grief, and the king and queen utter their lamentations, and perform the prince's obsequies -Tála-ketu then returns to the hermitage and releases the prince.

## Chapter 21

## \|\| 21.1 \|\|

*sa rājaputraḥ saṃprāpya vegādātmapuraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pitrorvavandiṣuḥ pādau didṛkṣuśca madālasām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Kuvalayásva, returning home, learnt what had happened -He mourns his loss, and shunning women lives a cheerful life -The Nága king Asvatara, hearing this story, engages in austerities and extols Sarasvatí - Sarasvatí, propitiated by him, restores him his companion Kambala, and gives them both perfect skill in poetry and music -Both propitiate S'iva, who at their request gives Asvatara Madálasá as his daughter, restored to life as before -At Asvatara's suggestion, his sons invite Kuvalayásva to their palace in Pátála and introduce him to their father -Asvatara asks Kuvalayásva to relate his story.

The sons spoke:

1\. The king's son reaching then his own city in haste, desirous to salute his parents' feet respectfully, and eager to see Madálasá,

## \|\| 21.2 \|\|

## Chapter 22

## \|\| 22.1 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*kṛtāhāraṃ mahātmanāmadhipaṃ pavanāśinām \|*  
*upāsāñcakrire putrau bhūpālatanayastathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Nága king Asvatara asks Kuvalayásva what gift he can confer on him -Kuvalayásva replies he needs nothing, and is sufficiently gratified by the king's favour -The king urges him and at his sons' suggestion the prince asks to see Madálasá even in illusion -The king brings her in as an illusion, and afterwards restores her to Kuvalayásva.

Jada spoke:

1\. His two sons and the king's son respectfully attended the

## \|\| 22.2 \|\|

*kathābhiranurūpābhiḥ sa mahātmā bhujaṅgamaḥ \|*  
*prītiṃ sañjanayāmāsa putrasakhyuruvāca ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. high souled king of the Nágas, after he had banquetted. The high-souled Nága manifested kindly regard towards his sons'

## \|\| 22.3 \|\|

*tava bhadra ! sukhaṃ brūhi gehamabhyāgatasya yat \|*  
*kartavyamutsṛjāśaṅkāṃ pitarīva suto mayi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. friend with suitable conversation, and said, "Declare, Sir, what pleasure I must do thee who hast entered my house: cast away hesitation towards me as a son would towards his

## \|\| 22.4 \|\|

*rajataṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā vastraṃ vāhanamāsanam \|*  
*yadvābhimatamatyarthaṃ durlabhaṃ tadvṛṇuṣva mām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. father. Whether silver or gold, raiment, carriages, or seats, or whatever thou dost highly appreciate that is hard to be got ask that of me."

Kuvalayásva spoke:

## \|\| 22.5 \|\|

*kuvalayāśva uvāca*  
*tava prasādādbhagavan ! suvarṇādi gṛhe mama \|*  
*piturasti mamādyāpina kiñcit kāryamīdṛśam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. "Through thy favour, illustrious Sir! gold and other wealth are in my father's house; I have no need of any such thing

## \|\| 22.6 \|\|

*tāte varṣasahasrāṇi śāsatīmāṃ vasundharām \|*  
*tathaiva tvayi pātālaṃ na me yāñconmukaṃ manaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. at all now. While my father roles this earth for thousands of years and thou also rulest Pátála, my mind is not expectant

## \|\| 22.7 \|\|

*te svargyāśca supuṇyāśca yeṣāṃ pitari jīvati \|*  
*tṛṇakoṭisamaṃ vittaṃ tāruṇyādvittakoṭiṣu \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. in solicitation. They are both possessed of Svarga and are very rich in merit, who from their youth possess, in their father's lifetime, a mere particle of wealth amidst his

## \|\| 22.8 \|\|

*mitrāṇi tulyaśiṣṭāni tadvaddehamanāmayam \|*  
*janitā dhriyate vittaṃ yauvanaṃ kinnu nāsti me \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. krores of wealth, friends equally-educated, and a body free from sickness. My father holds the wealth; have I

## \|\| 22.9 \|\|

*asatyarthe nṛṇāṃ yāñcāpravaṇaṃ jāyate manaḥ \|*  
*satyaśeṣe kathaṃ yāñcāṃ mama jihvā kariṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. not youth? When wealth is wanting, men's minds become prone to petitions. When I have it in full measure, how shall

## \|\| 22.10 \|\|

*yairna cintyaṃ dhanaṃ kiñcinmama gehe 'sti nāsti vā \|*  
*pitṛbāhutarucchāyāṃ saṃśritāḥ sukhino hi te \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. my tongue make petition? Those who need not think whether they have any riches at home or not, happy are they, sheltered in the shadow of the tree of their father's arm.

## \|\| 22.11 \|\|

*ye tu bālyāt prabhṛtyeva vinā pitrā kuṭumbinaḥ \|*  
*te sukhāsvādavibhraṃśānmanye dhātraiva vañcitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. But those, who even from childhood losing their father have had the care of a family, they have in my opinion, through the ruin of their taste for happiness, been tricked by

## \|\| 22.12 \|\|

*tadvayaṃ tvatprasādena dhanaratnādisañcayān \|*  
*pitṛmuktān prayacchāmaḥ kāmato nityamarthinām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. the Creator. We therefore through thy favour always give willingly to supplicants the hoards of money, gems and other

## \|\| 22.13 \|\|

*tat sarvamiha saṃprāptaṃ yadaṅghriyugalaṃ tava \|*  
*maccūḍāmaṇinā spṛṣṭaṃ yaccāṅgasparśamāptavān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. wealth left by our fathers. I have everything then here, since I have touched thy feet with my crest-jewel, since I have couched thy body."

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 22.14 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*ityevaṃ prasṛtaṃ vākyamuktaḥ pannagasattamaḥ \|*  
*prāha rājasutaṃ prītyā putrayorupakāriṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Being answered thus in a modest speech, the noble Nága replied kindly to the young prince, the benefactor of his sons.

The Nága spoke:

## \|\| 22.15 \|\|

*nāga uvāca*  
*yadi ratnasuvarṇādi matto 'vāptuṃ na te manaḥ \|*  
*yadanyanmanasaḥ prītyai tadbrūhi tvaṃ dadāmyaham \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. "If it be not thy mind to receive of me gems, gold or other gift; whatever else may please thy mind, mention thou it. I will give it thee."

Kuvalayásva spoke:

## \|\| 22.16 \|\|

*kuvalayāśva uvāca*  
*bhagavaṃstvatprasādena prārthitasya gṛhe mama \|*  
*sarvamasti viśeṣeṇa samprāptaṃ tava darśanāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. "My lord, through thy favour, I whom thou dost ask have everything at home: it has been gained especially through

## \|\| 22.17 \|\|

*kṛtakṛtyo 'smi caitena saphalaṃ jīvitañca me \|*  
*yadaṅgasaṃśleṣamitastava devasya mānuṣaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. sight of thee. And herein I am successful, and my life has been rewarded, that I a mortal have embraced thy body who

## \|\| 22.18 \|\|

*mamottamāṅge tvatpādarajasā yadihāspadam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tenaiva na prāptaṃ kiṃ mayā pannageśvara \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. art divine; that the dust of thy feet has found a seat on my head.What indeed have I not gained thereby, O Nága

## \|\| 22.19 \|\|

*yadi tvavaśyaṃ dātavyo varo mama yathepsitaḥ \|*  
*tatpuṇyakarmasaṃskāro hṛdayānmā vyapaitu me \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. king? But if thou needs must give me the boon that I desire, then let not the faculty of working righteousness

## \|\| 22.20 \|\|

*suvarṇamaṇiratnādi vāhanaṃ gṛhamāsanam \|*  
*striyo 'nnapānaṃ putrāśca cārumālyānulepan \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. depart from my heart. Gold, gems, jewels and such like, carriages, houses, seats, women, food and drink, and children,

## \|\| 22.21 \|\|

*ete ca vividhāḥ kāmā gītavādyādikañca yat \|*  
*sarvametanmama mataṃ phalaṃ puṇyavanaspateḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. and tasteful garlands and ointments, -both these various objects of desire, and also vocal and instrumental music and whatever other music there be - all this I hold to be the fruit

## \|\| 22.22 \|\|

*tasmānnareṇa tanmulaḥ kāryo yatnaḥ kṛtātmanā \|*  
*kartavyaḥ puṇyasaktānāṃ na kiñcidbhuvi durlabham \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. of the tree of good works. Therefore a man must start from the root thereof; he must exert himself, while ruling his spirit; nothing in the world is hard of attainment to those who adhere to good works."

Asvatara spoke:

## \|\| 22.23 \|\|

*aśvatara uvāca*  
*evaṃ bhaviṣyati prājña ! tava dharmāśritā matiḥ \|*  
*satyañcaitat phalaṃ sarvaṃ dharmasyoktaṃ yathā tvayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. "So shall thy mind be, O wise man, relying on righteousness; and truly all this is the fruit of righteousness as thou

## \|\| 22.24 \|\|

*tathāpyavaśyaṃ madgehamāgatena tvayādhunā \|*  
*grāhyaṃ yanmānuṣe loke duṣprāptaṃ bhavato matam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. hast said. Nevertheless thou must certainly take, now that thou hast entered my house, what thou thinkest hard to be gained in the human world."

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 22.25 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*tasyaitadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa tadā nṛpanandanaḥ \|*  
*mukāvalokanañcakre pannageśvaraputrayoḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Having heard this his speech, the young prince then

## \|\| 22.26 \|\|

*tatastau praṇipatyobhau rājaputrasya yanmatam \|*  
*tat pituḥ sakalaṃ vīrau kathayāmāsatuḥ sphuṭam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. looked at the faces of the Nága king's sons. Thereupon both those heroes prostrating themselves told their father clearly all the young prince's thoughts.

The sons spoke:

## \|\| 22.27 \|\|

*tato 'sya patnī dayitā śrutvemaṃ vinipātitam \|*  
*atyajaddayitān prāṇān vipralabdhā durātmanā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. "When this prince's beloved wife heard that he was slain, she forsook her dear life, being deceived by a certain cruel,

## \|\| 22.28 \|\|

*kenāpi kṛtavaireṇa dānavena kubuddhinā \|*  
*gandharvarājasya sutā nāmnā khyātā madālasā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. bad-minded Dánava, who shewed his enmity. She was the

## \|\| 22.29 \|\|

*kutajño 'yaṃ tatastāta ! pratijñāṃ kṛtavānimām \|*  
*nānyā bhāryā bhavitrīti varjayitvā madālasām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. daughter of the Gandharva king; she was named Madálasá. Then he, mindful of the past, made this vow, dear father,

## \|\| 22.30 \|\|

*draṣṭuṃ tāṃ cārusarvāṅgīmayaṃ vīra ! ṛtadhvajaḥ \|*  
*tāta ! vāñchati yadyetat kriyate tat kṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. 'No other shall be my wife save Madálasá.' This hero Ritadhvaja longs, dear father, to behold her, lovely-limbed: if this may be done, let it be done."

Asvatara spoke:

## \|\| 22.31 \|\|

*aśvatara uvāca*  
*bhūtairviyogino yogastādṛśaireva tādṛśaḥ \|*  
*kathametadvinā svapnaṃ māyāṃ vā śambaroditām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. "Such magical power as that belongs to one who is exempt from such gross elements. How can this be except as a dream or as an illusion proceeding from S'ambara?"

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 22.32 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*praṇipatya bhujaṅgeśaṃ putraḥ śatrujitastataḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ premalajjāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then S'atru-jit's son prostrated himself before the highsouled Nága king and replied, being touched with affection

## \|\| 22.33 \|\|

*māyāmayīmapyadhunā mama tāta ! madālasām \|*  
*yadi darśayate manye paraṃ kṛtamanugraham \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. and modesty. "If thou show me now, dear father, Madálasá even in illusion, I hold that thou hast done me the greatest favour."

Asvatara spoke:

## \|\| 22.34 \|\|

*aśvatara uvāca*  
*tasmāt paśyeha vatsa ! tvaṃ māyāñced draṣṭumicchasi \|*  
*anugrāhyo bhavān gehaṃ bālo 'pyabhyāgato guruḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. "Look thou here then, my son, if thou wouldest see the illusion. I must show thee favour; a visitor at one's house, though a child, is master.”

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 22.35 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*ānayāmāsa nāgendro gṛhaguptāṃ madālasām \|*  
*darśayāmāsa ca tadā rājaputrāya tāṃ śubhām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Nága king led in Madálasá who was concealed in the house, and next he uttered some gibberish distinctly in order to

## \|\| 22.36 \|\|

*teṣāṃ saṃmohanārthāya jjalpa ca tataḥ sphuṭam \|*  
*seyaṃ na veti te bhāryā rājaputra ! madālasā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. bewilder them. And then he showed the young prince the beauteous lady, saying, "Is she or is she not, O prince, thy wife Mádalasá?"

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 22.37 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*sa dṛṣṭvā tāṃ tadā tanvīṃ tatkṣaṇāt vigatatrapaḥ \|*  
*priyeti tāmabhimukhaṃ yayau vācamudīrayan \|*  
*nivārayāmāsa ca taṃ nāgaḥ so 'śvatarastvaran \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then, seeing the slender one, he lost his reticence that very moment; he moved towards her, uttering the word "Beloved!" And the NágaAsvatara hasting held him off.

Asvatara spoke:

## \|\| 22.38-42 \|\|

*aśvatara uvāca*  
*māyeyaṃ putra ! mā sprākṣīḥ prāgeva kathitaṃ tava \|\| 38 \|\|*

*antardhānamupaityāśu māyā saṃsparśanādibhiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ papāta medinyāṃ sa tu mūrcchāpariplutaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*hā priyeti vadan so 'tha cintayāmāsa bhāminīm \|*  
*moho mamāyaṃ no veti nālaṃ pratyayavānaham \|\| 40 \|\|*

*aho sneho 'sya nṛpatermamoparyacalaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*yenāyaṃ pātano 'rīṇāṃ vinā śastreṇa pātitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*māmeti darśitā tena mithyā māyeti yatsphuṭam \|*  
*vāyvambutejasāṃ bhumerākāśasya ca ceṣṭayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. "It is illusion, my son! touch her not! I told thee so at first. The illusion quickly vanishes when touched or otherwise meddled with." Thereupon he fell to the ground, overwhelmed by a faint; and exclaiming "Ah Beloved!" he thought of his noble wife. "Alas for the love of this king towards my steadfast mind, whereby I have been thus overthrown without the weapons of foes. She was shown as an illusion, though it was clearly no illusion at all by reason of the action of air, water and fire, earth and ether."

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 22.43 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*tataḥ kuvalayāśvaṃ taṃ samāśvāsya bhujaṅgamaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tat sarvaṃ mṛtasañjīvanādikam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the Nága reviving Kuvalayásva, related to him the whole story of her recovery from death and all else that had happened.

## \|\| 22.44 \|\|

*tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratilabhya kāntāṃ*  
*praṇamya nāgaṃ nijamāmjagama \|*  
*saṃstūyamānaḥ svapure tamaśca- māruhya sañcintitamabhyupetam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereat rejoicing he took again his loved one, and after doing obeisance to the Nága departed in great splendour, mounted on the horse, to his own city, having attained the object of his thoughts.

## \|\| 22.45-46 \|\|

*śṛṇuyāddhaktiparvaṃ yo bhairantyeṇa mānavaḥ \|*  
*vedadhoṣaphalaṃ tena prāpataṃ vai bhuvi durlabham \|\| 45 \|\|*

*samaprāpoti sukhaṃ nityaṃ sarvakāmasamanvitaḥ\|*  
*loke ca durlabhaṃ tasya nāsti kiñcitna vidyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. A man who listens continuously with faith obtains the fruit which is declared in Vedas and scarce in this world. He gains eternal happiness with all desires and there is no unachievable thing for him in the world.

## Chapter 23

## \|\| 23.1 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*āgamya svapuraṃ so 'tha pitroḥ sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tanvaṅgī yathā prāptā punarmṛtā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Kuvalayásva, returning home, lives in perfect happiness with Madálasá -He succeeds his father Satru-jit -A son is born to them, Vi-krán-ta -Madálasá prattles to the infant.

Jada spoke:

1\. Reaching then his city he narrated the whole story fully to his parents, how he had regained his slender-limbed one who

## \|\| 23.2 \|\|

*nanāma sā ca caraṇau śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ śubhā \|*  
*svajanañca yathāpūrvaṃ vandanāśleṣaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. had died. And the beautiful, slender-limbed lady bowed at the feet of her father and mother-in-law, and did honour as

## \|\| 23.3 \|\|

*pūjayāmāsa tanvaṅgī yathānyāyaṃ yathāvayaḥ \|*  
*tato mahotsavo jajñe paurāṇāṃ tatra vai pure \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. before to her kindred with obeisance, embraces and such

## \|\| 23.4 \|\|

*ṛtadhvajaśca suciraṃ tayā reme sumadhyayā \|*  
*nirjhareṣu ca śailānāṃ nimnagāpulineṣu ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. greetings, according to propriety, and their ages. Then the citizens held a great festival there in the city. And Rita-dhvaja long enjoyed himself with his beautiful

## \|\| 23.5 \|\|

*kānaneṣu ca ramyeṣu tathaivopavaneṣu ca \|*  
*puṇyakṣayaṃ vāñchamānā sāpi kāmopabogataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. waisted wife, both among mountain torrents, and on river sand-banks, and amid pleasant woods, and in groves. She also, longing to consume her merit by the delights of love,

## \|\| 23.6 \|\|

*saha tenātikāntena reme ramyāsu bhūmiṣu \|*  
*tataḥ kālena mahatā śatrujit sa narādhipaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. enjoyed herself with him, her greatly-beloved, in pleasant places.

## \|\| 23.7 \|\|

*samyak praśāsya vasudhāṃ kāladharmamupeyivān \|*  
*tataḥ paurā mahātmānaṃ putraṃ tasya ṛtadhvajam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A long time afterwards the king Satru-jit, having ruled the earth worthily, underwent the law of Death.Then the citizens

## \|\| 23.8 \|\|

*abhyaṣiñcanta rājānamudārācāraceṣṭitam \|*  
*samyak pālayatastasya prajāḥ putrānivaurasān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. inaugurated as king his high-souled son Rita-dhvaja, noble in conduct and action. While he duly protected his subjects as if they were his

## \|\| 23.9 \|\|

*madālasāyāḥ sañjajñe putraḥ prathamajastataḥ \|*  
*tasya cakre pitā nāma vikrānta iti dhīmataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. own sons, Madálasá gave birth to her first-born son. The

## \|\| 23.10 \|\|

*tutuṣustena vai bhṛtyā jahāsa ca madālasā \|*  
*sā vai madālasā putraṃ bālamuttānaśāyinam \|*  
*ullāpanacchalenāha rudamānamavisvaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. father gave that clever child the name Vi-kránta. The retainers were pleased thereat and Madálasá laughed. Madálasá spoke to her infant boy in the way of prattle, as he lay on his back crying not unmelodiously.

## \|\| 23.11 \|\|

*śuddho 'si re tāta ! na te 'sti nāma*  
*kṛtaṃ hi te kalpanayādhunaiva \|*  
*pañcātmakaṃ dehamidaṃ tavaitan*  
*naivāsya tvaṃ rodiṣi kasya hetoḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. "Perfect art thou, darling, nor has thy name been given thee now in mere fancy. This very body of thine is composed of the five elements, not indeed for this reason dost thou cry

## \|\| 23.12 \|\|

*na vā bhavān roditi vai svajanmā*  
*śabdo 'yamāsādya mahīśaśūnum \|*  
*vikalpyamānā vividhā guṇāste*  
*'guṇāśca bhautāḥ sakalendriyeṣu \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. wherefore then? Nor indeed does your highness (this title is thy birth-right) cry because thou art a king's son. Doubtful are the various good and bad qualities, that are connected

## \|\| 23.13 \|\|

*bhūtāni bhūtaiḥ paridurbalāni*  
*vṛddhiṃ samāyānti yatheha puṃsaḥ \|*  
*annāmbupānādibhireva kasya*  
*na te 'sti vṛddhirna ca te 'sti hāniḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. with the elements, in all thy organs. Since in a man here the elements, extremely weak, increase by the means of the elements, namely, by means of the food and water and other nutriments given, of what hast thou no gain, of what hast

## \|\| 23.14 \|\|

*tvaṃ kañcuke śīryamāṇe nije 'smiṃs*  
*tasmiṃśca dehe mūḍhatāṃ mā vrajethāḥ \|*  
*śubhāśubhaiḥ karmabhirdehametan*  
*madādimūḍhaiḥ sañcukaste 'pinaddhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. thou no loss? Do not grow infatuated at this thy bodice which is already decaying, and in that thy body; thy body is given thee by good and bad deeds; the bodice is fastened on thee by persons infatuated with pride and other passions.

## \|\| 23.15 \|\|

*tāteti kiñcittanayeti kiñcid*  
*ambeti kiñciddayiteti kiñcit \|*  
*mameti kiñcinna mameti kiñcit*  
*tvaṃ bhūtasaṅghaṃ bahumānayethāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Do thou greatly esteem each aggregate of elements -some one aggregate as a dear father, some other as a child, some other as a mother, some other as a loved wife, some other

## \|\| 23.16 \|\|

*duḥ khāni duḥ khopagamāya bhogān*  
*sukhāya jānāti vimūḍhacetāḥ \|*  
*tānyeva duḥ khāni punaḥ sukhāni*  
*jānātyavidvāna suvimūḍhayetāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. as thy own property, some other as not thy own. A man beguiled in mind thinks that evils tend to assuage evils, that enjoyments tend to happiness. Again the unwise man, greatly beguiled in mind, thinks that these very evils are pleasures.

## \|\| 23.17 \|\|

*hāso 'sthisandarśanamakṣiyugmam*  
*atyujjvalaṃ tarjanamaṅganāyāḥ kucādipīnaṃ piśitaṃ ghanaṃ tat*  
*sthānaṃ rateḥ kiṃ narakaṃ na yoṣit \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Laughter, gazing at the bones, a pair of excessively bright mocking eyes, firm plump flesh in the breasts and elsewhere, in a woman - that is Love's abode; is not woman hell?

## \|\| 23.18 \|\|

*yānaṃ kṣitau yānagatañca dehaṃ*  
*dehe 'pi cānyaḥ puruṣo niviṣṭaḥ \|*  
*mamatvabuddhirna tathā yathā sve*  
*dehe 'timātraṃ bata mūḍhataiṣā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The carriage rests on the earth; and the body is seated in the carriage; and even in the body there is another seated, the soul. There is not the same perception of ownership in one's body, as there is this excessive infatuation with it."

Jada spoke:

## \|\| 23.19 \|\|

*tyaja dharmamadharmaṃ ca ubhe satyānṛte tyaja \|*  
*ubhe satyātṛte tyaktvā yena tyajasi tattyaja \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Now the queen trained up that son; as he grew day by day,

## \|\| 23.20 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*vardhamānaṃ sutaṃ sā tu rājapatnī dine dine \|*  
*tamullāpādinā bodhamanayannirmamātmakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. to unselfish thought by talking and other means. As he regularly gained strength, as he gained his father's intelligence, even so he acquired knowledge of himself through his

## \|\| 23.21 \|\|

*yathāyathaṃ balaṃ lebhe yathā lebhe matiṃ pituḥ \|*  
*tathā tathātmabodhañca so 'vāpanmātṛbhāṣitaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. mother's talk. So the youth, instructed by her from his birth, having understanding and being unselfish, did not turn his mind towards family life.

## \|\| 23.22 \|\|

*itthaṃ tayā sa tanayo janmaprabhṛti bodhitaḥ \|*  
*cakāra na matiṃ prājño gārhasthyaṃ prati nirmamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A second son was born to her. His father named him.

## \|\| 23.23 \|\|

*dvitīyo 'syāḥ suto jajñe tasya nāmākarotpitā \|*

1\. Now being talked to in this way by his mother every day,

## Chapter 25

## \|\| 25.1 \|\|

*jaḍa uvāca*  
*tanmāturvacanaṃ śrutvā so 'larko mātaraṃ punaḥ \|*  
*papraccha varṇadharmāṃśca dharmā ye cāśrameṣu ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

Madálasá enunciates to Alarka the special duties of the four castes -and of the four periods of a bráhman's life -and the duties common to those four castes and periods, which must be strenuously maintained.

Jada spoke:

1\. Having listened to that his mother's exhortation, Alarka also further questioned his mother both about the duties of the four classes, and about the duties appertaining to the four periods of a brahman's life.

Alarka spoke:

## \|\| 25.2 \|\|

*alarka uvāca*  
*kathito 'yaṃ mahābhāge ! rājyatantrāśritastvayā \|*  
*dharmaṃ tamahamicchāmi śrotuṃ varṇāśramātmakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. "Thou hast expounded, gracious lady, this the duty relating to the system of kingly government. I wish to hear that duty which concerns the four classes and the four periods of a brahman's life."

Madálasá spoke:

## \|\| 25.3 \|\|

*madālasovāca*  
*dānamadhyayanaṃ yajño brāhmaṇasya tridhā mataḥ \|*  
*nānyaścaturtho dharmo 'sti dharmastasyāpadaṃ vinā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. "A bráhman's duty is held to be threefold -liberality, study, sacrifice. There is no other fourth duty. His duty is regard

## \|\| 25.4 \|\|

*yājanādhyāpane śuddhe tathā pūtapratigrahaḥ \|*  
*eṣā samyak samākhyatā trividhā cāsya jīvikā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. less of his position. Irreproachable sacrificial and educational occupations, and the acceptance of gifts from the purified -this is fitly proclaimed his threefold means of livelihood

## \|\| 25.5 \|\|

*dānamadhyayanaṃ yajñaḥ kṣatriyasyāpyayaṃ tridhā \|*  
*dharmaḥ proktaḥ kṣite rakṣā śastrājīvañca jīvikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Liberality, study, sacrifice -this is declared to be the threefold duty of a kshatriya also: protection of the earth, and subsistence by weapons are his means of livelihood. Liberality study, sacrifice, -that indeed is the threefold duty of a vaisya also: merchandise, and the tending of cattle, and agriculture

(Note: here the verse 5 is followed by verse 7 also in the original book)

## \|\| 25.7 \|\|

*dānaṃ yajño 'tha śuśrūṣā dvijātīnāṃ tridhā mayā \|*  
*vyākhyātaḥ śūdradharmo 'pi jīvikā kārukarma ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. are his means of livelihood. Liberality, and sacrifice, obedience to dvijas, I have declared to be the threefold duty of the súdra also; and his means of livelihood are a handicraft,

## \|\| 25.8 \|\|

*tadvad dvijātiśuśrūṣā poṣaṇaṃ krayavikrayau \|*  
*varṇadharmāstvime proktāḥ śrūyantāṃ cāśramāśrayāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. obedience likewise to dvijas, nourishing them, buying and selling. These are said to be the duties of the four classes. "Hear also the connexions among the four periods of a bráhman's

## \|\| 25.9 \|\|

*svavarṇadharmāt saṃsiddhiṃ naraḥ prāpnoti na cyutaḥ \|*

15\. guru his fee with words of eulogy. But let him enter on the griha-stha period when desirous of the period of family life; or, by his own wish, on the vána-prastha period and on the

*tato 'samānarṣikulāṃ tulyāṃ bhāryāmarogiṇīm \|*

18\. a griha-stha's status, let him then rightly marry a wife, sprung from the family of a different Rishi, his equal, free from sickness, not deformed, for the sake of a griha-stha's

## Chapter 26

## \|\| 26.1 \|\|

*alarka uvāca*

Madálasá explains to Alarka the position of a griha-stha -and personifies as a cow, the Vedas, pious acts, the words of the good and the words sváhá, svadhá, vashat and hanta -She describes the bali offering, and utsarga oblation -the duties of a griha-stha to guests -the sráddha -and further duties to guests -She pronounces a blessing on the griha-stha state -and quotes a song by Atri on it.

Alarka spoke:

1\. "And what men must do who are engaged in the griha-stha period; and what becomes confined in the absence of action,

## \|\| 26.2 \|\|

2\. and what increases by action; and what is beneficial to men; and what a good man should avoid at home; and how things are done-declare that accurately to me who ask."

Madálasá spoke:

## \|\| 26.3 \|\|

*madālasovāca*  
*vatsa ! gārhasthyamādāya naraḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*
