72\. away, so Brahmá is both Prakriti and the Soul. The Imperceptible is declared to be his sphere of action; hence

## \|\| 42.73 \|\|

*etatsamastaṃ jānīyāt kṣetrakṣetrajñalakṣaṇam \|*  
*ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitastu saḥ \|*  
*abuddhipūrvaḥ prathamaḥ prādurbhūtastaḍidyathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Brahmá is called Kshetra-jna, the Soul. A man should know all these characteristics of the Soul and its sphere of action. Such was this creation from Prakriti; and it is governed by the Soul; the first stage of creation was preceded by nonintelligence, it became manifest like the lightning.

## Chapter 43

## \|\| 43.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*bhagavaṃstvaṇḍasambhūtiryathāvat kathitā mama \|*  
*brahmāṇḍe brahmaṇo janma tathā coktaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya moralizes on Brahmá and Prakriti -and describes Vishnu and S'iva as special forms of Brahmá - He explains how human and divine years are reckoned, the duration of the four ages, the Krita, the Tretá, the Dvápara and the Kálí, and of a Manvantara, and the length of Brahma's day and life.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1.Adorable Sir! thou hast related to me correctly the genesis of the egg, and thou hast told me of the birth of the mighty

## \|\| 43.2 \|\|

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tvatto bhṛgukulodbhava \|*  
*yadāna sṛṣṭirbhūtānāmasti kinnu na cāsti vā \|*  
*kāle vai pralayasyānte sarvasminnupasaṃhṛte \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Soul Brahmá within the egg of Brahmá. I wish to hear this from thee, O scion of Bhrigu's race, when things are not created, and nothing exists, everything having been destroyed byTime at the end of the dissolution of the Universe.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 43.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*yadā tu prakṛtau yāti layaṃ viśvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*tadocyate prākṛto 'yaṃ vidvadbhiḥ pratisañcaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When all this universe becomes dissolved in Nature, this

## \|\| 43.4 \|\|

*svātmanyavasthitevyakte vikāre pratisaṃhṛte \|*  
*prakṛtiḥ puruṣaścaiva sādharmyeṇāvatiṣṭhataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. dissolution is designated 'natural' by the wise. When the Imperceptible subsists within itself, and when all modification is suspended, Nature and the Soul subsist with sameness

## \|\| 43.5 \|\|

*tadā tamaśca sattvañca samatvena vyavasthitau \|*  
*anudriktāvanūnau ca tatprotau ca parasparam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. of character. Then both darkness and goodness subsist in equipoise, neither being in excess or in deficiency, and

## \|\| 43.6 \|\|

*tileṣu vā yathā tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ payasi vā sthitam \|*  
*tathā tamasi sattve ca rajo 'pyanusṛtaṃ sthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. permeated by each other. Just as oil exists in sesamum seeds, or as ghee in milk, so passion also exists permeant within darkness and goodness.

## \|\| 43.7 \|\|

*utpattirbrahmaṇo yāvadāyuṣo dviparārdhikam \|*  
*tāvaddinaṃ pareśasya tatsamā saṃyame niśā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The day of the Supreme Lord lasts from the birth of Brahmá, as long as the two half paras which compose his life; and his night during the dissolution is of the same

## \|\| 43.8 \|\|

*aharmukhe prabuddhastu jagadādiranādimān \|*  
*sarvaheturacintyātmā paraḥ ko 'pyaparakriyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. duration. Now at the dawn of day he awakes, he who is the origin of the universe, who is without beginning, who is the cause of all things, whose soul transcends thought; every one else works in an inferior way.

## \|\| 43.9 \|\|

*prakṛtiṃ puruṣañcaiva prāviśyāśu jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*kṣobhayāmāsa yogena pareṇa parameśvaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Supreme God, quickly enters into Nature and the Soul, as the lord of the universe, and agitates them with his intense

## \|\| 43.10 \|\|

*yathā mado navastrīṇāṃ yathā vā mādhavānilaḥ \|*  
*anupraviṣṭaḥ kṣobhāya tathāsau yogamūrtimān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. supernatural power. Just as love, or a breeze of Spring, entering into young women tends to produce agitation, so does he, who is the embodiment of supernatural power.

## \|\| 43.11 \|\|

*pradhāne kṣobhyamāne tu sa devo brahmasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*samutpanno 'ṇḍakoṣastho yathā te kathitaṃ mayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When Pradhána is agitated, the god Brahmá is born and is contained within the cavity of the egg, as I have already

## \|\| 43.12 \|\|

*sa eva kṣobhakaḥ pūrvaṃ sa kṣobhyaḥ prakṛteḥ patiḥ \|*  
*sa saṅkocavikāśābhyāṃ pradhānatve 'pi ca sthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. told thee. At first he is the agitator; as the husband of Nature, he is the thing to be agitated; and he exists with

## \|\| 43.13 \|\|

*atpannaḥ sa jagadyoniraguṇo 'pi rajoguṇam \|*  
*bhuñjan pravartate sarge brahmatvaṃ samupāśritaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. contraction and expansion even in the state of Pradhána. He is born, though he is the birth-place of the universe; though devoid of qualities, he possesses the quality of passion; when he assumes the character of Brahmá, he engages in creation.

## \|\| 43.14 \|\|

*brahmatve sa prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā tataḥ sattvātirekavān \|*  
*viṣṇutvametya dharmeṇa kurute paripālanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the character of Brahmá he creates mankind; then possessing an excess of goodness, he becomesVishnu and

## \|\| 43.15 \|\|

*tatastamoguṇodrikto rudratve cākhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*upasaṃhṛtya vai śete trailokyaṃ triguṇo 'guṇaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. protects them righteously; then, with darkness preponderating in him, he as Rudra dissolves the whole universe with its three worlds, and sleeps. He possesses the three qualities,

## \|\| 43.16 \|\|

*yathā prāgvyāpakaḥ kṣetrī pālako lāvakastathā \|*  
*yathā sa saṃjñāmāyāti brahmaviṣṇvīśakāriṇīm \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. and yet he is destitute of qualities. Just as he is at first the pervading Soul, then the preserver, and lastly the destroyer, so he takes appellations which designate him as Brahmá,

## \|\| 43.17 \|\|

*brahmatve sṛjate lokān rudratve saṃharatyapi \|*  
*viṣṇutve cāpyudāsīnastistro 'vasthāḥ svayambhuvaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Vishnu or S'iva. As Brahmá he creates the world; and as Rudra he destroys them; and as Vishnu he holds a neutral position.These are the three conditions of the Self-existent.

## \|\| 43.18 \|\|

*rajo brahmā tamo rudro viṣṇuḥ sattvaṃ jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*eta eva trayo devā eta eva trayo guṇāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Passion and Brahmá; darkness and Rudra; goodness and, Vishnu the lord of the world: these indeed are the three

## \|\| 43.19 \|\|

*anyonyamithunā hyete anyonyāśrayiṇastathā \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ viyogo nahyeṣāṃ na tyajanti parasparam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. deities; these indeed are the three qualities. These verily are mutually paired, and are mutually dependant: they are not separated for a moment; they do not forsake one another.

## \|\| 43.20 \|\|

*evaṃ brahmā jagatpūrvo devadevaścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*rajoguṇaṃ samāśritya straṣṭṭatve sa vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus Brahmá, the four-faced god of gods, is anterior to the universe: assuming the quality of passion, he engages in creation.

## \|\| 43.21 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbho devādiranādirupacārataḥ \|*  
*bhūpadmakarṇikāsaṃstho brahmāgre samajāyata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Brahmá who is adored as Hiranya-garbha, the first of the gods, and without beginning, who sits in the middle of the

## \|\| 43.22 \|\|

*tasya varṣaśataṃ tvekaṃ paramāyurmahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmyeṇaiva hi mānena tasya saṃkhyāṃ nibodha me \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. lotus-like earth, was born in the beginning. One hundred years is the full length of life for him, the high-souled, according to the true Bráhmya computation. Hear from me how it is reckoned.

## \|\| 43.23 \|\|

*nimeṣairdaśabhiḥ kāṣṭhā tathā pañcabhirucyate \|*  
*kalāstriṃśacca vai kāṣṭhā muhūrtaṃ triṃśattāḥ kalāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A káshthá is said to be composed of fifteen winks of the eyelids; and thirty káshthás make a kalá; and thirty such

## \|\| 43.24 \|\|

*ahorātraṃ muhūrtānāṃ nṛṇāṃ triṃśattu vai smṛtam \|*  
*ahorātraiśca triṃśadbhiḥ pakṣau dvau māsa ucyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. kalás make a muhúrta.A day and night among men contain, it has been settled, thirty muhúrtas; and with thirty days

## \|\| 43.25 \|\|

*taiḥ ṣaḍbhirayanaṃ varṣaṃ dve 'yane dakṣiṇottare \|*  
*taddevānāmahorātraṃ dinaṃ tatrottarāyaṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. are reckoned the two lunar fortnights and the month; of six months consists the sun's half-yearly course; the two halfyearly courses on the south and north of the equator compose the year. Such a year is a day and night of the gods; the day thereof is the sun's northern half-yearly course.

## \|\| 43.26 \|\|

*divyairvarṣasahasraistu kṛtatretādisaṃjñitam \|*  
*caturyugaṃ dvādaśabhistadvibhāgaṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Now of twelve thousand divine years consist the four ages named the Krita, the Tretá, &c. Hear from me how they are divided.

## \|\| 43.27 \|\|

*catvāri tu sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ kṛtamucyate \|*  
*śatāni sandhyā catvāri sandhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Now the Krita age is said to have contained four thousand years; its commencing twilight was four hundred years, and

## \|\| 43.28 \|\|

*tretā trīṇi sahasrāṇi divyābdānāṃ śatatrayam \|*  
*tatsandhyā tatsamā caiva sandhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. the closing twilight was of the same duration. TheTretá age was three thousand divine years; and three hundred years was its commencing twilight, which was indeed of that duration, and its closing twilight was of the same duration.

## \|\| 43.29 \|\|

*dvāparaṃ dve sahasre tu varṣāṇāṃ dve śate tathā \|*  
*tasya sandhyā samākhyātā dve śatābde tadaṃśakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Dvápara age was two thousand years; and its commencing twilight is declared to have been two hundred years, and

## \|\| 43.30 \|\|

*kaliḥ sahasraṃ divyānāmabdānāṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*sandhyā sandhyāṃśakaścaiva śatakau samudāhṛtau \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. its closing twilight was two hundred years. The Kali age is a thousand divine years, O brahman; two hundreds of years are called its commencing and closing twilights;

## \|\| 43.31 \|\|

*eṣā dvādhaśasāhastrī yugākhyā kavibhiḥ kṛtā \|*  
*etat sahasraguṇitamo brāhmyamudāhṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. This period of twelve thousand divine years is called a yuga; it has been laid down by the poets; a thousand times this period are called one of Brahmá's days.

## \|\| 43.32 \|\|

*brahmaṇo divase brahman manavaḥ syuścaturdaśa \|*  
*bhavanti bhāgaśasteṣāṃ sahasraṃ tadvibhajyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In one of Brahmá's days, O brahman, there may be fourteen Manus. They live according to their portions; that

## \|\| 43.33 \|\|

*devāḥ saptarṣayaḥ sendrā manustatsūnavo nṛpāḥ \|*  
*manunā saha sṛjyante saṃhriyante ca pūrvavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. thousand is divided among them. The gods, the seven rishis, and Indra, Manu, and the kings his sons, are created with Manu and pass to dissolution with him in regular order.

## \|\| 43.34 \|\|

*caturyugānāṃ saṃkhyātā sādhikā hye kasaptatiḥ \|*  
*manvantaraṃ tasya saṃkhyāṃ mānuṣābdairnibodha me \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Seventy-one repetitions of the four ages, with a fraction in excess, constitute a manvantara; hear from me its computation in

## \|\| 43.35 \|\|

*triṃśatkoṭyastu saṃpūrṇāḥ saṃkhyātāḥ saṃkhyayā dvija \|*  
*satpaṣaṣṭistathānyāni niyutāni ca saṃkhyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. human years. Thirty full crores reckoned duly, O brahman,

## \|\| 43.36 \|\|

*viṃśatiśca sahasrāṇi kālo 'yaṃ sādhikaṃ vinā \|*  
*etanmanvantaraṃ proktaṃ divyairvarṣairnibodha me \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. and sixty-seven lakhs more by reckoning, and twenty thousands -this is the period of seventy-one times the four ages without the excess fraction; this is called a manvantara.

## \|\| 43.37 \|\|

*aṣṭau varṣasahasrāṇi divyayā saṃkhyayā yutam \|*  
*dvipañcāśattathānyāni sahasrāṇyadhikāni tu \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Hear it from me in divine years; eight hundred thousands of years by divine reckoning, and fifty-two thousands of

## \|\| 43.38 \|\|

*caturdaśaguṇo hyeṣa kālo brahmyamahaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*tasyānte pralayaḥ prokto brahman naimittiko budhaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. years more in addition. A day of Brahmá is declared to be this period multiplied fourteen times. At its termination the dissolution is declared by the wise to be the necessary result, O brahman.

## \|\| 43.39 \|\|

*bhūrloko 'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarlokaśca vināśinaḥ \|*  
*tathā vināśamāyānti maharlokaśca tiṣṭhati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Bhúr-loka, the Bhuvar-loka and the Svar-loka are perishable and pass to dissolution; and the Mahar-loka

## \|\| 43.40 \|\|

*tadvāsino 'pi tāpena janalokaṃ prayānti vai \|*  
*ekārṇave ca trailokye brahmā svapiti vai niśi \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. stands, yet the dwellers therein by reason of the heat go to the Jana-loka. And Brahmá sleeps indeed during the night in the three worlds which have been dissolved into one ocean.

## \|\| 43.41 \|\|

*tatpramāṇaiva sā rātristadante sṛjyate punaḥ \|*  
*evantu brahmaṇo varṣamekaṃ varṣaśatantu tat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. That night is of exactly the same duration. At its termination creation begins again. And so passes one of Brahmá's

## \|\| 43.42 \|\|

*śataṃ hi tasya varṣāṇāṃ paramityabhidhīyate \|*  
*pañcāśadbhistathā varṣaiḥ parārdhamiti kīrtyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. years, and a hundred years is the whole. For a hundred of his years is denominated a Para; and a Parárdha or half a

## \|\| 43.43 \|\|

*evamasya parārdhantu vyatītaṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*yasyānte 'bhūnmahākalpaḥ pādma ityabhiviśrutaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Para is well-known to be composed of fifty years. So then a Parárdha of his life has elapsed, O brahman; at the close of which occurred the Mahá-kalpa, which is famed as the Pádma.

## \|\| 43.44 \|\|

*dvitīyasya parārdhasya vartamānasya vai dvija \|*  
*vārāha iti kalpo 'yaṃ prathamaḥ parikalpitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Of the second Parárdha which is now passing, O brahman, the first kalpa (or cycle) ordained is this one called theVáráha.

## Chapter 44

## \|\| 44.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*yathā sasarja vai brahmā bhagavānādikṛt prajāḥ \|*  
*prajāpatiḥ patirdevastanme vistarato vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya continues -After the Pádma Mahá-kalpa Brahmá awoke, and as Náráyana raised the earth out of the sea of dissolution and fashioned it in its present shape -Then he created, first, the vegetable world secondly, the animal world -thirdly, the gods -fourthly, mankind -fifthly, Anugraha -and sixthly, the Bhútas - Márkandeya summarizes the nine creations, viz., these six, and the three described in Canto XLV.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. Tell me fully how Brahmá, the adorable, the creator, the lord of all creatures, the master, the divine, created all creatures.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 44.2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kathayāmyeṣa te brahman sasarja bhagavān yathā \|*

2\. Here I tell thee, O brahman, how the adorable eternal framer of the worlds created all the universe moveable and immoveable.

## Chapter 45

## \|\| 45.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*samāsāt kathitā sṛṣṭiḥ samyag bhagavatā mama \|*  
*devādīnāṃ bhavaṃ brahman vistarāttu bravīhi me \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya relates how Brahmá created the Asuras, the gods, the pitris and mankind, and the night and day and the two twilights -He mentions the times when those beings are powerful -He relates the creation of the Rákshasas, Yakshas, Serpents, Pisác'as, and Gandharvas -Next of all beasts, birds and other animals -Then of various sacred hymns and metres -Then of the lightning, thunder, and other phenomena -And lastly Brahmá assigned all things their shapes, pursuits and names.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. O adorable Sir, right well hast thou related the creation briefly to me; tell me, O bráhman, fully of the origin of the gods.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 45.2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kuśalākuśalairbrahman ! bhāvitā pūrvakamarmabhiḥ \|*  
*khyātā tathā hyanirmuktāḥ pralaye hyu pasaṃhṛtāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Creation is impregnated with the good and bad actions of previous existence, O bráhman; and because of this wellknown law, created beings, though they are destroyed in the dissolution, are not delivered, from the consequences of their actions.

## \|\| 45.3 \|\|

*devādyāḥ sthāvarāntāśca prajā brahmaṃścaturvidhāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ kurvataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ jajñire mānasāstadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The gods and other divine beings, and stationary things, and the four classes of mankind, O bráhman, were produced in his mind when Brahmá was engaged in creation.

## \|\| 45.4 \|\|

*tato devāsurān pitṝn mānuṣāṃśca catuṣṭayam \|*  
*sisṛkṣurambhāṃsyetāni svamātmānamayūyujat \|\| 4 \|\|*

## \|\| 45.5 \|\|

## Chapter 46

## \|\| 46.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*arvākstrotastu kathito bhavatā yastu mānuṣaḥ \|*  
*brahman ! vistarato brūhi brahmā samasṛjadyathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya describes the creation of the primeval human race, and their simple condition and happy life - When they ultimately died out, modern men fell from the sky, and lived in kalpa trees -Passionate affection sprung up among them -and covetousness next, which destroyed the trees, and drove them to form communities -Their measures of length are explained and fortresses, towns, villages and houses described - The Tretá Age began -with the existing rivers and vegetation -and the people lived on the vegetation - They then took private possession of property according to might, and the vegetation perished -Then they supplicated Brahmá, and he created all existing cereals and plants -The seventeen cereals and the fourteen sacrificial plants are specified -Brahmá ordained their means of livelihood, which could be gained only through labour, and their laws, castes, &c. -The spheres assigned to various classes after death are mentioned.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. Thou hast told me, Sir, of the group of beings in which the stream of life passes downwards; tell me fully, O

## \|\| 46.2 \|\|

2\. bráhman, how Brahmá created the human creation, and how he created the classes of men, and how their qualities, O wise Sir; and tell me what business has been assigned to the bráhmans and those other classes severally.

52\. to dwell in. As trees were their first kind of houses, so, with a remembrance of all that, those people built their houses.

## \|\| 46.53 \|\|

*vṛkṣasyaivaṅgatāḥ śākhāstathaivañcāparī gatāḥ \|*

53\. As some branches of a tree go in one direction, and others go in another direction, and some rise upwards and some bend downwards, even so they fashioned the branches in their

## \|\| 46.54 \|\|

54\. houses. Those branches, which were the branches of the kalpa trees at first, O bráhman, became rooms in the houses in consequence among those people.

## \|\| 46.55 \|\|

*kṛtvā dvandvopaghātante vārtopāyamacintayan \|*

55\. Those people ruined the trees by their strife, and afterwards pondered on their means of livelihood.When the kalpa

## \|\| 46.56 \|\|

*viṣādavyākulāstā vai prajāstṛṣṇākṣudhārditāḥ \|*

56\. trees had utterly perished along with the honey, those people were distressed by their afflictions, and suffered from thirst and hunger. Then became manifest their perfection at the

## \|\| 46.57 \|\|

*vārtāsvasādhitā hyanyā vṛṣṭistāsāṃ nikāmataḥ \|*

57\. beginning of the Tretá age. For their other business was spontaneously accomplished; they had rain according to their desire. The waters of their rain are the rivers which

## \|\| 46.58 \|\|

*vṛṣṭyāvaruddhairabhavat strotaḥ khātāni nimnagāḥ \|*

58\. flow here. By the obstruction of the rain the rivers, which existed on the earth scanty of water before that, became deep flowing channels.

## \|\| 46.59 \|\|

*tato bhūmeśca saṃyogādoṣadhyastāstadā bhavan \|*  
*aphālakṛṣṭāścānuptā grāmyāraṇyāścaturdaśa \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. And then by their union with the earth plants came into existence, of fourteen kinds, both those which grow on uncultivated soil, and those which grow unsown, both cultivated

## \|\| 46.60 \|\|

*ṛtupuṣpaphalāścaiva vṛkṣā gulmāśca jajñire \|*  
*prādurbhāvastu tretāyāmādyo 'yamauṣadhasya tu \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. and wild.And treesand shrubsbearingflowersandfruitin their seasons were produced. This manifestation of

## \|\| 46.61 \|\|

*tenauṣadhena vartante prajāstretāyuge mune \|*  
*rāgalobhau samāsādya prajāścākasmikau tadā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. vegetation appeared first in the Tretá age. On that vegetation the people subsist in the Tretá age, O Muni. And then

## \|\| 46.62 \|\|

*tatastāḥ paryagvahṇanta nadīkṣetrāṇi parvatān \|*  
*vṛkṣagulmauṣadhīścaivamātmanyāyādyathābalam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. lapsing into novel passion and covetousness those people next took possession of rivers and fields, mountains, and trees, shrubs and plants in their own right even according to might.

## \|\| 46.63 \|\|

*tena doṣeṇa tā neśurauṣadhyo miṣatāṃ dvija \|*  
*agrasad bhūryugapattāstadauṣadhyo mahāmate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Through that their sin those plants perished before their very eyes, and the earth then devoured those plants at once, O

## \|\| 46.64 \|\|

*punastāsu praṇaṣṭāsu vibhrāntāstāḥ punaḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ kṣudhārtāḥ parameṣṭhinam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. most wise bráhman. Moreover when that vegetation had perished, those people fell into still further confusion. Suffering from hunger, they resorted to Brahmá, the most

## \|\| 46.65 \|\|

*sa cāpi tattvato jñātvā tadā grastāṃ vasundharām \|*

65\. high, as their preserver. And he, the mighty lord, knowing full well then that the earth had swallowed it up, milked

## \|\| 46.66 \|\|

*dugdheyaṃ gaustadā tena śasyāni pṛthivītale \|*

66\. her treating mount Meru as her calf. This earth-cow was then milked by him, the cereals came into existence on the

## \|\| 46.67 \|\|

*oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntā gaṇāḥ saptadaśā smṛtāḥ \|*  
*vrīhayaśca yavāścaiva godhūmā aṇavastilāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. face of the earth, the seeds, the cultivated and wild plants besides, which are annuals, known as comprising seventeen classes according to tradition. The various kinds of both

## \|\| 46.68 \|\|

*priyaṅgavo hyudārāśca koradūṣāḥ sacīnakāḥ \|*  
*māṣā mudgā masūrāśca niṣpāvāḥ sakulatthakāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. rice and barley, wheat, anu grain, sesamum, priyangu, udára, koradúsha, and c'ínaka, másha, green gram,

## \|\| 46.69 \|\|

*āḍhakāścaṇakāścaiva gaṇāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ityetā oṣadhīnāntu grāmyāṇāṃ jātayaḥ purā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. and masúra, the finest pulse, and kulatthaka, ádhaka pulse, and chick-pea and hemp are known as the seven teen classes. These are the olden kinds of cultivated plants.

## \|\| 46.70 \|\|

*oṣadhyo jajñiyāścaiva grāmyāraṇyāścaturdaśa \|*  
*vrīhayaśca yavāścaiva godhūmā aṇavastilāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70.And there are fourteen kinds of plants for use in sacrifices, both cultivated and wild, viz., the various kinds of both rice

## \|\| 46.71 \|\|

*priyaṅgusaptamā hyete aṣṭamāstu kulatthakāḥ \|*  
*śyāmākāstvatha nīvārā yattilā sagavedhukāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. and barley, wheat, anu grain, sesamum, and seventh among them priyangu, and eighth kulatthaka, and syámáka grain,

## \|\| 46.72 \|\|

*kuruvindā markaṭakāstathā veṇuyavāśca ye \|*

72\. wild rice, wild sesamum, and gavedhuka grass, kuruvinda grass, markataka, and venu-gradha; and these indeed are traditionally known as the fourteen cultivated and wild plants

## \|\| 46.73 \|\|

*yadā prasṛṣṭā oṣadhyo na prarohanti tāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sa tāsāṃ vṛddhyarthaṃ vārtopāyañcakāra ha \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. for use in sacrifices. When these plants are abandoned, they do not spring forth again. Thereupon the adorable self-existent Brahmá devised

## \|\| 46.74 \|\|

*brahmā svayambhūrbhagavān hastasiddhiñca karmajām \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛtyathauṣadhyaḥ kṛṣṭapacyāstu jajñire \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. means of livelihood for the advancement of those people, and the perfection of the hands which results from work. Thenceforward plants were produced, which must ripen after ploughing.

## \|\| 46.75 \|\|

*saṃsiddhāyāntu vārtāyāṃ tatastāsāṃ svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*maryādāṃ sthāpayāmāsa yathānyāyaṃ yathāguṇam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. But when their livelihood was thoroughly ordained, the lord himself next established bounds for them according to

## \|\| 46.76 \|\|

*varṇānāmāśramāṇāñca dharmān dharmabhṛtāṃvara \|*  
*lokānāṃ sarvavarṇānāṃ samyagdharmārthapālinām \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. justice and according to their qualities; also the laws of the castes and of the four periods of a bráhman's life, and of the worlds with all their castes which duly maintain righteousness and wealth, O most righteous Muni.

## \|\| 46.77 \|\|

*prājāpatyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ smṛtaṃ sthānaṃ kriyāvatām \|*  
*sthānamaindraṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ saṃgrāmeṣvapalāyinām \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Prájápatya is traditionally declared to be the sphere assigned after death to bráhmans who perform the ceremonies. Aindra is the sphere of kshatriyas who flee not in battle.

## \|\| 46.78 \|\|

*vaiśyānāṃ mārutaṃ sthānaṃ svadharmamanuvartatām \|*  
*gāndharvaṃ śūdrajātīnāṃ paricaryānuvartatām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Máruta is the sphere of vaisyas who observe their own proper laws. Gándharva is the sphere of the various classes

## \|\| 46.79 \|\|

*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇāmṛṣīṇāmūrdhvaretasām \|*  
*smṛtaṃ teṣāntu yat sthānaṃ tadeva guruvāsinām \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. of súdras who perform menial service. The sphere of those eighty-eight thousand rishis who live in perpetual chastity has been traditionally declared to be that of the inhabitants

## \|\| 46.80 \|\|

*saptarṣoṇāntu yat sthānaṃ smṛtaṃ tadvai vanaukasām \|*  
*prājāpatyaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ nyāsināṃ brahmaṇaḥ kṣayam \|*  
*yogināmamṛtaṃ sthānamiti vai sthānakalpanā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. of Jupiter. The sphere of the Seven Rishis has been traditionally declared to be that of hermits. Prájápatya is the sphere of householders; the abode, of Brahmá is for those men who have abandoned all worldly concerns; the world of immortality is for yogis -such is the ordinance of the various spheres assigned after death.

## Chapter 47

## \|\| 47.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tato 'bhidyāyatastasya jajñire mānasīḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*taccharīrasamutpannaiḥ kāryaistaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ saha \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmá next created the nine Sages, Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Maríc'i, Daksha, Atri and Vasishtha -and also Rudra, Sankalpa and Dharma -All these were all-wise and devoid of passions -Brahmá in anger created a being half male, half female, who at his order divided himself into many male and female beings.

Brahmá then created the Manu Sváyambhuva and his wife Sata-rúpá -They had two sons Priya-vrata and Uttána-páda, and also two daughters. Ruc'i married one daughter Riddhi and begat Yajna and Dakshiná.

Daksha married the other daughter Prasúti and begot 24 daughters, whose names are mentioned, and who became Dharma's wives, and also 11 other daughters whose names are mentioned, and who became the wives of the other sages and of Agni and the Pitris -The children of these daughters are mentioned.

A-dharma and his offspring are mentioned, Naraka, Bhaya, Mrityu &c. -The actions of Mrityu's sons are explained -Chief among them is Duhsaha -to him Brahmá assigned a dwelling and raiment, a long catalogue of bad deeds as nourishment, and certain places and times for his success, but excluded a list of other persons and places from his influence.

Márkandeya spoke:

1.Then while he was meditating, mankind were begotten in his mind, together with their occupations, and implements

## \|\| 47.2 \|\|

*kṣetrajñāḥ samavartanta gātrebyastasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*te sarve samavartanta ye mayā pragudāhṛtāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. which were produced from his body. Spirits in bodily form were produced from the limbs of him, the wise god. All those whom I have already mentioned came into existence.

## \|\| 47.3 \|\|

*devādyāḥ sthāvarāntāśca traiguṇyaviṣayāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*evaṃbhūtāni sṛṣṭāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. All created beings from the gods down to those whose condition is stationary are known to be subject to the three qualities such was the constitution of created things, immoveable and moveable.

## \|\| 47.4 \|\|

*yadāsya tāḥ prajāḥ sarvā na vyavardhanta dhīmataḥ \|*  
*athānyānmānasān putrānu sadṛśānātmano 'sṛjat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When all that offspring of him, the wise one, did not increase, he created other mind-born sons like unto himself, viz.,

## \|\| 47.5 \|\|

*bhṛguṃ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratumaṅgirasantathā \|*  
*marīciṃ dakṣamatriñca vasiṣṭañcaiva mānasam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Angiras, Maríc’i, Daksha, and Atri, and the mind-born Vasishtha -these were the

## \|\| 47.6 \|\|

*nava brahmāṇa ityete purāṇe niścayaṅgatāḥ \|*  
*tato 'sṛjat punarbrahmā rudraṃ krodhātmasambhavam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. nine sons of Brahmá, they are positively mentioned in the Puránas. Next Brahmá further created Rudra, whose birth was from

## \|\| 47.7 \|\|

*saṅkalpañcaiva dharmañca pūrveṣāmapi pūrvajam \|*  
*sanandanādayo ye ca pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. his soul when it was angry, and Sankalpa, and Dharma who was begotten before all the preceding sons. And those who with their sons and other relatives were first

## \|\| 47.8 \|\|

*na te lokeṣu sajjanto nirapekṣāḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*sarve te 'nāgatajñānā vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. created by the Self-existent, felt no attachment for the worlds, but showed disregard and were composed in mind. They all knew the future, they were free from passion, free from envy.

## \|\| 47.9 \|\|

*teṣvevaṃ nirapekṣeṣu lokasṛṣṭau mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇo 'būnmahākrodhastatrotpannor'kasannibhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When they thus showed disregard at the creation of the worlds, the high-souled Brahmá grew very wrathful; then

## \|\| 47.10 \|\|

*ardhanārīnaravapuḥ puruṣo 'tiśarīravān \|*  
*vibhajātmānamityuktvā sa tadāntardadhe tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. was produced there a male like to the sun, possessed of an immense body, the body being half man's and half woman's.

## \|\| 47.11 \|\|

*sa cokto vai pṛthak strītvaṃ puruṣatvaṃ tathākarot \|*  
*bibheda puruṣatvañca daśadhā caikadhā tu saḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. "Divide thyself" said the god, and then disappeared.And he being thus accosted separated the female and male natures; and he divided the male nature into eleven parts.

## \|\| 47.12 \|\|

*saumyāsaumyaistathā śāntaiḥ puṃstvaṃ strītvañca sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*bibheda bahudhā devaḥ puruṣairasitaiḥ sitaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then the divine lord divided the male and female natures into many parts with men, gentle and cruel, calm, black and white.

## \|\| 47.13 \|\|

*tato brahmātmasambhūtaṃ pūrvaṃ svāyambhuvaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ kṛtvā prajāpālo manuṃ dvija \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Next the lord Brahmá became the guardian of his offspring by creating the first Manu Sváyambhuva, begotten

## \|\| 47.14 \|\|

*śatarūpāñca tāṃ nārīṃ taponirdhūtakalmaṣām \|*  
*svāyambhuvo manurdevaḥ patnītve jagṛhe vibhuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. from and like unto himself, O bráhman, and the woman Sata-rúpá, who was cleansed from blemishes through austerities. The divine and mighty Manu Sváyambhuva took her

## \|\| 47.15 \|\|

*tasmācca puruṣāt putrau śatarūpā vyajāyata \|*  
*priyavratottānapādau prakhyātāvātmakarmabhiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. for his wife. And through him her husband Sata-rúpá brought forth two sons, Priya-vrata and Uttána-páda, famed

## \|\| 47.16 \|\|

*kanye dve ca tathā ṛddhiṃ prasūtiñca tataḥ pitā \|*  
*dadau pursūtiṃ dakṣāya tathā ṛddhiṃ ruceḥ purā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. through their own actions, and two daughters also, Riddhi and Prasúti. Then their father gave Prasúti in marriage to

*prajāpatiḥ sa jagrāha tayoryajñaḥ sadakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*putro jajñe mahābhāga ! dampatīmithunaṃ tataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Daksha and Riddhi to Ruc'i of yore. The Prajá-pati Rúc'i took his wife, and from them both a sonYajna was born and a daughter Dakshiná, O illustrious Sir; these two then

## \|\| 47.18 \|\|

*yajñasya dakṣiṇāyāntu putrā dvādaśa jajñire \|*  
*yāmā iti samākhyātā devāḥ svāyambhuvo 'ntare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. became husband and wife, and Yajna begat of Dakshiná twelve sons; the glorious sons of Yajna and Dakshiná were

## \|\| 47.19 \|\|

*tasya putrāstu yajñasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ sabhāsvarāḥ \|*  
*prasūtyāñca tathā dakṣaścatastro viṃśatistathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. the gods well known as the Yámas in the epoch of Manu Sváyambhuva. And Daksha moreover begat twenty and four daughters of

## \|\| 47.20 \|\|

*sasarja kanyāstāsāñca samyaṅnāmāni me śṛṇu \|*  
*śraddhā lakṣmīrdhṛtistuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā kriyā tathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Prasúti; hear also from me their names in order -Sraddhá (Faith), Lakshmí (Good Fortune), Dhriti (Constancy), Tushti (Satisfaction), Pushti (Nourishment), Medhá (MentalVigour),

## \|\| 47.21 \|\|

*buddhirlajjā vapuḥ śāntiḥ siddhiḥ kīrtistrayodaśī \|*

21\. and Kriyá (Action), Buddhi (Intelligence), Lajjá (Modesty), Vapus (Bodily Beauty), Sánti (Tranquillity), Siddhi (Perfection), and Kírti (Fame) the thirteenth. The lord Dharma took these daughters of Daksha for his wives.

## \|\| 47.22 \|\|

*tābhyaḥ śiṣṭā yavīyasya ekādaśa sulocanāḥ \|*  
*khyātiḥ satyatha sambhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītistathā kṣamā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Besides them and younger were the eleven lovely-eyed daughters -Khyáti (Celebrity), and Satí (Truth), Sambhúti (Fitness), Smriti (Memory), Príti (Affection), and Kshamá

## \|\| 47.23 \|\|

*santatiścānasūyā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā \|*  
*bhṛgurbhavo marīciśca tathā caivāṅgirā muniḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (Patience), and Sannati (Humility), and Anasúyá (Sincerity), Urjá (Strength), Sváhá (the oblation to the gods), and Svadhá (the oblation to the pitris). The Rishis Bhrigu,

## \|\| 47.24 \|\|

*pulastyaḥ pulahaścaiva kratuśca ṛṣayastathā \|*  
*vasiṣṭho 'tristathā vahniḥ pitaraśca yathākramam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Bhava and Maríc’i, and the Muni Angiras also, Pulastya and Pulaha, and Kratu,Vasishtha, andAtri, Vahni and the

## \|\| 47.25 \|\|

*khyātyādyā jagṛhuḥ kanyā munayo munisattamāḥ \|*  
*śraddhā kāmaṃ śrīśca darpaṃ niyamaṃ dhṛtirātmajam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Pitris in order -these Munis, the most illustrious among Munis, took these daughters, Khyáti and the others, in marriage. Sraddhá gave birth to Káma (Love); and Srí to Darpa

## \|\| 47.26 \|\|

*santoṣañca tathā tuṣṭirlobhaṃ puṣṭirajāyata \|*  
*medhā śrutaṃ kriyā daṇḍaṃ nayaṃ vinayameva ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. (Pride); Dhriti to Niyama (Restraint) her son; and Tushti also to Santosha (Contentment); Pushti to Lobha (Covetousness); Medhá to Sruta (Revelation); Kriyá to Danda (Punishment), Naya (Prudence), and Vinaya (Decorum);

## \|\| 47.27 \|\|

27\. Buddhi gave birth to Bodha (Wisdom); and Lajjá to Vinaya (Decorum);Vapus toVyavasáya (Industry) her son; and

## \|\| 47.28 \|\|

28\. S'ánti gave birth to Kshema (Ease); Siddhi to Sukha (Happiness); Kírti to Yasas (Renown). These were the offspring of Dharma. She bare by Káma a grandson to Dharma, namely, Harsha (Joy) who brims over with joyousness.

## \|\| 47.29 \|\|

*hiṃsā bhāryā tvadharmasya tasyāṃ jajñe tathānṛtam \|*

29\. Now Himsá (Injury) was the wife of A-dharma (Unrighteousness); and Anrita (Falsehood) was born of her, and a daughter Nirriti (Destruction) was born of her, and two sons

## \|\| 47.30 \|\|

*māyā ca vedanā caiva mithunaṃ dvayametayoḥ \|*

30\. Naraka (Hell) and Bhaya (Fear), and Máyá (Illusion) and Vedaná (Pain). And with these two females the two sons formed two married pairs; and of those two, Máyá gave birth to Mrityu (Death) who carries created beings away, and

## \|\| 47.31 \|\|

*vedanātmasutañcāpi duḥkhaṃ jajñe 'tha rauravāt \|*  
*mṛtyorvyādhi-jarā-śoka-tṛṣṇā-krodhāśca jajñire \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Vedaná gave birth by Raurava to her son Duhkha (Misery). And Vyádhi (Sickness), Jará (Old Age), Soka (Grief), Trishná (Thirst) and Krodha (Anger) were begotten by

## \|\| 47.32 \|\|

*duḥ khodbhavāḥ smṛtā hyete sarve vādharmalakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*naiṣāṃ bhāryāsti putro vā sarve te hyūrdhvaretasaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Mrityu; or all these, who have the characteristics of Adharma, are traditionally declared to have sprung from Duhkha. No wife have they, nor son; they all live in perpetual chastity.

## \|\| 47.33 \|\|

*nirṛtiśca tathā cānyā mṛtyorbhāryābhavanmune \|*  
*alakṣmīrnāma tasyāñca mṛtyoḥ putrāścaturdaśa \|\| 33 \|\|*

Brahmá spoke:

## \|\| 47.41 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*nāttavyante jagadidaṃ jahi kopaṃ śamaṃ vraja \|*  
*tyajaināntāmasī vṛttimapāsya rajasaḥ kalām \|\| 41 \|\|*

Duhsaha spoke:

## \|\| 47.42 \|\|

*kṣutkṣāmo 'smi jagannātha ! pipāsuścāpi durbalaḥ \|*

Brahmá spoke:

## \|\| 47.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*tavāśrayo gṛhaṃ puṃsāṃ janaścādhārmiko balam \|*

## Chapter 48

## \|\| 48.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*duḥ sahasyābhavadbhāryā nirmāṣṭirnāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*jātā kalestu bhāryāyāmṛtau cāṇḍāladarśanāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Duhsaha had eight sons and eight daughters -their names are mentioned -The evil functions of the several sons and daughters are described, and the remedies against them -Their offspring are mentioned, and their evil actions described.

These beings are almost all personifications of physical injuries, moral vices and social offences.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Duhsaha had a wife named Nirmáshti; now she was begotten in Kali's wife when she saw a c'andála at the time of

## \|\| 48.2 \|\|

*tayorapatyānyabhavane jagadvyāpīni ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*aṣṭau kumārāḥ kanyāśca tathāṣṭāvatibhīṣaṇāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. her menstruation. They had sixteen children, who pervade the world, eight sons and eight daughters, all very terrible.

## \|\| 48.3 \|\|

*tantākṛṣṭistathoktiśca parivartastathāparaḥ \|*  
*aṅgadhruk śakuniścaiva gaṇḍaprāntaratistathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Dantákrishti and Ukti, and Parivarta the next,Anga-dhrish

## \|\| 48.4 \|\|

*garbhahā sasyahā cānyaḥ kumārāstanayāstayoḥ \|*

4\. and Sakuni and Ganda-pránta-rati, Garbha-han and the last Sasya-han were their male children.And they had eight

## \|\| 48.5 \|\|

*niyojikā vai prathamā tathaivānyā virodhinī \|*  
*svayaṃhārakarī caiva bhrāmaṇī ṛtuhārikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. daughters besides; hear their names from me. The first was Niyojiká, and the second Virodhiní, and Svayam-hára-karí,

## \|\| 48.6 \|\|

*smṛtibījahare cānye tayoḥ kanye 'tidāruṇe \|*  
*vidveṣaṇyaṣṭamī nāma kanyā lokabhayāvahā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Bhrámaní, Ritu-báriká, and two other very terrible daughters Smriti-hará and Víja-hará; and the eighth daughter was named Vidveshaní who causes terror to mankind.

## \|\| 48.7 \|\|

*etāsāṃ karma vakṣyāmi doṣapraśamanañca yat \|*  
*aṣṭānāñca kumārāṇāṃ śruyatāṃ dvijasattama \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I will describe what the several functions of the eight sons are, and what are the remedies against the evils which they work; hearken to me, O bráhman.

## \|\| 48.8 \|\|

*dantākṛṣṭiḥ prasuptānāṃ bālānāṃ daśanasthitaḥ \|*  
*karoti dantasaṃgharṣaṃ cikīrṣurduḥ sahāgamam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Dantákrishti taking his station in the teeth of newly born children produces intense wind, with the desire of effecting

## \|\| 48.9 \|\|

*tasyopaśamanaṃ kāryaṃ suptasya sitasarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*śayanasyopari kṣiptairmānuṣairdaśanopari \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. an attack from Duhsaha. The remedy against him is to be applied by men by means of white mustard cast upon the bed

*suvārccalauṣadhīsnānāttathā sacchāstrakīrtanāt \|*  
*uṣṭrakaṇṭakakhaḍgāsthi-kṣaumavastravidhāraṇāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. and upon the teeth of the sleeping child; and by bathing it with medicinal herbs of great splendour, by reciting good scriptures, and by supporting it on a camel, a thorn, a sword, a bone, or a linen cloth.

## \|\| 48.11 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatyanyakumārastu tathāsttvityasakṛd bruvan \|*

11\. Now the second son assigns good and bad fortune to men, while he says repeatedly, "let it be so!"; hence he is called

*duṣṭe śrute tathaivokte kīrtanīyo janārdanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Ukti, and that is his precise function. Hence wise men must always say, "May fate be auspicious!" And when anything

*carācaragururbrahmā yā yasya kuladevatā \|*  
*anyagarbhe parān garbhān sadaiva parivartayan \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. bad is heard or spoken, let praise be offered to S'iva, and to Brahmá, the spiritual preceptor of all that exists both moveable and immoveable, and to each person's own particular family-deity.

14\. The son who finds delight in always interchanging the foetus between one womb and another, and in interchanging the words in the mouth of a speaker, is called Parivartaka;

## \|\| 48.15 \|\|

36\. liquor-stores, the colour out of saffron and other coloured objects, and the thread out of cotton clothes. She is rightly named Svayam-háriká, for she is perpetually taking things

39\. Now the other daughter, who produces perturbation in a

40\. man who dwells in one place, is called Bhrámaní. Now a man should secure protection against her by scattering white mustard seed on his seat, on his bed, and on the ground

47\. And the eighth daughter named Dveshani, who causes terror among mankind, is she who renders a man, or even

## \|\| 48.48 \|\|

*eteṣāntu kumārāṇāṃ kanyānāṃ dvijasattama \|*

## \|\| 48.67 \|\|

## \|\| 48.68 \|\|

## Chapter 49

## \|\| 49.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityeṣa tāmasaḥ sargo brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*rudrasargaṃ pravakṣyāmi tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya narrates the creation of Rudra in his eight personalities -and mentions their names, stations, wives and sons -He mentions briefly the wives and offspring of the rishis, Bhrigu (from whom he himself was descended), Maríc’i, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Vasishtha, and Agni, and also of the Pitris.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Such was the creation, which Brahmá of inscrutable origin made, characterized by darkness. I will tell thee of the creation of the Rudras. Hearken to me while I narrate it.

## Chapter 50

## \|\| 50.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*svāyambhuvaṃ tvayākhyātametanmanvantarañca yat \|*  
*tadahaṃ bhagavan ! samyak śrotumicchāmi kathyatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya states the duration of the Manvantaras, and mentions the names of the Manus past, present and future -He mentions the descendants of Manu Sváyambhuva and his son Priya-vrata, and explains how the whole world with its seven continents was peopled by them and divided among them -Jambu-dvipa was assigned to Priya-vrata's son Agnidhra, and was portioned out among Agnidhra's sons -His eldest son Nábhi begot Rishabha, and Rishabha begot Bharata, to whom India was assigned.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. Adorable Sir! I wish to hear fully of this Sváyambhuva Manvantara also which thou hast mentioned. Tell me of it,

## \|\| 50.2 \|\|

*manvantarapramāṇañca devā devarṣayastathā \|*  
*ye ca kṣitīśā bhagavan ! devendraścaiva yastathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. and also of the duration of this Manvantara, and its gods and rishis, and the kings who ruled during it, and also who was the lord of the gods during it, adorable Sir!

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 50.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*manvantarāṇāṃ saṃkhyātā sādhikā hyekasaptatiḥ \|*  
*mānuṣeṇa pramāṇena śṛṇu manvantarañca me \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saptaṣaṣṭistathānyāni niyutāni ca saṃkhyayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

## \|\| 50.5 \|\|

*manvantarapramāṇañca ityetat sādhikaṃ vinā \|*

## Chapter 51

## \|\| 51.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*katidvīpāḥ samudrā vā parvatā vā kati dvija \|*  
*kiyanti caiva varṣāṇi teṣāṃ nadyaśca kā mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya tells Kraushtuki further the size of the earth, and the order and dimensions of the seven continents and their oceans -He describes Jambu-dvípa, the countries in it, and Meru and the other mountains; and mentions various local facts.

Kraustuki spoke:

1\. How many are the continents, and how many the oceans, and how many are the mountains, O bráhman?And how many are the countries, and what are their rivers, O Muni?

## \|\| 51.2 \|\|

*mahābhūtapramāṇañca lokālokantathaiva ca \|*  
*paryāsaṃ parimāṇañca gatiñcandrārkayorapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. And the size of the great objects of nature, and the Loká-loka mountain-range; the circumference, and the size and

## \|\| 51.3 \|\|

*etat prabrūhi me sarvaṃ vistareṇa mahāmune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. the course of the moon and the sun also -tell me all this at length, O great Muni.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 51.4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śatārdhakoṭivistārā pṛthivī kṛtstraśo dvija \|*  
*tasyā hi sthānamakhilaṃ kathayāmi śṛṇuṣva tat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The earth is fifty times ten million yojanas broad in every direction, O bráhman. I tell thee of its entire constitution,

## \|\| 51.5 \|\|

*ye te dvīpā mayā proktā jambudvīpādayo dvija \|*  
*puṣkarāntā mahābhāga ! śṛṇveṣāṃ vistaraṃ punaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

## Chapter 53

## \|\| 53.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*

Márkandeya describes the course of the River Ganges from the moon on to mount Meru, then in four streams flowing east, south, west and north, of which the southern stream was allowed by S'iva to flow through India at the entreaties of King Bhagíratha.

He describes briefly the happy condition of all the other countries (except India) in Jambu-dvípa.

1\. The foot of Náráyana, moreover, who is the origin of the universe, supports the earth.The divine river Ganges

16\. Now she flowed on to mount Su-pársva also, which is at the foot of Meru; there she is famed as Somá. She flowed

*tatpāvayantī saṃprāptā mahābhadraṃ sarovaram \|*  
*tataśca śaṅkhakūṭaṃ sā prayātā vai mahānadī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. to the wood of Savitri. Overflowing it, she reached lake Mahá-bhadra; and thence she passed as a great river to

## \|\| 53.18 \|\|

*tasmācca vṛṣabhādīn sā kramāt prāpya śiloccayān \|*  
*mahārṇavamanuprāptā plāvayitvottarān kurūn \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. mount S'ankha-kúta; and thence reaching in succession Vrishabha and the other mountains on the north, and overflowing the Northern Kurus she entered the great ocean.

## \|\| 53.19 \|\|

*evameṣā mayā gaṅgāṃ kathitā te dvijarṣabha \|*  
*jambudvīpaniveśaśca varṣāṇi ca yathātatham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus I have appropriately described to thee, O bráhman, this river, the Ganges, and the countries according to their

## \|\| 53.20 \|\|

*vasanti teṣu sarveṣu prajāḥ kiṃpuruṣādiṣu \|*  
*sukhaprāyā nirātaṅkā nyūnatotkarṣavarjitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. arrangement in Jambu-dvípa. In Kim-purusha and all the other countries dwell people, who have almost unalloyed happiness, who are free from sickness, and who are exempt

## \|\| 53.21 \|\|

*navasvapi ca varṣeṣu sapta sapta kulācalāḥ \|*  
*ekaikasmiṃstathā deśe nadyaścādriviniḥ sṛtāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. from low and high diversities of condition. In each of the nine countries in it are seven mountain ranges. And then in each country there are rivers flowing down from the

## \|\| 53.22 \|\|

*yāni kiṃpuruṣādyāni varṣāṇyaṣṭau dvijottama \|*  
*teṣūdbhijjāni toyāni meghavāryatra bhārate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. mountains. In Kim-purusha and the seven other countries, O bráhman, waters bubble up from the ground; here in Bhárata

## \|\| 53.23 \|\|

*vārkṣo svābhāvikī deśyā toyotthā mānasī tathā \|*  
*karmajā ca nṛṇāṃ siddharvarṣeṣveteṣu cāṣṭasu \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. we have rain. And in these eight countries men enjoy a perfection which comes from the trees, from their own natural dispositions, from the localities, from the water, from

## \|\| 53.24 \|\|

*kāmapradebhyo vṛkṣebhyo vārkṣo siddhiḥ svabhāvajā \|*  
*svābhāvikī samākhyātā tṛptirdeśyā ca daiśikī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. their mental condition and from their actions. The treebestowed perfection is obtained from the trees that grant them every wish; the natural is well-known as that which springs from the natural disposition; and the local delight

## \|\| 53.25 \|\|

*apāṃ śaukṣmyācca toyotthā dhyānopetā ca mānasī \|*  
*upāsanādikāryāttu dharmajā sāpyudāhṛtā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. is that which is connected with the land itself; and the water-given perfection comes from the delicacy of the water; and the mental is derived from meditation; and the perfection which comes from reverential service and the performance of other duties is denominated righteousness-produced.

## \|\| 53.26 \|\|

*na caiteṣu yugāvasthā nādhyo vyādhayo na ca \|*  
*puṇyāpuṇyasamārambho naiva teṣu dvijottama \|\| 26 \|\|*

26.And in these countries the ages do not exist, nor bodily nor mental sicknesses; nor is there any undertaking involving merit or demerit there, O brahman.

## Chapter 54

## \|\| 54.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*bhagavan ! kathitantvetajjambūdvīpaṃ samāsataḥ \|*  
*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ karma nānyatra puṇyadam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya mentions the nine divisions of Bhárata, one of which is India -He mentions the seven mountain ranges in India (exclusive of the Himálaya Mountains) and names twenty-two separate hills -He mentions the chief rivers in India, grouping them according to the mountain ranges out of which they rise -He mentions the chief peoples in India and on its borders, arranging them according to the main natural divisions of the country -and he concludes with general descriptive remarks and an encomium on India as the sole land of action.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. Adorable Sir! thou hast fully described this Jambu-dvípa. Just as thou hast declared it, merit-producing action exists

## \|\| 54.2 \|\|

*pāpāya vā mahābhāga ! varjayitvā tu bhāratam \|*  
*itaḥ svargaśca mokṣaśca madhyañcāntañca gamyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. nowhere else, nor action that tends to sin, except in Bhárata, O illustrious Sir! And from this land both Svarga is attained, and final emancipation from existence, and the medium

## \|\| 54.3 \|\|

*na khalvanyatra martyānāṃ bhūmau karma vidhīyate \|*  
*tasmādvistaraśo brahman ! mamaitadbhārataṃ vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. end also. Verily nowhere else on earth is action ordained for mortals. Therefore tell me, O bráhman, about

## \|\| 54.4 \|\|

*ye cāsya bhedā yāvanto yathāvat sthitireva ca \|*  
*varṣo 'yaṃ dvijaśārdūla ! ye cāsmin deśaparvatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. this Bhárata in detail, and what are its divisions, and how many they are, and what is its constitution accurately; it is the country, and what are the provinces and the mountains in it, O bráhman?

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 54.5 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*bhāratasyāsya varṣasya nava bhedānnibodha me \|*  
*samudrāntaritā jñeyāste tvagamyāḥ parasparam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hear from me the nine divisions of this country Bhárata;

## \|\| 54.6 \|\|

*indradvīpaḥ kaśerumāṃstāmravarṇo gabhastimān \|*  
*nāgadvīpastathā saumyo gāndharvo vāruṇastathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. they must be known as extending to the ocean, but as being mutually inaccessible. They are Indra-dvípa, Kaserúmat,

## \|\| 54.7 \|\|

*ayantu navamasteṣāṃ dvīpaḥ sāgarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ hasastraṃ vai dvīpo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇottarāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Támra-varna, Gabhasti-mat, and Nága-dvípa, Saumya, Gándharva, and Váruna, and this is the ninth dvípa among them, and it is surrounded by the sea. This dvípa

## \|\| 54.8 \|\|

*pūrve kirātā yasyānte paścime yavanāstathā \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścāntaḥ sthitā dvija \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. is a thousand yojanas from south to north.At its east end are the Kirátas, and at the west the Yavanas. Within it dwell bráhmans, kshatriyas, vaisyas and súdras, O bráhman.

## \|\| 54.9 \|\|

*ijyādhyāyavaṇijyādyaiḥ karmabhiḥ kṛtapāvanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃvyavahāraśca ebhiḥ karmabhiriṣyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They accomplish their purification with the occupations of sacrifice, meditation, trade, &c.; and they seek their

## \|\| 54.10 \|\|

*svargāpavargaprāptiśca puṇyaṃ pāpañca vai tadā \|*  
*mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣaparvataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. mutual business through these occupations, and they gain Svarga or final emancipation from existence, merit and sin then. The seven mountain ranges in it are Mahendra,

## \|\| 54.11 \|\|

*vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca saptaivātra kulācalāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sahasraśaścānye bhūdharā ye samīpagāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Malaya, Sahya, S'ukti-mat, the Riksha mountains, and Vindhya, and Páripátra.And there are other hills besides them, in thousands, which are situated

## \|\| 54.12 \|\|

*vistārocchrayiṇo ramyā vipulāścātra sānavaḥ \|*  
*kolāhalaḥ savaibhrājo mandaro dardurācalaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. near them. Their summits are broad and lofty, and are delightful and spacious; - Koláhala, and Vaibhrája,

## \|\| 54.13 \|\|

*vātasvano vaidyutaśca mainākaḥ svarasastathā \|*  
*tuṅgaprastho nāgagirī rocanaḥ pāṇḍarācalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Mandara, the hill Durdura, Váta-svana, and Vaidyuta, Maináka, and Svarasa, Tunga-prastha, Nága-giri, Roc'ana, the

## \|\| 54.14 \|\|

*puṣpo girirdurjayanto raivator'buda eva ca \|*  
*ṛṣyamūkaḥ sagomantaḥ kūṭaśailaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śrīparvataścakoraśca śataśo 'nye ca parvatāḥ \|*

*taiḥ pīyante saritśreṣṭhā yāstāḥ samyaṅnibodha me \|*

*yamunā ca śatadruśca vitasterāvatī kuhuḥ \|*

*vipāśā devikā raṅkṣurniścīrā gaṇḍakī tathā \|*

*atharvāścārkaliṅgāśca malakāśca vṛkaiḥ saha \|*

## \|\| 54.36 \|\|

*aparāntāśca śūdrāśca pallavāścarmakhaṇḍikāḥ \|*

*śatadrujāḥ kaliṅgāśca pāradā hālamūṣikāḥ \|*

## \|\| 54.43 \|\|

*yathā pravaṅgā raṅgeyā mānadā mānavartikāḥ \|*

*pulindāśca sumīnāśca rūpapāḥ svāpadaiḥ saha \|*

*tośalāḥ kośalāścaiva traipurā vaidiśāstathā \|*

## \|\| 54.61 \|\|

## \|\| 54.63 \|\|

## \|\| 54.64 \|\|

## Chapter 55

## \|\| 55.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*bhagavan ! kathitaṃ samyak bhavatā bhārataṃ mama \|*  
*saritaḥ parvatā deśā ye ca tatra vasanti vai \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya continuing represents India as resting upon Vishnu in the form of a tortoise looking eastward, and distributes the various countries and peoples accordingly over the several parts of his body, together with the corresponding lunar constellations. He gives an astrological application to this arrangement and enjoins the performance of religious rites to avoid calamity. He also distributes the constellations of the Zodiac over the Tortoise's, body.

Kraushtuki spoke

1\. Adorable Sir! Thou hast duly declared Bhárata to me, its

## \|\| 55.2 \|\|

*kintu kūrmastvayā pūrvaṃ bhārate bhagavān hariḥ \|*  
*kathitastasya saṃsthānaṃ śrotumicchāmyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. rivers, mountains, countries, and the people who inhabit it. But thou didst previously make mention of the Tortoise, who is the adorable Vishnu, in Bhárata; I desire to hear fully about his position.

## \|\| 55.3 \|\|

*kathaṃ sa saṃsthito devaḥ kūrmarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*śubhāśubhaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vyajyate ca tataḥ katham \|*  
*yathāmukhaṃ yathāpādantasya tad brūhyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. What position does he, the god Janárdana, occupy in his form of the Tortoise? And how are weal and woe indicated thereby to mankind according to the position of his face and of his feet? Expound all that about him.

Márkandeya spoke

## \|\| 55.4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*prāṅmukho bhagavān ! devaḥ kūrmarūpī vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*ākramya bhārataṃ varṣaṃ navabhedamidaṃ dvija \|\| 4 \|\|*

## \|\| 55.5 \|\|

*viṣayāśca dvijaśreṣṭha ! ye samyak tānnibodha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

## \|\| 57.1 \|\|

Márkandeya briefly describes the continents, Kimpurusha Hari-varsha, Ilávrita, Ramyaka and Hiran-maya, and their inhabitants.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. I will tell thee, O bráhman, what the continent Kim-purusha is; where men with real bodies live ten thousand

## \|\| 57.3 \|\|

3\. it grows very high, it is like a grove. Those men are always drinking the juice of its fruit; and the women are born with lasting youthfulness and are fragrant as the lotus.

## \|\| 57.4 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ kiṃpuruṣāddharivarṣaṃ pracakṣyate \|*

5\. mankind are born of the appearance of gold; they all descend there from the world of the gods, and are shaped like the gods in all respects. In Hari-varsha all the men quaff

## Chapter 58

## \|\| 58.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*  
*kathitaṃ bhavatā samyag yat pṛṣṭo 'si mahāmune \|*  
*bhūsamudrādisaṃsthānaṃ pramāṇāni tathā grahāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya begins the relation of the Svároc'isha Manvantara -A young bráhman, by virtue of a magic ointment applied to his feet, visits the Himálaya mountains in half a day -The scenery there described - He wishes to return home, but the magic ointment has been dissolved by the snow, and he loses his way -The Apsaras Varúthiní meets him, and falling in love with him begs him for his love -He refuses all her entreaties, and at length appeals to the gárhapatya fire to help him homeward.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. Thou hast duly related what thou wast asked, O great muni, namely, the constitution of the earth, ocean, &c., their dimensions,

## \|\| 58.2 \|\|

*teṣāñcaiva pramāṇañca nakṣatrāṇāñca saṃsthitiḥ \|*  
*bhūrādayastathā lokāḥ pātālānyakhilānyapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. also the planets and their dimensions, and the constitution of the constellations, and the bhúr-loka and the other

## \|\| 58.3 \|\|

*svāyambhuvaṃ tathā khyātaṃ mune ! manvantaraṃ mama \|*  
*tadantarāṇyahaṃ śrotumicche manvantarāṇi vai \|*  
*manvantarādhipān devānṛṣīṃstattanayānnṛpān \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. worlds, and all the Lower Regions. And thou hast declared the Sváyambhuva Manvantara to me, O muni. Next I wish to hear about the Manvantaras which succeeded that, the deities who ruled over the Manvantaras, the rishis, and the kings who were their sons.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 58.4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*manvantaraṃ mayākhyātaṃ tava svāyambhuvaṃ ca yat \|*  
*svārociṣākhyamanyat tu śṛṇu tasmādanantaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I have made known to thee the Manvantara which is called Sváyambhuva. Now next to that hear about another which is named after Svárocisa.

## \|\| 58.5 \|\|

*kaścid dvijātipravaraḥ pure 'bhūdaruṇāspade \|*

*athāgato\|ñatithiḥ kaścit kadācittasya veśmani \|*

9\. skilled in the magic art. Now being requested by the former, whose mind was purified by faith, he described to him both

10\. countries and charming towns, forests, rivers, and mountains, and holy sanctuaries. Then the former filled with

The bráhman spoke:

Márkandeya spoke:

44\. with deference and spoke this word -"Who art thou, O maiden bright as the lotus-cup? Or on whom dost thou attend? I am a bráhman, I have come here from the city

## \|\| 58.51 \|\|

## \|\| 58.60 \|\|

## Chapter 63

## \|\| 63.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*

Sva-roc'is had three sons whom he settled in separate kingdoms, Vijaya in a city Vijaya in Káma-rúpa, Merunanda in Nanda-vatí in the North, and Prabháva in Tála in the South. -One day he met the goddess of a forest, and had by her a son Dyuti-mat Svároc'isha, who became a Manu. -Sva-roc'is, being again admonished by a conversation between two ducks, gives himself up to a religious life and dies.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Thus were those does discarded by the buck. Sva-rocis,

## Chapter 64

## \|\| 64.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tataḥ svārociṣaṃ nāmnā dyutimantaṃ prajāpatim \|*

Márkandeya mentions the gods, rishis and kings in the Svároc'isha Manvantara.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Then the adorable god made the Prajápati named Svárocisha Dyuti-mat a Manu. Listen to his Manvantara; who were

## \|\| 64.2 \|\|

*tatrāntare tu ye devā munayastatsutāśca ye \|*

2\. the gods during that period, who were the munis and their sons, who were the princes, listen while I tell of them, O Kraushtuki.

## \|\| 64.3 \|\|

*devāḥ pārāvatāstatra tathaiva tuṣitā dvija \|*  
*svārociṣe'ntare cendro vipaściditi viśrutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

## \|\| 64.4 \|\|

*ūrjastambastathā prāṇo datto'lirṛṣabhastathā \|*

4\. Indra was famed as Vipas-cit. Urja, Tamba and Prána, Dattoli and Rishabha, Niscara and Cárva-vírat were the seven

*caitrakiṃpuruṣādyāśca sutāstasya mahātmanaḥ \|*

5\. rishis in that period. And seven sons had that high souled Manu, C'aitra, Kim-purusha, &c., very valiant, guardians of

## \|\| 64.6 \|\|

*tasya manvantaraṃ yāvattāvattadvaṃśavistare \|*  
*bhukteyamavaniḥ sarvā dvitīyaṃ vai tadantaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. the earth. So long as his Manvantara lasted, all this earth was enjoyed among the outspreadings of his family. That was the second Manvantara.

## \|\| 64.7 \|\|

*svarociṣastu caritaṃ janma svārociṣasya ca \|*  
*niśamya mucyate pāpaiḥ śraddhadhāno hi mānavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Now the man who hears of Sva-rocis' deeds and Svárocisha's birth, and believes them, is delivered from his sins.

*krauṣṭukiruvāca*

King Uttama banished his queen to a forest because of her persistent unloving behaviour. -A bráhman whose wife had been carried off invokes the king's help to recover her. -The king in searching for her reaches a muni's hermitage, and is censured by the muni for his conduct to the queen.
