*dvāsthaināṃ duṣṭahṛdayāmādāya vijane vane \|*  
*parityajyāśu naitatte vicāryaṃ vacanaṃ mama \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. to her, he called the door-keeper and said, -"O door keeper! Take this lady of evil heart to a desolate forest and abandon her forthwith! Deliberate thou not on this my command!"

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 66.19 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato nṛpasya vacanamavicāryamavekṣya saḥ \|*  
*dvāḥsthastatyāja tāṃ subhrūmāropya syandane vane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thereupon the door-keeper, deeming the king's word was not to be questioned, mounted the beautiful-browed lady in a

## \|\| 66.20 \|\|

*sā ca taṃ vipine tyāgaṃ nītā tena mahībhṛtā \|*  
*apaśyamānā taṃ mene paraṃ kṛtamanugraham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. chariot and left her in a forest. And she, when abandoned thus by the king in the forest and being away from his sight,

## \|\| 66.21 \|\|

*so'pi tatrānurāgārtidahyamānātmamānasaḥ \|*  
*auttānapādirbhūpālo nānyāṃ bhāryāmavindata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. held he had done her the greatest favour. And king Auttána- pádi, with soul and mind burning with the anguish of love

## \|\| 66.22 \|\|

*sasmāra tāṃ sucārvaṅgīmaharniśamanirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*cakāra ca nijaṃ rājyaṃ prajādharmeṇa pālayan \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. for her, took no other wife. He remembered her who was beauteous in every limb, day and night bereft of ease, and ruled his kingdom, governing his people righteously.

## \|\| 66.23 \|\|

*prajāḥ pālayatastasya pituḥ putrānivaurasān \|*  
*āgatya brāhmaṇaḥ kaścididamāhārttamānasaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. While he ruled his people, as a father his own children, a certain bráhman suffering in mind arrived and spoke thus -

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 66.24 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca mahārāja bhṛśārtto'smi śrūyatāṃ gadato mama \|*  
*nṛṇāmārtiparitrāṇamanyato na narādhipāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Mahá-rája! in grievous suffering am I; hearken while I speak. Men's deliverance from pain comes from no where

## \|\| 66.25 \|\|

*mama bhāryā prasuptasya kenāpyapahṛtā niśi \|*  
*gṛhadvāramanuddhāṭya tāṃ samānetumarhasi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. but the king! Some one carried off my wife by night while I slept, without unlocking the house door. Deign to bring her back to me.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 66.26 \|\|

*rājovāca na vetsi kenāpahṛtā kva vā nītā tu sā dvija \|*  
*yatāmi vigrahe kasya kuto vāpyānayāmi tām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Knowest thou not, O bráhman, who carried her off or where has she been taken? With whom shall I strive in fight? or whence shall I bring her back?

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 66.27 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca tathaiva sthagite dvāri prasuptasya gṛhe mama \|*  
*hṛtā hi bhāryā kiṃ kenetyetadvijñāyate bhavān \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. While I slept just as I was, with the door fastened, O king, why and by whom my wife was carried off-this thou, Sir,

## \|\| 66.28 \|\|

*tvaṃ rakṣitā no nṛpate ṣaḍbhāgādānavetanaḥ \|*  
*dharmasya te'to niścintāḥ svapanti manujā niśi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. knowest. Thou art our guardian, O king, whose due is the levy of a sixth part of our wealth. Therefore men sleep at night, freed from anxiety about justice.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 66.29 \|\|

*rājovāca na te dṛṣṭā mayā bhāryā yādṛgrūpā ca dehataḥ \|*  
*vayaścaiva samākhyāhi kiṃśīlā brāhmaṇī ca te \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I have not seen thy Wife. Tell me what is she like in body, and what is her age; and of what disposition is the bráhman lady?

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 66.30 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca kaṭhoranetrā sātyuccā hrasvabāhuḥ kṛśānanā \|*  
*( lambodarīṃ hasvasphijaṃ tathā hrasvastanīṃ nṛpa) virūparūpā bhūpāla na nindāmi tathaiva tām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Sharp-eyed is she, very tall, short-armed, thin-faced, Ungainly in form, O king. I defame her not by this description;

## \|\| 66.31 \|\|

*vāci bhūpātiparuṣā na saumyā sā ca śīlataḥ \|*  
*ityākhyātā mayā bhāryā sā karālanirīkṣaṇā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. very harsh in speech, and ungentle is she in disposition, O king-thus I have described my wife; she is a do-nothing,

## \|\| 66.32 \|\|

*manāgatītaṃ bhūpāla tasyāśca prathamaṃ vayaḥ \|*  
*tādṛgrūpā hi me bhāryā satyametanmayoditam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. unpleasant in look, and she has slightly passed early womanhood, O king. Such is my wife in form; true is this I have spoken.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 66.33 \|\|

*rājovāca alaṃ te brāhmaṇa tayā bhāryāmanyāṃ dadāmi te \|*  
*sukhāya bhāryā kalyāṇī duḥkhaheturhi tādṛśī \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Enough hast thou had of her, O bráhman. I will give thee another wife. An excellent wife tends to one's happiness,

## \|\| 66.34 \|\|

*alpā kurūpatā vipra kāraṇaṃ śīlamuttamam \|*  
*rūpaśīlavihīnā yā tyājyā te'nyena sā hṛtā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. such a one as that is verily a source of pain. Bodily beauty consists in healthfulness, O bráhman, its cause is a noble disposition. She who has neither beauty nor good disposition should be abandoned for that very reason.

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 66.35 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca rakṣyā bhāryā mahīpāla iti ca śrutiruttamā \|*  
*bhāryāyāṃ rakṣyamāṇāyāṃ prajā bhavati rakṣitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. "A wife must be guarded," O king -such is our highest divine teaching.When a wife is guarded, the offspring is

## \|\| 66.36 \|\|

*ātmā hi jāyate tasya sā rakṣyāto nareśvara \|*  
*prajāyāṃ rakṣyamāṇāyāmātmā bhavati rakṣitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. guarded. For the Soul is born in her, hence she must be guarded, O king. When the offspring is guarded, the Soul is guarded.

## \|\| 66.37 \|\|

*tasyāmarakṣyamāṇāyāṃ bhavitā varṇasaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*sa pātayenmahīpāla pūrvānsvargādadhaḥ pitṝn \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When she is not guarded, there will arise confusion among the castes; that will hurl one's forefathers down from

## \|\| 66.38 \|\|

*anujñāya guruṃ rājandattvānyāṃ jātavedase \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Svarga, O king.And I may have loss of righteousness from day to-day, while I remain wifeless; and that, through the destruction of the perpetual ceremonies, will tend to my

## \|\| 66.39 \|\|

*samidhaṃ tu mayā bhāryā vṛteyaṃ karkaśā yataḥ \|*  
*kathametāṃ vihāyānyabhāryayā saha sañcare \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. downfall.And in her will be my offspring, O king. She will give thee the sixth part; she will be a cause of righteousness.

## \|\| 66.40 \|\|

*gṛhyadharmo yato brahma prāpyate śāśvataṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*pūrvoḍhayā tu dharmeṇa gṛhī kurvanna sīdati \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. For that reason I have declared this to thee. Bring back my wife who has been carried off, my lord, since your honour is placed supreme for our protection.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 66.41 \|\|

*tyaktvā tāṃ ca kriyāṃ kurvannaiva karmaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*agninā saha yā nūnaṃ sā jagāma gṛhaṃ śubhā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The king, on hearing him so speak, took thought, and mounted his great chariot which was furnished with every

## \|\| 66.42 \|\|

*dharmasya grahaṇe sā tu pūrvoḍhaiva praśasyate \|*  
*śaṭhāyācāraṇāttasyā jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. useful requisite. Hither and thither he wandered over the earth with that bráhman, and saw a fine hermitage of ascetics

## \|\| 66.43 \|\|

*dharmahāniścānudinamabhāryasya bhavenmama \|*  
*nityakriyāṇāṃ vibhraṃśātsa cāpi patanāya me \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. in a large forest; and alighting there he entered and saw a muni, seated on a silken cushion, and blazing as it were with

## \|\| 66.44 \|\|

*tasyāṃ ca pṛthivīpāla bhavitrī mama santatiḥ \|*  
*tava ṣaḍbhāgadātrī sā bhavitrī dharmahetukī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. splendour. Seeing the king arrived, he rose in haste, and welcoming him with full respect commanded his disciple to

## \|\| 66.45 \|\|

*tadetatte mayā khyātā patnī yā me hṛtā prabho \|*  
*tāṃ samānaya rakṣāyāṃ bhavānadhikṛto yataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. bring the arghya offering. His disciple said to him quietly " Why should the arghya be given to him, O muni? Think well of it and command me, for I carry out thy command."

## \|\| 66.46 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sa tasyaivaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā vimṛśya ca nareśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarvopakaraṇairyuktamāruroha mahāratham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then the bráhman being acquainted with the king's history, with self-possession did him respect in conversation and by giving him a seat.

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 66.47 \|\|

*itaścetaśca tenāsau paribabhrāma medinīm \|*  
*dadarśa ca mahāraṇye tāpasāśramamuttamam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Why hast thou come here, Sir; and what dost thou wish to do? I know thee, O king, to be Uttána-páda's son Uttama.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 66.48 \|\|

*avatīrya ca tatrāsau praviśya dadṛśe munim \|*  
*kauśyāṃ bṛṣyāṃ samāsīnaṃ jvalantamiva tejasā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. A bráhman's wife was carried off from his house by some one whose person is unknown, O muni: to seek her I have

## \|\| 66.49 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā nṛpatiṃ prāpya samutthāya tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*sammānya svāgatenaiva śiṣyamāhārghyamānaya \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. come here. Deign, adorable Sir, in compassion to tell me, who have reached thy house and am prostrate before thee, what I ask thee!

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 66.50 \|\|

*tamāha śiṣyaḥ śanakairdātavyo'rghyo'sya kiṃ mune \|*  
*tadājñāpaya sañcintya tavājñāṃ hi karomyaham \|\| 50 \|\|*

50.Ask me, O king, without fear what thou must ask. I will tell thee truthfully if I ought to tell it thee.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 66.51 \|\|

*tato'vagatavṛttānto bhūpatestasya sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*sambhāṣāsanadānena cakre sammānamātmavān \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Why is the arghya offering kept back, which thou wast prepared to give me on first seeing me on my arrival at thy house, O muni?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 66.52 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca kiṃ nimittamihāyāto bhavānkiṃ te cikirṣitam \|*  
*uttānapādatanayaṃ vedmi tvāmuttamaṃ nṛpa \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When through agitation at the sight of thee, O king, I commanded this disciple to give it, then I was cautioned by him.

## \|\| 66.53 \|\|

*rājovāca brāhmaṇasya gṛhādbhāryā kenāpyapahṛtā mune \|*  
*avijñātasyarūpeṇa tāmanveṣṭumihāgataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Through my favour he knows the future in this world, as

## \|\| 66.54 \|\|

*pṛcchāmi yatte tanme tvaṃ praṇatasyānukampayā \|*  
*abhyāgatasyātha gṛhaṃ bhagavanvaktumarhasi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I know both the past and the present thoroughly. When he said, "Consider and give thy order," then I also knew it; hence I did not give thee the arghya according to precept.

## \|\| 66.55 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*pṛccha māmavanīpāla yatpraṣṭavyamaśaṅikitaḥ \|*  
*vaktavyaṃ cettava mayā kathayiṣyāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Truly O king, thou art worthy of the arghya and thou belongest to the race of Sváyambhuva; nevertheless we deem thee Uttama not fit for the arghya.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 66.56 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*gṛhāgatāya yo mahyaṃ prathame darśane mune \|*  
*tvayā samudyato dātuṃ kathaṃ so'rghyo nivartitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. What then have I done, O bráhman, whether wittingly or unwittingly, that arriving after a long time I am not worthy of the arghya from thee?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 66.57 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*tvaddarśanena rabhasādajñapto'yaṃ mayā nṛpa \|*  
*yadā tadāhametena śiṣyeṇa pratibodhitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Hast thou forgotten, both that thou didst abandon thy wife in the forest, and that along with her thou didst abandon

## \|\| 66.58 \|\|

*eṣa vetti jagatyatra matprasādādanāgatam \|*  
*yathāhaṃ samatītañca vartamānañca sarvataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. all thy righteousness, O king. Through neglect of religious acts a man becomes unfit to be touched by his adherents, like one on whom ordure and urine have been showered; thou

## \|\| 66.59 \|\|

*ālocyājñāpayetyukte tato jñātaṃ mayāpi tat \|*  
*tato na dattavānarghamahaṃ tubhyaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. hast neglected an act of permanent observance. Just as a complaisant wife must bear with her husband though he be of

## \|\| 66.60 \|\|

*satyaṃ rājan ! tvamarghārhaḥ kule svāyambhuvasya ca \|*  
*tathāpi nārghayogyaṃ tvāṃ manyāmo vayamuttamam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. bad disposition, so a wife although of bad disposition must be cherished by her husband, O king. Ungracious indeed was that bráhman's wife who was carried off; nevertheless he, being a lover of righteousness, very much excels

## \|\| 66.61 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*kiṃ kṛtaṃ hi mayā brahman ! jñānādajñānato 'pi vā \|*  
*yena tvattor'ghamarhāmi nāhamabhyāgataścirāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. thee, O king. Thou establishest other men in their proper ways of righteousness when they swerve therefrom, O king. What other person will establish thee when thou swervest from thy righteousness?

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 66.62 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*kiṃ vismṛtante yatpatnī tvayā tyaktā ca kānane \|*  
*parityaktastayā sārdhaṃ tvayā dharmo nṛpākhilaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. A gazing-stock was the king when thus addressed by the wise rishi; and saying "So be it!" he enquired about the

## \|\| 66.63 \|\|

*pakṣeṇa karmaṇo hānyā prayātyasparśatāṃ naraḥ \|*  
*viṇmūtrairvārṣikī yasya hāniste nityakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. brahman's wife who had been carried off -"Adorable Sir, who has taken away the bráhman's wife, or where is she? Thou Sir knowest unerringly the past and the future in this world."

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 66.64 \|\|

*patnyānukūlayā bhāvyaṃ yathāśīle 'pi bhartari \|*  
*duḥ śīlāpi tathā bhāryā poṣaṇīyā nareśvara \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. A Rákshasa named Valáka, son of Adri, has captured her, and thou shall see her now in Utpalávataka forest, O king.

## \|\| 66.65 \|\|

*pratikūlā hi sā patnī tasya viprasya yā hṛtā \|*  
*tathāpi dharmakāmo 'sau tvāmudyotitavān nṛpa \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Go, unite the bráhman with his wife quickly. Let him not become a seat of sin as thou art day after day.

## Chapter 67

## \|\| 67.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*athāruroha svarathaṃ praṇipatya mahāmunim \|*  
*tenākhyātaṃ vanantacca prayayāvutpalāvatam \|\| 1 \|\|*

King Uttama finds the brahman's wife in the forest and is courteously received by the Rákshasa, who says he carried her off in order to impair the bráhman's religious merit. -At the king's request the Rákshasa consumes her evil disposition and restores her to her husband.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Then the king prostrated himself before the great muni, and mounted his chariot, and went to the forest Utpalávata

## \|\| 67.2 \|\|

*yathākhyātasvarūpāñca bhāryāṃ bhartrā dvijasya tām \|*  
*bhakṣayantīṃ dadārśātha śrīphalāni nareśvaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2.mentionedby him. Andtheking saw thebráhman's wife, in appearance such as her husband described her, eating the

## \|\| 67.3 \|\|

*papraccha ca kathaṃ bhadre ! tvametadvanamāgatā \|*  
*sphuṭaṃ bravīhi vaiśālerapi bhāryā suśarmaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. fruit of the bel tree; and asked -"How didst thou come to this forest, lady? tell me plainly; art thou the wife of Sus'arman Vaisáli?

The bráhman woman spoke:

## \|\| 67.4 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca*  
*sutāhamatirātrasya dvijasya vanavāsinaḥ \|*  
*patnī viśālaputrasya yasya nāma tvayoditam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I am daughter of the bráhman Ati-rátra, who dwells in the forest, and wife of Visála's son whose name thou hast uttered.

## \|\| 67.5 \|\|

*sāhaṃ hṛtā balākena rākṣasena durātmanā \|*  
*prasuptā bhavanasyānte bhrātṛmātṛviyojitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Being such, I was carried off by the evil-minded Rákshasa Valáka, while asleep at the extremity of my house, and parted

## \|\| 67.6 \|\|

*bhasmībhavatu tadrakṣo yenāsmyevaṃ viyojitā \|*  
*mātrā bhrātṛbhiranyaiśca tiṣṭāmyatra suduḥ khitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. from my brothers and mother. May that Rákshasa become ashes, by whom I have been parted thus from my mother, brothers and other relatives! Here I remain in great affliction.

## \|\| 67.7 \|\|

*asmin vane 'tigahane tenānīyāhamujjhitā \|*  
*na vedmi kāraṇaṃ ki tannopabhuṅkte na khādati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Bringing me to this very dense forest he has cast me off. I know not what is the reason he neither has intercourse with me nor devours me.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 67.8 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*api tajjñāyate rakṣastvāmutsṛjya kva vai gatam \|*  
*ahaṃ bhartrā tavaivātra preṣito dvijanandini \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Perchance thou knowest, where has the Rákshasa gone after leaving thee? I have been sent here by thy husband indeed, O bráhman lady.

The bráhman woman spoke:

## \|\| 67.9 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyuvāca*  
*asyaiva kānanasyānte sa tiṣṭhati niśācaraḥ \|*  
*praviśya paśyatu bhavān na bibheti tato yadi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The night-stalking demon stands at the edge of this very forest. Enter and see him, Sir, if thou dost not fear him.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 67.10 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*praviveśa tataḥ so 'tha tayā vartmani darśite \|*  
*dadṛśe parivāreṇa samavetañca rākṣasam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then he entered by the path that she showed, and saw the

## \|\| 67.11 \|\|

*dṛṣṭamātre tatastasmin tvaramāṇaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*dūrādeva mahīṃ mūrdhnā spṛśan pādāntikaṃ yayau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Rákshasa attended by his retinue. Then the Rákshasa hurrying, the moment he saw him, touching the earth with his head from afar indeed, approached his feet.

The Rákshasa spoke:

## \|\| 67.12 \|\|

*rākṣasa uvāca*  
*mamātrāgacchatā gehaṃ prasādaste mahān kṛtaḥ \|*  
*praśādhi kiṃ karomyeṣa vasāmi viṣaye tava \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thou hast done me great favour in that thou hast come to my abode here. Give me thy command.What shall I do,

## \|\| 67.13 \|\|

*arghañcemaṃ pratīccha tvaṃ sthīyatāñcedamāsanam \|*  
*vayaṃ bhṛtyā bhavān svāmī dṛḍhamājñāpayasva mām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. such as I am here? I dwell within thy country. Accept thou this arghya offering, and let this seat be placed for thee. We are servants, thou, Sir, art master; command me firmly.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 67.14 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*kṛtameva tvayā sarvaṃ sarvāmevātithikriyām \|*  
*kimarthaṃ brāhmaṇavadhūstvayānītā niśācara \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thou hast done everything, even every rite due to a guest. Why hast thou brought the bráhman's wife here, O night

## \|\| 67.15 \|\|

*neyaṃ surūpā santyanyā bhāryārthañced hṛtā tvayā \|*  
*bhakṣyārthaṃ cetkathaṃ nāttā tvayaitatkathyatāṃ mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. stalker? She is not comely; there are others comely, if thou didst carry her off for a wife: if to devour her, why hast thou not eaten her?Tell me this.

The Rákshasa spoke:

## \|\| 67.16 \|\|

*rākṣasa uvāca*  
*na vayaṃ mānuṣāhārā anye te nṛpa ! rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*sukṛtasya phalaṃ yattu tadaśnīmo vayaṃ nṛpa \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. We do not feed on men; such are other Rákshasas. But we eat the fruit that springs from a good deed, O king; and we

## \|\| 67.17 \|\|

*svabhāvañca manuṣyāṇāṃ yoṣitāñca vimānitāḥ \|*  
*mānitāśca samaśnīmo na vayaṃ jantukhādakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. consume the natural disposition of men and women, being treated with disrespect, and yet honoured; we are not eaters

## \|\| 67.18 \|\|

*yadasmābhirnṛṇāṃ kṣāntirbhuktā krudhyanti te tadā \|*  
*bhukte duṣṭe svabhāve ca guṇavanto bhavanti ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. of living creatures. When we have eaten the patience of men, they become enraged; and when we have eaten their

## \|\| 67.19 \|\|

*santi naḥ pramadā bhūpa ! rūpeṇāpsarasāṃ samāḥ \|*  
*rākṣasyastāsu tiṣṭhatsu mānuṣīṣu ratiḥ katham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. evil nature, they also become virtuous. We have Rákshasís who are fascinating, rivalling theApsarases in beauty, O king; while they are with us, how should we delight in the females of mankind?

The king spoke:

## \|\| 67.20 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*yadyeṣā nopabhogāya nāhārāya niśācara \|*  
*gṛhaṃ praviśya viprasya tatkimeṣā hṛtā tvayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If she is not for sensual enjoyment nor for food, O nightroamer, why then didst thou enter the bráhman's house and carry her off?

The Rákshasa spoke:

## \|\| 67.21 \|\|

*rākṣasa uvāca*  
*mantravit sa dvijaśreṣṭho yajñe yajñe gatasya me \|*  
*rakṣoghnamantrapaṭhanāt karotyuccāṭanaṃ nṛpa \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That excellent bráhman, learned in spells, keeps on expelling me, when I go to sacrifice after sacrifice, by uttering spells that

## \|\| 67.22 \|\|

*vayaṃ bubhukṣitāstasya mantroccāṭanakarmaṇā \|*  
*kva yāmaḥ sarvayajñeṣu sa ṛtvig bhavati dvijaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. destroy Rákshasas, O king. By reason of his spells and expulsive rites we were a-hungered; where shall we go? that

## \|\| 67.23 \|\|

*tato 'smābhiridantasya vaikalyamupapāditam \|*  
*patnyā vinā pumānijyākarmayogyo na jāyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. bráhman is the priest at every sacrifice. Therefore we inflicted this damage on him; without a wife a man becomes unfit to perform sacrifices.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 67.24 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*vaikalyoccāraṇāttasya brāhmaṇasya mahāmateḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sa rājātibhṛśaṃ viṣaṇṇaḥ samajāyata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At his announcement of the high-minded bráhman's impaired condition the king became exceedingly dejected then,

## \|\| 67.25 \|\|

*vaikalyamevaṃ viprasya vadanmāmeva nindati \|*  
*anarhamarghasya ca māṃ so 'pyāha munisattamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. thinking "While he speaks of the bráhman's impaired condition, it is me indeed he censures. That best of munis also

## \|\| 67.26 \|\|

*vaikalyaṃ tasya viprasya rākṣaso 'pyāha me yathā \|*  
*apatnīkatayā so 'haṃ saṅkaṭaṃ mahadāsthitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. said I was unworthy of the argha offering.As the Rákshasa also has spoken to me of that bráhman's impaired condition, I being in like plight am placed in a great strait, because I am wifeless."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 67.27 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*evaṃ cintayatastasya punarapyāha rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*praṇāmanamro rājānaṃ baddhāñjalipuṭo mune \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. While he thus thought, O muni, the Rákshasa spoke again to the king, bowing in obeisance and placing his hands

## \|\| 67.28 \|\|

*narendrājñāpradānena prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ mama \|*  
*bhṛtyasya praṇatasya tvaṃ yuṣmadviṣayavāsinaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. together respectfully -"O king, favour with thy command me, thy servant, prostrate before thee, a dweller within thy realm."

The king spoke:

## \|\| 67.29 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*svabhāvaṃ vayamaśnīmastvayoktaṃ yanniśācara \|*  
*tadarthino vayaṃ yena kāryeṇa śṛṇu tanmama \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Since thou hast said, O night-roamer -"We feed on a person's disposition," hear then from me what deed we solicit.

## \|\| 67.30 \|\|

*asyāstvayādya brāhmaṇyā dauḥ śīlyamupabhujyatām \|*  
*yena tvayāttadauḥ śīlyā tadvinītā bhavediyam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Do thou consume this bráhman woman's evil disposition this day; since she will have her evil disposition eaten by thee,

## \|\| 67.31 \|\|

*nīyatāṃ yasya bhāryeyaṃ tasya veśma niśācara \|*  
*asmin kṛte kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ gṛhamabhyāgatasya me \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. she may then become good in behaviour. Take her to his house whose wife she is, O night-roamer. When this is done, thou hast done all for me who am come as a guest to thy house.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 67.32 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tataḥ sa rākṣasastasyāḥ praviśyāntaḥ svamāyayā \|*  
*bhakṣayāmāsa dauḥ śīlyaṃ nijaśaktyā nṛpājñayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thereupon the Rákshasa, entering within her though his own faculty of illusion, devoured her evil disposition by his

## \|\| 67.33 \|\|

*dauḥ śīlyenātiraudreṇa patnī tasya dvijanmanaḥ \|*  
*tena sā saṃparityaktā tamāha jagatīpatim \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. own power at the king's command. Being rid entirely of that very violent evil disposition that bráhman's wife said

## \|\| 67.34 \|\|

*svakarmaphalapākena bhartustasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*viyojitāhaṃ taddheturayamāsīnniśācaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. to the king -"By the maturing of the fruit of my own actions I was separated from that magnanimous man, my husband; this night-roaming demon was the cause thereof.

## \|\| 67.35 \|\|

*nāsya doṣo na vā tasya mama bharturmahātmanaḥ \|*  
*mamaiva doṣo nānyasya sukṛtaṃ hyupabhujyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He is not in fault, nor that magnanimous man, my husband; mine in truth was the fault, no one else's. A good deed is

## \|\| 67.36 \|\|

*anyajanmani kasyāpi viprayogaḥ kṛto mayā \|*  
*so 'yaṃ mamāpyupagataḥ ko doṣo 'sya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. verily enjoyed. In some former life I separated myself from some husband; that same separation has been encountered again even by me. What fault is there in this magnanimous man?"

The Rákshasa spoke:

## \|\| 67.37 \|\|

*rākṣasa uvāca*  
*prāpayāmi tavādeśādimāṃ bhartṛgṛhaṃ prabho \|*  
*yadanyatkaraṇīyante tadājñāpaya pārthiva \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. I will cause her to reach her husband's house at thy command, my lord. Enjoin me whatever else should be done for thee, O king!

The king spoke:

## \|\| 67.38 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*asmin kṛte kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tvayā me rajanīcara \|*  
*āgantavyañca te vīra ! kāryakāle smṛtena me \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When this is done, thou hast done all for me, O nightroamer. And thou must come, O hero, at the time of action when I recall thee to mind.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 67.39 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*nathetyuktvā tu tadrakṣastāmādāya dvijāṅganām \|*  
*ninye bhartṛgṛhaṃ śuddhāṃ dauḥ śolyāpagamāttadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. "So be it!" then quoth the Rákshasa, and taking the bráhman woman conveyed her, purified then by the removal of her evil disposition, to her husband's house.

## Chapter 68

## \|\| 68.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tāṃ preṣayitvā rājāpi svabhartṛgṛhamaṅganām \|*  
*cintayāmāsa niḥ śvasya kimatra sukataṃ bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

King Uttama visits the rishi, learns his queen has been taken to Pátála by a Nága king, who then curses his daughter for hiding the queen from him -and he is also told his unhappy married life was caused by adverse planetary influence.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Now the king, after despatching the woman to her husband's house, sighed and thought, "What good deed may there be

## \|\| 68.2 \|\|

*anarghayogyatā kaṣṭaṃ sa māmāha mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*vaikalyaṃ vipramuddiśya tathāhāyaṃ niśācaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. in this? The high-minded muni declared I was wretched because of my unfitness for the arghya offering; and this night-roaming demon spoke of 'impaired condition' with

## \|\| 68.3 \|\|

*so 'haṃ kathaṃ kariṣyāmi tyaktā patnī mayā hi sā \|*  
*athavā jñānadṛṣṭiṃ taṃ pṛcchāmi munisattamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. reference to the bráhman. Being such, what shall I do, for I abandoned her, my wife? Or shall I enquire of that best of munis who has the eye of knowledge?"

## \|\| 68.4 \|\|

*sañcintyetthaṃ sa bhūpālaḥ samāruhya ca taṃ ratham \|*  
*yayau yatra sa dharmātmā trikālajño mahāminiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thus pondered the king, and mounting the chariot went where dwelt the great muni, righteous in soul, who knew the

## \|\| 68.5 \|\|

*avaruhya rathāt so 'tha taṃ sametya praṇamya ca \|*  
*yathāvṛttaṃ samācakhyau rākṣasena samāgamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. three periods of time. And descending from the chariot he approached and prostrated himself before that muni, and related how happened his meeting with the Rákshasa, and

## \|\| 68.6 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyā darśanañcaiva dauḥ śīlyāpagamaṃ tathā \|*  
*preṣaṇaṃ bhartṛgehe ca kāryamāgamane ca yat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. his interview with the bráhman woman, and the removal of her evil disposition, and her despatch to her husband's house, and what was his business in coming back.

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 68.7 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*jñātametanmayā pūrvaṃ yat kṛtante narādhipa \|*  
*kāryamāgamane caiva matsamīpe tavākhilam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I knew this before, which thou hast done, O king, and

## \|\| 68.8 \|\|

*pṛccha māmiha kiṃ kāryaṃ mayetyudvignamānasaḥ \|*  
*tvayyāgate mahīpāla ! śṛṇu kāryañca yattvayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. the whole of thy business in coming back to me. Ask me here "what must I do?" with anxious mind; and since

## \|\| 68.9 \|\|

*patnī dharmārthakāmānāṃ kāraṇaṃ prabalaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*viśeṣataśca dharmasya santyaktastyajatā hi tām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. thou art come, O king, hear what thou must do. A wife is a potent cause of righteousness, wealth and love among men; and in particular one who forsakes her has in sooth

## \|\| 68.10 \|\|

*apatnīko naro bhūpa ! na yogyo nijakarmaṇām \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vāpi vaiśyaḥ śūdro 'pi vā nṛpa \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. abandoned righteousness.Awifeless man, O king, is not fit for his own works, be he bráhman or kshatriya, vaisya or

## \|\| 68.11 \|\|

*tyajatā bhavatā patnīṃ na śobhanamanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*atyājyo hi yathā bhartā strīṇāṃ bharyā tathā nṛṇām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. even súdra, O king. No brilliant deed didst thou do, Sir, when thou didst abandon thy wife; for as women must not forsake a husband, so men must not forsake a wife.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 68.12 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*bhagavan ! kiṃ karomyeṣa vipāko mama karmaṇām \|*  
*nānukūlānukūlasya yasmāttyaktā tato mayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Adorable Sir, what shall I do, such as I am? It was the maturing of my actions, that I abandoned her because she was not favourably disposed to me while I was favourable

## \|\| 68.13 \|\|

*yadyatkaroti tat kṣāntaṃ dahyamānena cetasā \|*  
*bhagavaṃstadviyogārtibibhītenāntarātmanā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. to her. Whatever one does, that one endures with one's mind burning, even that with one's inmost soul terrified at the

## \|\| 68.14 \|\|

*sāmprataṃ tu vane tyaktā na vedmi kva nu sā gatā \|*  
*bhakṣitā vāpi vipine siṃhavyāghraniśācaraiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. pain of separation thereby, adorable Sir. But now I know not where she when abandoned in the forest has gone, or whether she has been devoured by lions, tigers and nightroaming beasts in the forest.

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 68.15 \|\|

*ṛṣīruvāca*  
*na bhakṣitā sā bhūpāla ! sihavyāghraniśācaraiḥ \|*  
*sā tvaviplutacāritrā sāmpratantu rasātale \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. She has not been devoured by lions or tigers or nightroaming beasts, O king, but she is now in Rasátala with unblemished character.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 68.16 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*sā nītā kena pātālamāste sādūṣitā katham \|*  
*atyadbhutamidaṃ brahman ! yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Who conveyed her to Pátála? How dwells she there uncorrupted? Most wonderful is this, O bráhman; deign to tell me of it as it happened.

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 68.17 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*pātāle nāgarājo 'sti prakhyātaśca kapotakaḥ \|*  
*tena dṛṣṭā tvayā tyaktā bhramamāṇā mahāvane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In Pátála is a Nága king and he is famed as Kapotaka. He saw her when abandoned by thee she was wandering

## \|\| 68.18 \|\|

*sā rūpaśālinī tena sānurāgeṇa pārthiva \|*  
*veditārthena pātālaṃ nītā sā yuvatī tadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. in the great forest. Enamoured of her then he declared his object and carried the beautiful young queen to Pátála, O

## \|\| 68.19 \|\|

*tatastasya sutā subhrūrnandā nāma mahīpate \|*  
*bhāryā manoramā cāsya nāgarājasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. king. Now that wise Nága king has a beautiful-browed

## \|\| 68.20 \|\|

*tayā mātuḥ sapatnīyaṃ sā bhavitrīti śobhanā \|*  
*dṛṣṭā svagehaṃ sā nītā guptā cāntaḥ pure śubhā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. daughter named Nandá, O king, and a charming wife. That daughter saw thy beautiful queen, and thinking, "this bright lady will become a rival wife to my mother," brought her to her own house and concealed her in the women's apartments.

## \|\| 68.21 \|\|

*yadā tu yācitā nandā na dadāti nṛpottaram \|*  
*mūkā bhaviṣyasītyāha tadā tāṃ tanayāṃ pitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. But Nandá, when entreated, continually refuses to answer the king; then the father cursed her his daughter that she should

## \|\| 68.22 \|\|

*evaṃ śaptā sutā tena sā cāste tatra bhūpate \|*  
*nītā tenoragendreṇa dhṛtā tatsutayā satī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. become dumb. Thus did he curse his daughter; and she, thy wife, remains there, O king, carried off by that Nága king, detained by his daughter, and still chaste.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 68.23 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tato rājā paraṃ harṣamavāpya tamapṛcchata \|*  
*dvijavaryaṃ svadaurbhāgyakāraṇaṃ dayitāṃ prati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Rejoicing greatly thereat, the king asked the eminent bráhman what was the reason of his ill-fortune with regard to his darling wife.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 68.24 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*bhagavan ! sarvalokasya mayi prītiranuttamā \|*  
*kinnu tatkāraṇaṃ yena svapatnī nātivatsalā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Adorable Sir! I meet with the utmost affection from all the world, what then is the reason, why my own wife is not very

## \|\| 68.25 \|\|

*mama cāsāvatīveṣṭā prāṇebhyo 'pi mahāmune \|*  
*sā ca māṃ prati duḥ śīlā brūhi yatkāraṇaṃ dvija \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. tender? On the one hand I dearly long for her even beyond my own life, O great muni, and on the other she is ill-disposed towards me. Say, what is the reason, O bráhman.

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 68.26 \|\|

*ṛṣīruvāca*  
*pāṇigrahaṇakāle tvaṃ sūryabhaumaśanaiścaraiḥ \|*  
*śukravācaspatibhyāñca tava bhāryāvalokitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When thou didst take her hand in marriage, the Sun and Mars and Saturn looked on thee, and Venus and Jupiter

## \|\| 68.27 \|\|

*tanmuhūrte 'bhavaccandrastasyāḥ somasutastathā \|*  
*parasparavipakṣau tau tataḥ pārthiva ! te bhṛśam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. looked on thy wife. At that moment the moon was favourable to thee, and Mercury to her. Those two groups of planets are mutually hostile; hence they have been

## \|\| 68.28 \|\|

*tadgaccha tvaṃ svadharmeṇa paripālaya medinīm \|*  
*patnīsahāyaḥ sarvāśca kuru dharmavatīḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. exceedingly adverse to thee, O king. Go then; attended by thy wife, rule the earth in thy righteousness, and perform every rite that pertains to righteousness!

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 68.29 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityukte praṇipatyainamāruhya syandanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*uttamaḥ pṛthivīpāla ājagāma nijaṃ puram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. At this exhortation king Uttama prostrated himself before the muni, and then mounting his chariot went to his own city.

## Chapter 69

## \|\| 69.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tataḥ svanagaraṃ prāpya taṃ dadarśa dvijaṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*sametaṃ bhāryayā caiva śīlavatyā mudānvitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The bráhman performs a sacrifice which turns the queen's heart to the king, and the Rákshasa brings her back from Pátála -The bráhman frees the Nága princess from the curse, and she coming to thank the king promises him a son who shall be a Manu -Accordingly a son is born who was the Manu Auttama.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Then arriving at his city, the king saw the joyful bráhman accompanied by his wife also who was sweet-dispositioned.

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 69.2 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*rājavarya ! kṛtārtho 'smi yato dharmo hi rakṣitaḥ \|*  
*dharmajñaneha bhavatā bhāryāmānayatā mama \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O noble king, successful am I inasmuch as righteousness has been preserved by thee, who art wise in righteousness here and who bringest back my wife.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 69.3 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*kṛtārthastvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha ! nijadharmānupālanāt \|*  
*vayaṃ saṅkaṭino vipra ! yeṣāṃ patnī na veśmani \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Successful art thou, O bráhman, because thou observest thy own laws of righteousness. I am in a strait, who have no wife at home, O bráhman.

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 69.4 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*narendra ! sā hi vipine bhakṣitā śvanāpadairyadi \|*  
*alantayā kimanyasyā na pāṇirgṛhyate tvayā \|*  
*krodhasya vaśamāgamya dharmo na rakṣitastvayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O king, if she, thy queen, has indeed been devoured by wild beasts in the forest, away with her! Why dost thou not take another's hand in marriage? Falling under the dominion of anger thou didst not preserve righteousness.

The king spoke:

## \|\| 69.5 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*na bhakṣitā me dayitā śvāpadaiḥ sā hi jīvati \|*  
*avidūṣitacāritrā kathametatkaromyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. My darling wife is not devoured by wild beasts; indeed she is alive, with character unblemished. How shall I act in this matter?

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 69.6 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*yadi jīvati te bhāryā na caiva vyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*tadapatnīkatājanma kiṃ pāpaṃ kriyate tvayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. If thy wife lives and has not gone astray, why then dost thou commit a sin which will render thee wifeless in another birth?

The king spoke:

## \|\| 69.7 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*ānītāpi hi sā vipra ! pratikūlā sadaiva me \|*  
*duḥ khāya na sukhāyālaṃ tasyā maitrī na vai mayi \|*  
*tathā tvaṃ kuru yatnaṃ me yathā sā vaśagāminī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In sooth, although she were brought back, she is ever opposed to me, O bráhman, she would tend to unhappiness, not to happiness; enough! her friendship is not at all towards me. Do thou so strive for me that she may become submissive unto me.

The bráhman spoke:

## \|\| 69.8 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*tava saṃprītaye tasyā vareṣṭirupakāriṇī \|*  
*kriyate mitrakāmairyā mitravindāṃ karomi tām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Vara sacrifice is beneficial for mutual affection between thee and her. I will perform the

## \|\| 69.9 \|\|

*aprītayoḥ prītikaro sā hi saṃjananī param \|*  
*bhāryāpatyormanuṣyendra ! tāntaveṣṭiṃ karomyaham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Mitra-vindá sacrifice which those perform who wish for friends; for it produces affection between two persons who love not each other; it creates the warmest affection between wife and husband, O king. I will perform that sacrifice for thee.

## \|\| 69.10 \|\|

*yatra tiṣṭhati sā subhrūstava bhāryā mahīpate \|*  
*tasmādānoyatāṃ sā te parāṃ prītimupaiṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Fetch thy beautiful-browed wife from wherever she is now, O king; she shall feel the warmest love for thee!

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 69.11 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tu sambhārānaśeṣānavanīpatiḥ \|*  
*ānināya cakāreṣṭiṃ sa ca tāṃ dvijasattamaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus admonished, the king then collected all the materials

## \|\| 69.12 \|\|

*saptakṛtvaḥ sa tu tadā cakāreṣṭiṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tasya rājño dvijaśreṣṭho bhāryāsampādanāya vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. requisite, and the bráhman performed that sacrifice. Seven times then the bráhman performed the sacrifice in repetition

## \|\| 69.13 \|\|

*yadāropitamaitrīntāmamanyata mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*svabhartari tadā viprastamuvāca narādhipam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. in order to procure for the king his wife. When the great muni deemed that he had aroused friendliness within her towards her husband, then he, the bráhman, addressed the

## \|\| 69.14 \|\|

*ānīyatāṃ naraśreṣṭha ! yā taveṣṭātmano 'ntikam \|*  
*bhuṅkṣva bhogāṃstayā sārdhaṃ yaja yajñāṃstathādṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. king -"Fetch her, O king, who is dear to thee, close to thy soul; enjoy all enjoyments with her, and offer sacrifices, being duly respected."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 69.15 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityuktastena vipreṇa bhūpālo vismitastadā \|*  
*sasmāra taṃ mahāvīryaṃ satyasandhaṃ niśācaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus exhorted by the bráhman the king a-wondering then recalled to mind the very valiant, truthful, night-roaming

## \|\| 69.16 \|\|

*smṛtastena tadā sadyaḥ samupetya narādhipam \|*  
*kiṃ karomīti so 'pyāha praṇipatya mahāmune \|\| 16 \|\|*

## Chapter 71

## \|\| 71.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*

King Sva-ráshtra being driven from his kingdom by enemies became an ascetic, and met his deceased queen in the shape of a doe during a great flood. -He begot a son by her who became the Manu Támasa. - The gods, rishis and kings of that manvantara are named.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. There lived on the earth a famous king, by name Sva-ráshtra, valiant, an offerer of many sacrifices, wise, invincible

The rishi Rita-vác' had a son who was bad because born under the constellation Revatí, and the rishi made the constellation fall with his curse. -A daughter was born therefrom whom the rishi Pramuca adopted and named Revatí. -King Durgama visited Pramuca and married Revatí, and the constellation was restored to its place at the marriage. -They had a son, the Manu Raivata. -The gods, rishis and kings in his period are named.

## \|\| 72.35 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*agnisālāṃ gato viprastacchrutvā tasya bhāṣitam \|*  
*priyetyāmantraṇañcaiva niścakrāma tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The bráhman, who was in the room where the sacred fire burned, heard that his speech and the hailing her as "Dear!"

## \|\| 72.36 \|\|

*sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ rājānaṃ durgamaṃ muniḥ \|*  
*narendracihnasahitaṃ praśrayāvanataṃ puraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. and came out in haste. The muni saw high-souled king Durgama, bearing the royal insignia, bowing respectfully before him.

## \|\| 72.37 \|\|

*tasmin dṛṣṭe tataḥ śiṣyamuvāca sa tu gautamam \|*

37\. Now on seeing him he spoke at once to his disciple Gautama -"Gautama! bring quickly the argha offering for this king.

## \|\| 72.38 \|\|

*ekastāvadayaṃ bhūpaścirakālādupāgataḥ.*  
*jāmātā ca viśeṣeṇa yogyor'ghasya mato mama \|\| 38 \|\|*

38.At length he has come alone after a long time, this king and in particular my son-in-law; I deem him worthy of the argha."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 72.39 \|\|

40\. silence the king accepted the argha. When the king bad taken a seat and accepted the argha, the bráhman, the great

## \|\| 72.41 \|\|

*koṣe bale 'tha mitreṣu bhṛtyāmātye nareśvara \|*

41\. muni, addressed him a welcome -"I trust thou rarest well in thy home, in thy treasury, and army, in thy friends, in thy servants and ministers, and in thy own self whereon

## \|\| 72.42 \|\|

*patnī ca te kuśalinī yata evānutiṣṭhati \|*  
*pṛcchāmyasyāstato nāhaṃ kuśalinyo 'parāstava \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. rests every thing, O king of mighty arm!And thy wife fares well; since she is indeed at hand, I ask not therefore about her, but I hope thy other wives fare well!"

The king spoke:

## \|\| 72.43 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*tvatprasādādakuśalaṃ na kvacinmama suvrata \|*

43\. Through thy favour I have no ill-fortune any where, O strict observer of vows; and my curiosity is aroused, what wife have I here, O muni?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.44 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*revatī sumahābhāgā trailokyasyāpi sundarī \|*  
*tava bharyā varārohā tāṃ tvaṃ rājanna vetsi kim \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Most noble Revatí, beautiful even through the three worlds, is thy wife of exquisite figure; dost thou not know her, O king?

The king spoke:

## \|\| 72.45 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*subhadrāṃ śāntatanayāṃ kāverītanayāṃ vibho \|*  
*surāṣṭrajāṃ sujātāñca kadambāñca varūthajām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. My lord! Su-bhadrá, S'ánta's daughter, Káverí's daughter, and Su-játá born in Su-ráshtra, and Varútha's daughter

## \|\| 72.46 \|\|

*vipāṭhāṃ nandinīñcaiva vedmi bhāryāṃ gṛhe dvija \|*  
*tiṣṭhanti me na bhagavan revatīṃ vedmi kānviyam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Kadambá, Vipáthá, and Nandiní -these I know as my wives, O bráhman; they remain at my home. I know not Revati, adorable Sir; who then is she?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.47 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*priyeti sāmprataṃ yeyaṃ tvayoktā varavarṇinī \|*

47\. She is this maiden of beautiful complexion, whom thou didst address just now as "Dear!" Hast thou forgotten, O king? Worthy of praise is this lady of thy house!

The king spoke:

## \|\| 72.48 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*satyamuktaṃ mayā kintu bhāvo duṣṭo na me mune \|*  
*nātra kopaṃ bhavān kartumarhatyasmāsu yācitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In truth I said so, but no improper feeling had I, O muni. Deign not to be angry with me for this, I beseech thee, Sir!

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.49 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*tattvaṃ bravīṣi bhūpāla ! na bhāvastava dūṣitaḥ \|*  
*vyājahāra bhavānetadvahninā nṛpa coditaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thou speakest truly, O king; no improper feeling hadst thou.Thou didst utter this word, being impelled byAgni,

## \|\| 72.50 \|\|

*mayā pṛṣṭo hutavahaḥ ko 'syā bharteti pārthiva \|*  
*bhavitā tena cāpyukto bhavānevādya vai varaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O king. I askedAgni, "Who shall be her husband?" O king; and he replied that thou thyself, Sir, shouldst verily

## \|\| 72.51 \|\|

*tadgṛhyatāṃ mayā dattā tubhyaṃ kanyā narādhipa \|*  
*priyetyāmantritā ceyaṃ vicāraṃ kuruṣe katham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. be her bridegroom this day. Take her then; I give thee the maiden, O king, and thou didst hail her as "Dear!" How dost thou decide?

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 72.52 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tato 'sāvabhavanmaunī tenoktaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*ṛṣistathodyataḥ kartuṃ tasyā vaivāhikaṃ vidhim \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. At his address the king then kept silence; and the rishi

## \|\| 72.53 \|\|

*tamudyataṃ sā pitaraṃ vivāhāya mahāmune \|*  
*uvāca kanyā yatkiñcit praśrayāvanatānanā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. prepared to perform her wedding ceremony. The maiden spoke a little thing to her father who was prepared for the marriage, her countenance bent downward with respect -

## \|\| 72.54 \|\|

*yadi me prītimāṃstāta prisādaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*revatyṛkṣe vivāhaṃ me tatkarotu prasāditaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. "If thou lovest me, dear father, deign to give me a favour; perform then my marriage in the constellation Revati, since I have won thy favour."

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.55 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*revatyṛkṣaṃ na vai bhadre candrayogi vyavasthitam \|*  
*anyāni santi ṛkṣāṇi subhru vaivāhikāni te \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Fair maiden! the constellation Revatí is not declared to be one that unites with the moon. The constellations appropriate to thy marriage are others, O beautiful-browed!

The maiden spoke:

## \|\| 72.56 \|\|

*kanyovāca*  
*tāta tena vinā kālo viphalaḥ pratibhāti me \|*  
*vivāho viphale kāle madvidhāyāḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Dear father! without that constellation the time appears to me unprofitable. How may the marriage of such as me take place at an unprofitable time?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.57 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*ṛtavāgiti vikhyātastapasvī revatīṃ prati \|*  
*cakāra kopaṃ kruddhena tenarkṣaṃ vinipātitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The famous ascetic named Rita-vác was enraged against Revati; in his anger he caused the constellation to fall down.

## \|\| 72.58 \|\|

*mayā cāsmai pratijñātā bharyeti madirekṣaṇā \|*

58\. And I have promised thee as wife to this king, O maiden with intoxicating eyes; and if thou desirest not the marriage, we have fallen into a strait!

The maiden spoke:

## \|\| 72.59 \|\|

*kanyovāca*  
*ṛtavāk sa munistāta kimevaṃ taptavāṃstapaḥ \|*  
*na tvayā mama tātena brahmabandhoḥ sutāsmi kim \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Dear father! Why did that muni Rita-vác perform austerities in that fashion? Have I nought to do with thee as father?Am I the daughter of an unworthy bráhman?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.60 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*brahmabandhoḥ sutā na tvaṃ bāle naiva tapasvinaḥ \|*

60\. Thou art not the daughter of an unworthy bráhman, nor of an ascetic, O maiden. Thou art daughter to me who am striving to make other gods.

The maiden spoke:

## \|\| 72.61 \|\|

*kanyovāca*  
*tapasvī yadi me tātastatkimṛkṣamidaṃ divi \|*  
*samāropya vivāho me tadṛkṣe kriyate na tu \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. If my father is a practiser of austerities, why then does he not raise this constellation to the sky and perform my wedding under the constellation?

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.62 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*evaṃ bhavatu bhadrante bhadre prītimatī bhava \|*  
*āropayāmīndumārge revatyṛkṣaṃ kṛte tava \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Be it so! prosperity be thine, fair maiden; be thou affectionate! I raise the constellation Revati to the moon's pathway for thy sake.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 72.63 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tatastapaḥ prabhāveṇa revatyṛkṣaṃ mahāmuniḥ \|*

63\. Then by the power of his austerities the great muni placed the constellation Revati as before in conjunction with the

## \|\| 72.64 \|\|

*vivāhañcaiva duhiturvidhivad mantrayoginam \|*  
*niṣpādya prītimān bhūyo jāmātāramathābravīt \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. moon, O bráhman. And full of affection he celebrated his daughter's marriage accompanied with sacred texts according

## \|\| 72.65 \|\|

*audvāhikante bhūpāla kathyatāṃ kiṃ dadāmyaham \|*  
*durlabhyamapi dāsyāmi mamāpratihatantapaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. to rule, and said to his son-in-law again, "Tell me, O king, what shall I give thee as a wedding gift? I will give even that which is hard to be obtained, for irresistible are my austerities."

The king spoke:

## \|\| 72.66 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*manoḥ svayambhuvasyāhamutpannaḥ santatau mune \|*

66\. Of Manu Sváyambhuva's lineage I am sprung, O muni. I choose as gift a son who shall reign over a manvantara through thy favour.

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 72.67 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*bhaviṣyatyeṣa te kāmo manustvattanayo mahīm \|*  
*sakalāṃ bhokṣyate bhūpa dharmavicca bhaviṣyati \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. This thy wish shall be fulfilled. As a Manu thy son shall enjoy the whole earth, and shall be wise in righteousness, O king.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 72.68 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tāmādāya tato bhūpaḥ svameva nagaraṃ yayau \|*  
*tasmādajāyata suto revatyā raivato manuḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Then taking her the king went to his own city. From him

## \|\| 72.69 \|\|

*sametaḥ sakalairdharmairmānavairaparājitaḥ \|*  
*vijñātākhilaśāstrārtho vedavidyārthaśāstravit \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. was born of Revatí a son, the Manu Raivata, possessed of all righteousness, unconquered by mankind, who understood the meaning of every sacred book, who knew the Vedas, the sciences and the books of practical arts.

## \|\| 72.70 \|\|

*tasya manvantare devān munidevendrapārthivān \|*  
*kathyamānān mayā brahman nibodha susamāhitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Hear most composedly, O bráhman, about the gods, the munis, the lord of the gods and the kings in his manvantara, as

## \|\| 72.71 \|\|

*sumedhasastatra devāstathā bhūpatayo dvija \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhaścāmitābhaśca caturdaśa caturdaśa \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I mention them. The gods therein were the Su-medhases. And the kings wereVaikuntha and Amitábha, fourteen and

## \|\| 72.72 \|\|

*teṣāṃ devagaṇānāntu caturṇāmapi ceścaraḥ \|*  
*nāmnā vibhurabhūdindraḥ śatayajñopalakṣakaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. fourteen, O bráhman. And now the lord of those very four clashes of gods was namedVibhu, who was the regarder of a

## \|\| 72.73 \|\|

*hiraṇyalomā vedaśrīrūrdhvabāhustathāparaḥ \|*  
*vedabāhuḥ sudhāmā ca parjanyaśca mahāmuniḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. hundred sacrifices, O king. Hiranya-loman, Veda-srí, and also Urddhva-bábu,Veda-báhu, and Su-dháman and the great

## \|\| 72.74 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhaśca mahābhāgo vedavedāntapāragaḥ \|*  
*ete saptarṣayaścāsan raivatasyāntare manoḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. muni Parjanya, and illustrious Vasishtha who was thoroughly versed in theVedas andVedánta - these were the

## \|\| 72.75 \|\|

*balabandhurmahāvīryaḥ suyaṣṭavyastathāparaḥ \|*  
*satyakādyāstathaivāsan raivatasya manoḥ sutāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. seven rishis also in Manu Raivata's period. Bala-handhu mighty in valour, and also Su-yashtavya, and Satyaka and others were Manu Raivata's sons.

## \|\| 72.76 \|\|

*raivatāntāstu manavaḥ kathitā ye mayā tava \|*  
*svāyambhuvāśrayā hyete svārociṣamṛte manum \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Now these are the Manus down to Raivata, whom I have told thee about; they were indeed connected with Sváyambhuva, except Manu Svároc’isha.

## Chapter 73

## \|\| 73.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityetat kathitaṃ tubhyaṃ pañca manvantaraṃ tava \|*  
*cākṣuṣasya manoḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ śrūyatāmidamantaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

C'ákshusha when an infant was taken by a hag from his parents and changed for the son of king Vi-kránta, and was brought up as a prince. -On reaching boyhood he revealed the fraud, and abandoning his princely state became an ascetic. -Brahmá made him the sixth Manu. -The deities, rishis and kings of his period are mentioned.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Thus I have narrated these five manvantaras to thee. Hear about this sixth period, that of the Manu C’ákshusha.

## \|\| 73.2 \|\|

*anyajanmani jāto 'sau cakṣuṣaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*cākṣuṣatvamatastasya janmanyasminnapi dvija \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In another birth he was born from the eye of the supreme deity, hence in this birth also he retained the condition of

## \|\| 73.3 \|\|

*jātaṃ mātā nijotsaṅge sthitamullāpya taṃ punaḥ \|*  
*pariṣvajati hārdena punarullāpayatyatha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. C'ákshusha, O bráhman. His mother repeatedly makes him prattle as he lies in her lap after his birth, and embraces

## \|\| 73.4 \|\|

*jātismaraḥ sa jāto vai māturutsaṅgamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*jahāsa taṃ tadā mātā saṃkruddhā vākyamabravīt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. him lovingly and then again makes him prattle. Being indeed born with a recollection of his previous existences, he

## \|\| 73.5 \|\|

*bhītāsmi kimidaṃ vatsa ! hāso yadvadane tava \|*  
*akālabodhaḥ sañjātaḥ kaccit paśyasi śobhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. laughed as he lay on his mother's lap. His mother said to him angrily then -"I am frightened; what is this, my child, that there is laughter in thy mouth? Thou art born with premature intelligence. Perhaps thou seest something bright!"

The son spoke:

## \|\| 73.6 \|\|

*putra uvāca*  
*māmattumicchati puro mārjārī kima na paśyasi \|*  
*antardhānagatā ceyaṃ dvitīyā jātahāriṇī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Dost thou not see, a cat in front wishes to devour me? And another, the hag who seizes newly-born children, has

## \|\| 73.7 \|\|

*putraprītyā ca bhavatī sahārdā māmavekṣatī \|*  
*ullāpyollāpya bahuśaḥ pariṣvajati māṃ yataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. vanished. And since thou, lady, looking on me lovingly in thy affection for thy son, dost keep on making me prattle and

## \|\| 73.8 \|\|

*udbhūtapulakā snehasambhavāstrāvilekṣaṇā \|*  
*tato mamāgato hāsaḥ śṛṇu cāpyatra kāraṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. dost embrace me much, while thy hair rises up and thine eyes are suffused with tears springing from love, therefore

## \|\| 73.9 \|\|

*svārthe prasaktā mārjārī prasaktaṃ māmavekṣate \|*  
*tathāntardhānagā caiva dvitīyā jātahāriṇī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I chanced to laugh. Hear also the reason of it. The cat intent on its own object looks on me who am attached to thee; and the other also, the hag who seizes newly-born

## \|\| 73.10 \|\|

*svārthāya snigdhahṛdayā yathaivaite mamopari \|*  
*pravṛtte svārthamāsthāya tathaiva pratibhāsi me \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. children, has vanished. Just as these two, with hearts solicitous for their own self-interest, were busy over me, even so thou appearest to me to be engaged in thy own self-interest.

## \|\| 73.11 \|\|

*kintu madupabhogāya mārjārī jātahāriṇī \|*  
*tvantu krameṇopabhogyaṃ mattaḥ phalamabhīpsasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. But the cat and the hag who seizes newly-born children aimed at enjoying me; thou on the other hand desirest to obtain good results from me which shall be enjoyed

## \|\| 73.12 \|\|

*na māṃ jānāsi ko 'pyeṣa na caivāpakṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*saṅgataṃ nātikālīnaṃ pañcasaptadinātmakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. gradually. Thou dost not know me who I am, nor the benefit that I have conferred. Our meeting is for no very long time,

## \|\| 73.13 \|\|

*tathāpi strihyase sāstrā pariṣvajasi cāpyati \|*  
*tāteti vatsa ! bhadreti nirvyalīkaṃ bravīṣi mām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. a period of five and seven days. Nevertheless thou lovest and embracest me excessively with tears in thine eyes; sincerely thou callest me "dear child" and "lovely darling."

The mother spoke:

## \|\| 73.14 \|\|

*mātovāca*  
*na tvāhamupakārārthaṃ vatsa ! prītyā pariṣvaje \|*  
*na cedetadbhavatprītyai parityaktāsmyahaṃ tvayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. "It is not for the sake of a benefit that I embrace thee lovingly, my darling, nor shall I be deprived of thee, if this

## \|\| 73.15 \|\|

*svārtho mayā parityakto yastvatto me bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ityuktvā sā tamutsṛjya niṣkrāntā sūtikāgṛhāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. shall be for thy pleasure. I have now relinquished any selfinterest which shall accrue to me from thee."

## \|\| 73.16 \|\|

*jaḍāṅgabāhyakaraṇaṃ śuddhāntaḥ karaṇātmakam \|*  
*jahāra taṃ parityaktaṃ sā tadā jātahāriṇī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. So saying she left him and went out of the lying-in house. The hag Játa-háriní then seized him when left, his body and external organs of sense being apathetic, his heart and soul

## \|\| 73.17 \|\|

*sā hṛtvā taṃ tadā bālaṃ vikrāntasya mahībhṛtaḥ \|*  
*prasūtapatnīśayane nyasya tasyādade sutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. pure. Having seized the boy she placed him then as a newborn child on the bed of king Vi-kránta's wife, and took his

## \|\| 73.18 \|\|

*tamapyanyagṛhe nītvā gṛhītvā tasya cātmajam \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ bhakṣayāmāsa sā kramājjātahāriṇī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. new-born son and carried him to another house, and taking a son from that house she, Játa-háriní, in regular course

## \|\| 73.19 \|\|

*hṛtvā hṛtvā tṛtīyantu bhakṣayatyatinirghṛṇā \|*  
*karotyanudinaṃ sā nu parivartantathānyayoḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. devoured this third child. Now carrying children off in succession she devours the third child, totally devoid of pity; but she makes a substitution thus with the other two day after day.

## \|\| 73.20 \|\|

*vikrānto 'pi tatastasya sutasyaiva mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*kārayāmāsa saṃskārān rājanyasya bhavanti ye \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. And then king Vi-kránta performed the purificatory rites,

## \|\| 73.21 \|\|

*ānandeti ca nāmāsya pitā cakre vidhānataḥ \|*  
*mudā paramayā yukto vikrāntaḥ sa narādhipaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. which appertain to a prince, for that very son; and as father kingVi-kránta gave him the nameAnanda according to rule,

## \|\| 73.22 \|\|

*kṛtopanayanaṃ tantu gururāha kumārakam \|*  
*jananyāḥ prāgupasthānaṃ kriyatāñcābhivādanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. being himself filled with intense joy. Now when as a youth he had donned the sacred thread, his spiritual guide ordered him - "Approach before thy mother respectfully and salute

## \|\| 73.23 \|\|

*sa gurostadvacaḥ śrutvā vihasyaivamathābravīt \|*  
*vandyā me katamā mātā jananī pālanī nu kim \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. her!" Hearing that his guru's speech, he smiled and spoke thus -"Which of my mothers shall I praise, her who gave me birth or her who has nourished me?"

The guru spoke:

## \|\| 73.24 \|\|

*gururuvāca*  
*na tviyaṃ te mahābhāga ! janayitrī ruthātmajā \|*  
*vikrāntasyāgramahiṣī haiminī nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Not the latter, indeed! Thy mother who bore thee, noble youth, is Rutha's daughter, Vi-kránta's chief queen, Haiminí by name.

Ananda spoke:

## \|\| 73.25 \|\|

*ānanda uvāca*  
*iyaṃ janitrī caitrasya viśālagramavāsinaḥ \|*  
*viprāgryabodhaputrasya yo 'syāṃ jāto 'nyato vacam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. She is the mother of C'aitra, who dwells in the village Visála, as son of the leading bráhman Bodha, and who was born of her. I come from elsewhere.

The guru spoke:

## \|\| 73.26 \|\|

*gururuvāca*  
*kutastvaṃ kathayānanda ! caitraḥ ko vā tvayocyate \|*  
*saṅkaṭaṃ mahadābhāti kva jāto 'tra bravīṣi kim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Whence art thou? tell me, O Ananda. What C'aitra again dost thou mention? It appears to be a great difficulty. Where wast thou born?What dost thou say of this?

Ananda spoke:

## \|\| 73.27 \|\|

*ānanda uvāca*  
*jāto 'hamavanīndrasya kṣatriyasya gṛhe dvija \|*  
*tatpatnyāṃ giribhadrāyāmādade jātahāriṇī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I was born in a kshatriya king's house of his wife Giribhadrá, O bráhman. The hag that steals new-born children

## \|\| 73.28 \|\|

*tayātra mukto haiminyā gṛhītvā ca sutañca sā \|*  
*bodhasya dvijamukhyasya gṛhe nītavatī punaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. took me; she left me here, and taking Haimini's son also carried him further to the house of the leading bráhman

## \|\| 73.29 \|\|

*bhakṣayāmāsa ca sutaṃ tasya bodhadvijanmanaḥ \|*  
*sa tatra dvijasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛto haiminīsutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Bodha, and devoured the bráhman Bodha's son. Haimini's son has been consecrated with the sanctifying rites of a bráhman

## \|\| 73.30 \|\|

*vayamatra mahābhāga ! saṃskṛtā guruṇā tvayā \|*  
*mayā tava vacaḥ kāryamupaimi katamāṃ guro \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. there. I have been consecrated here by thee as guru, illustrious Sir. I must obey thy command: which mother shall I approach, O guru?

The guru spoke:

## \|\| 73.31 \|\|

*gururuvāca*  
*atīva gahanaṃ vatsa ! saṅkaṭaṃ mahadāgatam \|*  
*na vedmi kiñcinmohena bhramantīva hi buddhayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Extremely intricate, my child, is this great difficulty that has befallen. I understand it not at all, for my wits are wandering as it were through enchantment.

Ananda spoke:

## \|\| 73.32 \|\|

*ānanda uvāca*  
*mohasyāvasaraḥ ko 'tra jagatyevaṃ vyavasthite \|*  
*kaḥ kasya putro viprarṣe ! ko vā kasya nu bāndhavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. What case of enchantment is there here, while the world is thus constituted?Who is whose son, O bráhman rishi?

## \|\| 73.33 \|\|

*ārabhya janmano nṝṇāṃ sambandhitvamupaiti yaḥ \|*  
*anye sambandhino vipra ! mṛtyunā sannivartitāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Or who is not whose kinsman? Beginning from his birth, whatever man enters into connexions, the others who are connected with him are made to pass away by death, O

## \|\| 73.34 \|\|

*atrāpi jātasya sataḥ sambandhoyo 'sya bāndhavaiḥ \|*  
*so 'pyastaṅgate dehe prayātyeṣo 'khilakramaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. bráhman. Moreover when he is born here, whatever connexion he has with kinsmen, that also ceases with the ending

## \|\| 73.35 \|\|

*ato bravīmi saṃsāre vasataḥ ko na bāndhavaḥ \|*  
*ko vāpi satataṃ bandhuḥ kiṃ vo vibhrāmyate matiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. of his body. This is the entire process. Hence I say, "Who is not a kinsman to one who dwells in this worldly existence? Or who is a kinsman for ever?" Is thy mind

## \|\| 73.36 \|\|

*pitṛdvayaṃ mayā prāptamasminneva hi janmani \|*  
*mātṛdvayañca kiñcitraṃ yadanyad dehasambhave \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. bewildered? I have had two fathers indeed in this very birth, and two mothers; is it wonderful that it should be

## \|\| 73.37 \|\|

*so 'haṃ tapaḥ kariṣyāmi tvayā yo hyasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*viśālagrāmataḥ putraścaitra ānīyatāmiha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. otherwise in the recurring birth of the body? Being such, I will practise austerities. Do thou bring here C'aitra, who is indeed the son of this king, from the villageVisála.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 73.38 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tataḥ sa vismito rājā sabhāryaḥ saha bandhubhiḥ \|*  
*tasmānnivartya mamatāmanumene vanāya tam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thereupon the king was astonished with his wives and kinsmen; withdrawing his feeling of ownership from that

## \|\| 73.39 \|\|

*caitramānīya tanayaṃ rājyayogyaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*saṃmānya brāhmaṇaṃ yena putrabuddhyā sa pālitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. boy, he permitted him to depart to the forest. Fetching his son C'aitra he made him worthy of the kingdom, after honouring the bráhman who brought him up in the belief that he was his son.

## \|\| 73.40 \|\|

*so 'pyānandastapastepe bāla eva mahāvane \|*  
*karmaṇāṃ kṣupaṇārthāya vimukteḥ paripanthinām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. And he, Ananda, a mere boy, practised austerities in the great forest, in order to consume away his actions which

## \|\| 73.41 \|\|

*tapasyantaṃ tatastañca prāha devaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ tapyase vatsa ! tapastīvraṃ vadasva tat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. were adversaries in the path to final emancipation. And to him then as he practised austerities spoke the divine Prajá-pati -"Why art thou performing severe austerities my child? tell me that."

Ananda spoke:

## \|\| 73.42 \|\|

*ānanda uvāca*  
*ātmanaḥ śuddhikāmo 'haṃ karomi bhagavaṃstapaḥ \|*  
*bandhāya mama karmāṇi yāni tatkṣapaṇonmukhaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Desirous of purity of soul I perform austerities, adorable lord! setting my face towards consuming the actions which tend to fetter me.

Brahmá spoke:

## \|\| 73.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*kṣīṇādhikāro bhavati muktiyogyo na karmavān \|*  
*sattvādhikāravān muktimavāpsyati tato bhavān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He who is lord over consumed actions is fit for final emancipation, not he who engages in action. Hence Sir! thou shalt obtain final emancipation, when thou hast the lordship of

## \|\| 73.44 \|\|

*bhavatā manunā bhāvyaṃ ṣaṣṭhena vraja tat kuru \|*  
*alante tapasā tasmin kṛte muktimavāpsyasi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. goodness. Thou must be the sixth Manu; go; do accordingly! Enough of austerities for thee! When thou hast done that, thou shalt obtain final emancipation.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 73.45 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityukto brahmaṇā so 'pi tathetyuktvā mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tatkarmābhimukho yātastapaso virarāma ha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Being thus exhorted by Brahma, he then the high-minded replied, "So be it!" and went directing himself to that

## \|\| 73.46 \|\|

*cākṣuṣetyāha taṃ brahmā tapaso vinivartayan \|*  
*pūrvanāmnā babhūvātha prakhyātaścākṣuṣo manuḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. pursuit. He ceased indeed from austerities. Turning him away from austerities Brahmá addressed him as C'ákshusha; formerly he was known by that name; he became famous as Manu C'ákshusha.

## \|\| 73.47 \|\|

*upayeme vidarbhāṃ sa sutāmugrasya bhūbhṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyāñcotpādayāmāsa putrān prakhyātavikramān \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He married Vidarbhá, daughter of king Ugra, and begot by her sons celebrated for valour.

## \|\| 73.48 \|\|

*tasya manvantareśasya ye 'ntare tridaśā dvija \|*  
*ye carṣayastathaivendro ye sutāścāsya tān śṛṇu \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Hear, O bráhman, who were the gods of the period, while he reigned over the manvantara; and who were the rishis,

## \|\| 73.49 \|\|

*āpyā nāma surāstatra teṣāmeko 'ṣṭako gaṇaḥ \|*  
*prakhyātakarmaṇāṃ vipra ! yajñe havyabhujāmayam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. and who was the Indra, and who were his sons. The gods therein were named Aryas; they formed one group of eight persons; it was composed of those who had done famous deeds, who partook of the oblations at the sacrifice, O bráhman,

## \|\| 73.50 \|\|

*prakhyātabalavīryāṇāṃ prabhāmaṇḍaladurdṛśām \|*  
*dvitīyaśca prasūtākhyo devānāmaṣṭako gaṇaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. of those who were famous for strength and valour, who were hardly to be gazed at because of their halo of splendour. And the second class of gods was called Prasútas,

## \|\| 73.51 \|\|

*tathaivāṣṭaka evānyo bhavyākhyo devatāgaṇaḥ \|*  
*caturthaśca gaṇastatra yūthagākhyastathāṣṭakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. consisting of eight persons. There was another class of gods also called Bhavyas, consisting of just eight persons; and a fourth class therein was called Yútba-gas, which also

## \|\| 73.52 \|\|

*lekhasaṃjñāstathaivānye tatra manvantare dvija \|*  
*pañcame ca gaṇe devāstatsaṃjñā hyamṛtāśinaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. consisted of eight persons. There were, moreover, other gods called Lekha in a fifth class also in that manvantara,

## \|\| 73.53 \|\|

*śataṃ kratūnāmāhṛtya yasteṣāmadhipo 'bhavat \|*  
*manojavastathaivendraḥ saṃkhyāto yajñabhāgabhuk \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O bráhman; those so named fed indeed on amrita. And the Indra was Mano-java, who offered a hundred sacrifices and became their lord; he was reckoned the eater of a portion of

## \|\| 73.54 \|\|

*sumedhā virajāścaiva haviṣmānunnato madhuḥ \|*  
*atināmā sahiṣṇuśca saptāsanniti carṣayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. the sacrifices. And Su-medhas, and Vi-rajas, Havish-mat, Un-nata, Madhu, Ati-náman, and Sahishnu were the

## \|\| 73.55 \|\|

*ūru-puru-śatadyumnapramukhāḥ sumahābalāḥ \|*  
*cākṣuṣasya manoḥ putrāḥ pṛthivīpatayo 'bhavan \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. seven rishis. Manu C'ákshusha's sons, chief of whom were Urú, Puru, and S'ata-dyumna, very great in strength, were the kings of the earth.

## \|\| 73.56 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ mayā manvantaraṃ dvija \|*  
*cākṣuṣasya tathā janma caritañca mahātmanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Thus I have narrated to thee the sixth manvantara, O bráhman, both the birth and the exploits of high-souled

## \|\| 73.57 \|\|

*sāmprataṃ vartate yo 'yaṃ nāmnā vaivasvato manuḥ \|*  
*saptamīye 'ntare tasya devādyāstān śṛṇuṣva me \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. C'ákshusha. He who subsists at the present time is named Manu Vaivasvata; hear from me about the gods and other chief personages in his, the seventh, period.

## Chapter 74

## \|\| 74.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*mārtaṇḍa rasyaverbhāryā tanayā viśvakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*saṃjñā nāma mahābhāga tasyāṃ bhānurajījanat \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Sun married Tvashtri's daughter Sanjná, and their children were Manu Vaivasvata and Yama -Márkandeya narrates, how the Sun's splendour was pared down by Tvashtri because she could not endure it.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. The Sun Mártanda's wife wasVisva-karman's illustrious

## \|\| 74.2 \|\|

*manuṃ prakhyātayaśasamanekajñānapāragam \|*  
*vivasvataḥ suto yasmāttasmādvaivasvatastu saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. daughter, by name Sanjná. The Sun begot of her a son, a Manu, of celebrated fame, learned in many sciences; since he wasVivasvat's son, he was called Vaivasvata in sooth.

## \|\| 74.3 \|\|

*saṃjñā ca raviṇā dṛṣṭā nimīlayati locane \|*  
*yatastataḥ saroṣor'kaḥ saṃjñāṃ niṣṭhuramabravīt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. And Sanjná used to shut her eyes when the Sun gazed on her, and the Sun in anger thereat spoke sharply to Sanjná

## \|\| 74.4 \|\|

*mayi dṛṣṭe sadā yasmāt kuruṣe netrasaṃyamam \|*  
*tasmājjaniṣyase mūḍhe prajāsaṃyamanaṃ yamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. "Because thou dost always imprison thine eyes when thou seest me, O silly one, thou shalt therefore give birth to Yama, the imprisoner of mankind."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 74.5 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tataḥ sā capalāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ devī cakre bhayākulā \|*  
*vilolitadṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā punarāha ca tāṃ raviḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereupon the goddess, unnerved by fear, became wildeyed, and the Sun seeing her agitated glances addressed her

## \|\| 74.6 \|\|

*yasmādvilolitā dṛṣṭirmayi dṛṣṭe tvayādhunā \|*  
*tasmādvilolāṃ tanayāṃ nadīṃ tvaṃ prasaviṣyasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. again -"Since thine eye-sight has become agitated, now that thou hast seen me, thou shalt therefore give birth to a daughter, the river Vi-lolá."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 74.7 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tatastasyāntu saṃjajñe bhartṛśāpena tena vai \|*  
*yamaśca yamunā ceyaṃ prakhyātā sumahānadī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence through that her husband's curse Yama verily was born of her, and also Yamuná this famous and very great

## \|\| 74.8 \|\|

*sāpi saṃjñā ravestejaḥ sehe duḥ khena bhāminī \|*  
*asahantī ca sā tejaścintayāmāsa vai tadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. river. And it was with pain that Sanjná, the noble lady, endured the Sun's splendour; and then unable to bear the

## \|\| 74.9 \|\|

*kiṅkaromi kva gacchāmi kva gatāyāśca nirvṛtiḥ \|*  
*bhavenmama kathaṃ bhartā kopamarkaśca naiṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. splendour she fell into thought -"What am I to do?" Where am I to go?Where shall I go that I may find ease?And

## \|\| 74.10 \|\|

*iti saṃcintya bahudhā prajāpatisutā tadā \|*  
*bahu mene mahābhāgā pitṛsaṃśrayameva sā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. how shall the Sun, my husband, control his wrath?" So pondering in many ways, the Prajá-pati's illustrious daughter then thought much of actually taking refuge with her father.

## \|\| 74.11 \|\|

*tataḥ pitṛgṛhe gantuṃ kṛtabuddhiryaśasvinī \|*  
*chāyāmayīmātmatanuṃ nirmame dayitāṃ raveḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon the famous lady having resolved to go to her father's house fashioned her body, that the Sun loved, in

## \|\| 74.12 \|\|

*tāñcovāca tvayā veśmanyatra bhānoryathā mayā \|*  
*tathā samyagapatyeṣu vartitavyaṃ yathā ravau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. shadow-form, and addressed her shadow-self -"Remain thou here in the Sun's house even as I; and behave thou

## \|\| 74.13 \|\|

*pṛṣṭayāpi na vācyante tathaitadgamanaṃ mama \|*  
*saivāsmi nāma saṃjñeti vācyametatsadā vacaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. becomingly to the children even as to the Sun.And though questioned say nothing of this my going away; say always this, 'I am she indeed, Sanjná by name.' "

The Shadow-Sanjná spoke:

## \|\| 74.14 \|\|

*chāyasaṃjñovāca*  
*ākeśagrahaṇād devi ! āśāpācca vacastava \|*  
*kariṣye kathayiṣyāmi vṛttantu śāpakarṣaṇāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. "O lady, I will obey thy order and will so declare, as far as suffering my hair to be seized and as far as undergoing curses; it is performed indeed as far as drawing curses down upon myself."

## \|\| 74.15 \|\|

*ityuktā sā tadā devī jagāma bhavanaṃ pituḥ \|*  
*dadarśa tatra tvaṣṭāraṃ tapasā dhūtakalmaṣam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The goddess, receiving this assurance, then went to her father's abode. She sawTvashtri there cleansed from stain

## \|\| 74.16 \|\|

*bahumānācca tenāpi pūjitā viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*tasthau pitṛgṛhe sā tu kañcitkālamaninditā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. by means of austerities. And being honoured by him, Visva-karman, with much respect, she remained in her father's

## \|\| 74.17 \|\|

*tatastāṃ prāha cārvaṅgī pitā nāticiroṣitām \|*  
*stutvā ca tanayāṃ premabahumānapuraḥ saram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. house some time, unreproached. Then her father spoke to the beautiful lady, his daughter, when she had dwelt there not very long, after praising her and prefacing his speech with love and much respect

## \|\| 74.18 \|\|

*tvāntu me paśyato vatse dināni subahūnyapi \|*  
*muhūrtārdhasamāni syuḥ kintu dharmo vilupyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. "Now while I have been seeing thee my child, the days though very many may be reckoned as equal to half a moment;

## \|\| 74.19 \|\|

*bāndhaveṣu ciraṃ vāso nārīṇāṃ na yaśaskaraḥ \|*  
*manoratho bāndhavānāṃ nāryā bhartṛgṛhe sthitiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. nevertheless righteousness suffers loss. Dwelling a long time among kinsmen brings no good repute to women; kinsmen hold a woman's proper residence is in her husband's

## \|\| 74.20 \|\|

*sā tvaṃ trailokyanāthena bhartrā sūryeṇa saṅgatā \|*  
*pitṛgehe ciraṃ kālaṃ vastuṃ nārhasi putrike \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. house. Such art thou, and thou art mated to a husband, the Sun, the lord of the three worlds; deign not my daughter

## \|\| 74.21 \|\|

*sā tvaṃ bhartṛgṛhaṃ gaccha tuṣṭo 'haṃ pūjitāsi me \|*  
*punarāgamanaṃ kāryaṃ darśanāya śubhe mama \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. to dwell a long time in thy father's house. Being such, go thou to thy husband's home. I am pleased; thou hast been honoured by me. Thou must come again to see me, my beautiful one."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 74.22 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityuktā sā tadā pitrā tathetyuktvā ca sā mune \|*  
*saṃpūjayitvā pitaraṃ jagāmāthottarān kurūn \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thus was she admonished by her father then, and she agreeing saluted her father respectfully and went to the

## \|\| 74.23 \|\|

*sūryatāpamanicchantī tejasastasya bibhyatī \|*  
*tapaścacāra tatrāpi vaḍavārūpadhāriṇī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Northern Kurus, O muni, disliking the Sun's heat, afraid of his splendour; and there she practised austerities, changed into a mare's shape.

## \|\| 74.24 \|\|

*saṃjñeyamiti manvāno dvitīyāyāmahaspatiḥ \|*  
*janayāmāsa tanayau kanyāñcaikāṃ manoramām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The lord of day thinking the shadow-form, was Sanjná, begot

## \|\| 74.25 \|\|

*chāyāsaṃjñā tvapatyeṣu yathā sveṣvativatsalā \|*  
*tathā na saṃjñākanyāyāṃ putrayoścānvavartata \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. of that other two sons and a charming daughter. Now the Shadow-Sanjná was very affectionate to the other children just as to her own; Sanjná did not use to show special attention

## \|\| 74.26 \|\|

*lālanādyupabhogeṣu viśeṣamanuvāsaram \|*  
*manustat kṣāntavānasya yamastasyā na cakṣame \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. to her daughter and two sons daily by caresses and other marks of pleasure. Manu accepted that affection from

## \|\| 74.27 \|\|

*tāḍanāya ca vai kopāt pādastena samudyataḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ punaḥ kṣāntimatā na tu dehe nipātitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. her; Yama did not bear it patiently from her, and indeed he lifted his foot in anger to kick her, but, again moved with forbearance towards her, did not strike it against her body.

## \|\| 74.28 \|\|

*tataḥ śaśāpa taṃ kopācchāyāsaṃjñā yamaṃ dvija \|*  
*kiñcit prasphuramāṇauṣṭhī vicalatpāṇipallavā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thereupon, O bráhman, the Shadow-Sanjná in anger cursed Yama, her upper lip quivering slightly, and her delicate

## \|\| 74.29 \|\|

*pituḥ patnīmamaryādaṃ yanmāṃ tarjayase padā \|*  
*bhuvi tasmādayaṃ padāstavādyaiva patiṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. hand shaking -"Because thou spurnest me, thy father's wife, disrespectfully with thy foot, this thy foot shall therefore fall this very day to the earth."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 74.30 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*ityākarṇya yamaḥ śāpaṃ mātrā dattaṃ bhayāturaḥ \|*  
*abhyetya pitaraṃ prāha praṇipātapuraḥ saram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Yama, terrified on hearing the curse that his mother had pronounced on him, went to his father and falling prostrate before him spoke: -

Yama spoke:

## \|\| 74.31 \|\|

*yama uvāca*  
*tātaitanmahadāścaryaṃ na dṛṣṭamiti kenacit \|*  
*mātā vātsalyamutsṛjya śāpaṃ putre prayacchati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O father, this great marvel was never, seen by any one, that a mother casting love away imprecates a curse on her

## \|\| 74.32 \|\|

*yathā manurmamācaṣṭe neyaṃ matā tathā mama \|*  
*viguṇeṣvapi putreṣu na mātā viguṇā bhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. son. She is not mother to me in the same way as Manu calls her his mother; no mother would abandon her good qualities even towards sons devoid of good qualities.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 74.33 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*yamasyaitadvacaḥ śrutvā bhagavāṃstimirāpahaḥ \|*  
*chāyāsaṃjñāṃ samāhūya papraccha kva gateti sā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Hearing this speech from Yama, the adorable Dispeller of darkness called the Shadow-Sanjná and asked her - "Where

## \|\| 74.34 \|\|

*sā cāha tanayā tvaṣṭurahaṃ saṃjñā vibhāvaso \|*  
*patnī tava tvayāpatyānyetāni janitāni me \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. has she gone?" And she answered -"I am Tvashtri's daughter Sanjná, O god of fire, thy wife; through thee these children

## \|\| 74.35 \|\|

*itthaṃ vivasvataḥ sā tu bahuśaḥ pṛcchato yadā \|*  
*nācacakṣe tataḥ kruddho bhāsvāṃstāṃ śaptumudyataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. were begotten of me." Now when, as Vivasvat was thus questioning her repeatedly, she did not speak further, the Sun

*niśāmaya tadutpattiṃ vistarād gadato mama \|\| 1 \|\|*

The slaughter of Madhu and Kaitabha in the account of the Sávarnika Manvantara.

King Su-ratha being defeated and driven from his kingdom took refuge in the forest with a muni -He met a vaisya who had been driven from his home by his relatives, and both asked the muni about the selfish feelings which still possessed them. -He ascribes those feelings to the goddess Mahá-máyá or Great Illusion, and relates how Brahmá lauded the goddess at the end of a former kalpa in order to seek deliverance from the demons Madhu and Kaitabha, and how Vishnu awaking slew the demons.

Om! Reverence to C'andiká.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Súrya's son Sávarni is he who is called the eighth Manu.

Slaughter of the army of theAsura Mahisha.

The gods were defeated in a great battle formerly by the Asuras and driven from heaven, and the Asura Mahisha became supreme. -All the gods gave forth their special energies, which combined and formed the goddess C'andiká. -They gave her their weapons, and she fought with and destroyed the Asuras.
