## Chapter 81

## \|\| 81.1 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve devyā handrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*stutimārebhire kartuṃ nihate mahiṣāsure \|\| 1 \|\|*

The gods poured forth their praises to C'andiká on her victory -And she gave them the boon that she would always befriend them, if they recalled her to mind in calamities.

The rishi spoke:

1\. When that most valiant evil-souled army of the gods' foes was vanquished by the goddess, Sakra and the hosts of other gods poured forth their praises to her with their voices, reverently bending down their necks and shoulders, while their bodies looked handsome because their hair stood erect with exultation.

## \|\| 81.2 \|\|

*śakrādayaḥ suragaṇā nihate 'tivīrye*  
*tasmin durātmani surāribale ca devyā \|*  
*tāṃ tuṣṭubuḥ praṇatinamraśirodharāṃsā*  
*vāgbhiḥ praharṣapulakodgamacārudehāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The goddess, who stretched out this world by her power, Whose body comprises the entire powers of all the hosts of gods, Her, Ambiká, worthy of worship by all gods and great rishis, We bow before in faith; may she ordain blessings for us!

## \|\| 81.3 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*devyā yayā tatamidaṃ jagadātmaśaktyā*  
*niḥ śeṣadevagaṇaśaktisamūhamūrtyā \|*  
*tāmambikāmakhiladevamarṣipūjyāṃ*  
*bhaktyā natāḥ sma vidadhātu śubhāni sā naḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. May she, whose peerless majesty and power Ananta Adorable, Brahmá and Hara cannot in sooth declare, May she, C'andiká, to protect the entire world And to destroy the fear of evil turn her mind!

## \|\| 81.4 \|\|

*yasyāḥ prabhāvamatulaṃ bhagavānananto*  
*brahmā haraśca nahi vaktumalaṃ balaṃ ca \|*  
*sā caṇḍikākhilajagatparipālanāya*  
*nāśāya cāśubhayasya matiṃ karotu \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Her, who is Good-Fortune herself in the dwellings of men of good deeds, Ill-Fortune In those of men of sinful souls; who is Intelligence in the hearts of the prudent, Who is Faith in those of the good, and Modesty in that of the high-born man; Her, even thee, we bow before; protect the universe, O goddess!

## \|\| 81.5 \|\|

*yā śrīḥ svayaṃ sukṛtināṃ bhavaneṣvalakṣmīḥ*  
*pāpātmanāṃ kṛtadhiyāṃ hṛdayeṣu buddhiḥ \|*  
*śraddhāṃ satāṃ kulajanaprabhavasya lajjā*  
*tāṃ tvāṃ natāḥ sma paripālaya devi viśvam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Can we describe this thy thought-transcending form? Or thy abundant surpassing valour that destroyed the Asuras? Or thy surpassing feats which were displayed in battles Among all the hosts of Asuras, gods and others, O goddess?

## \|\| 81.6 \|\|

*kiṃ varṇayāma tava rūpamacintyametat*  
*kiṃ cātivīryamasurakṣayakāri bhūri \|*  
*kiṃ cāhaveṣu caritāni tavādbhutāni*  
*sarveṣu devyasuradevagaṇādikeṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thou art the cause of all the worlds! Though characterized by the three qualities, by faults Thou art not known! Even by Hari, Hara and the other gods thou art incomprehensible! Thou art the resort of all; thou art this entire world which is composed of parts! Thou verily art sublime original Nature untransformed!

## \|\| 81.7 \|\|

*hetuḥ samastajagatāṃ triguṇāpi doṣair*  
*na jñāyase hariharādibhirapyapārā \|*  
*sarvāśrayākhilamidaṃ jagadaṃśabhūtam*  
*avyākṛtā hi paramā prakṛtistvamādyā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thou, whose complete divinity by means of utterance Finds satisfaction in all sacrifices, O goddess, Art verily Sváhá, and givest satisfaction to the Pitri-hosts! Hence thou art in truth declared by men to be Svadhá also.

## \|\| 81.8 \|\|

*yasyāḥ samastasuratā samudīraṇena*  
*tṛptiṃ priyāti sakaleṣu makheṣu devi \|*  
*svāhāsi vai pitṛgaṇasya ca tṛptihetur*  
*uccāryase tvamata eva janaiḥ svadhā ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thou art she, who effects final emancipation, and performs great thought-transcending penances! Thou studiest with thy organs, which are the essence of strength, well-restrained! With munis, who seek final emancipation and who have shed all their faults, Thou art The Knowledge, adorable, sublime in sooth, O goddess!

## \|\| 81.9 \|\|

*yā muktiheturavicintyamahāvratā tvam*  
*abhyasyase suniyatendriyatattvasāraiḥ \|*  
*mokṣārthibhirmunibhirastasamastadoṣair*  
*vidyāsi sā bhagavatī paramā hi devi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Sound is thy soul! thou art the repository of the most spotless ric' and yajus hymns, And of the sámans, which have the charming-worded texts of the Ud-gítha! Thou as goddess art the tripleVeda, the adorable, and for the existence and production Of all the worlds art active; thou art the supreme destroyer of their pains!

## \|\| 81.10 \|\|

*śabdātmikā suvimalargyajuṣāṃ nidhānam*  
*udgītharamyapadapāṭhavatāṃ ca sāmnām \|*  
*devī trayī bhagavatī bhavabhāvanāya*  
*vārtā ca sarvajagatāṃ paramārtihantrī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thou art Mental Vigour O goddess! thou hast comprehended the essence of all the Scriptures! Thou art Durgá; the boat to cross the difficult ocean of existence; devoid of attachments! Thou art Srí, who has planted her dominion alone in the heart of Kaitabha's foe! Thou indeed art Gaurí, who has fixed her dwelling in the moon-crested god!

## \|\| 81.11 \|\|

*medhāsi devi viditākhilaśāstrasārā*  
*durgāsi durgabhavasāgaranaurasaṅgā \|*  
*śrīḥ kaiṭabhārihṛdayaikakṛtādhivāsā*  
*gaurī tvameva śaśimaulikṛtapratiṣṭhā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Slightly-smiling, spotless, resembling the full moon's Orb, beautiful as the choicest gold, and lovely was thy face! Yet 't was very marvellous that, being swayed by anger, TheAsura Mahisha suddenly smote thy face when he saw it.

## \|\| 81.12 \|\|

*īṣatsahāsamamalaṃ paripūrṇacandra-*  
*bimbānukāri kanakottamakāntikāntam \|*  
*atyadbhutaṃ prahṛtamāttaruṣā tathāpi*  
*vaktraṃ vilokya sahasā mahiṣāsureṇa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. But after seeing thy wrathful face, O goddess, terrible with its frowns, And sheeny in hue like the rising moon, that Mahisha Did not forthwith yield up his life, 't was passing wonderful! For who can live after beholding the King of Death enraged?

## \|\| 81.13 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tu devi kupitaṃ bhrukuṭīkarālam*  
*udyacchaśāṅkasadṛśacchavi yanna sadyaḥ \|*  
*prāṇānmumoca mahīṣastadatīva citraṃ*  
*kairjovyate hi kupitāntakadarśanena \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Be gracious, O goddess, as supreme lady, to life! When enraged thou dost forthwith destroy whole families! Known at this very moment is this, that here is brought to its end TheAsura Mahisha's most extensive might!

## \|\| 81.14 \|\|

*devi prasīda paramā bhavatī bhavāya*  
*sadyo vināśayasi kopavatī kulāni \|*  
*vijñātametadadhunaiva yadastametan*  
*nītaṃ balaṃ suvipulaṃ mahiṣāsurasya \|\| 14 \|\|*

14 Esteemed are they among the nations, theirs are riches, Theirs are glories, and their sum of righteousness perishes not, Happy are they indeed, and they possess devoted children, servants and wives, On whom thou, well-pleased, dost always bestow prosperity, O lady!

## \|\| 81.15 \|\|

*te saṃmatā janapadeṣu dhanāni teṣāṃ*  
*teṣāṃ yaśāṃsi na ca sīdati dharmavargaḥ \|*  
*dhanyāsta eva nibhṛtātmajabhṛtyadārā*  
*yeṣāṃ sadābhyudayadā bhavatī prasannā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All righteous actions ever indeed, O goddess, With utmost respect the man of good deeds daily performs, And gains heaven thereafter by thy favour, O lady. Dost thou not by him bestow rewards even on the three worlds, O goddess?

## \|\| 81.16 \|\|

*dharmyāṇi devi sakalāni sadaiva karmāṇy*  
*atyādṛtaḥ pratidinaṃ sukṛtī karoti \|*  
*svargaṃ prayāti ca tato bhavatīprasādāl*  
*lokatraye 'pi phaladā nanu devi tena \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thou, O Durgá, when called to mind, dost remove terror from every creature! Thou, when called to mind by those in health, dost bestow a mind extremely bright! What goddess but thou, O dispeller of poverty, pain and fear, Has ever benevolent thoughts in order to work benefits to all?

## \|\| 81.17 \|\|

*durge smṛtā harasi bhītimaśeṣajantoḥ*  
*svasthaiḥ smṛtā matimatīva śubhāṃ dadāsi \|*  
*dāridrayaduḥ khabhayahāriṇi kā tvadanyā*  
*sarvopakārakaraṇāya sadār''dracittā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By these slain foes the world attains to happiness; thus let these Forsooth practise sin so as to descend to hell for long! 'Meeting death in battle let them proceed to heaven' – Thinking thus, thou dost assuredly destroy the enemies, O goddess!

## \|\| 81.18 \|\|

*ebhirhatairjagadupaiti sukhaṃ tathaite*  
*kurvantu nāma narakāya cirāya pāpam \|*  
*saṃgrāmamṛtyumadhigamya divaṃ prayāntu*  
*matveti nūnamahitān vinihaṃsi devi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Having indeed seen them, why dost thou not, O lady, reduce to ashes All the Asuras, since thou directest thy weapons against the foes? 'Let even enemies, purified by dying in arms, attain in sooth to the bright worlds' – Such is thy most kindly intention towards even them.

## \|\| 81.19 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaiva kiṃ na bhavatī prakaroti bhasma*  
*sarvāsurānariṣu yatprahiṇoṣi śastram \|*  
*lokān prayāntu ripavo 'pi hi śastrapūtā*  
*itthaṃ matirbhavati teṣvapi te 'tisādhvī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. And though, neither by the sharp flashes of abundant light from thy scymitar, Nor by the copious lustre of thy spear-point, the eyes of the Asuras Were destroyed; yet, as they gazed upon thy countenance Which bore a portion of the radiant moon, this very thing happened.

## \|\| 81.20 \|\|

*khaḍgaprabhānikaravisphuraṇaistathograiḥ*  
*śūlāgrakāntinivahena dṛśo 'surāṇām \|*  
*yannāgatā vilayamaṃśumadindukhaṇḍa-*  
*yogyānanaṃ tava vilokayatāṃ tadetat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thy disposition, O goddess, subdues the conduct of men of evil conduct; And this thy form surpasses thought and rivalry by others; And thy valour vanquishes those who have robbed the gods of their prowess; Thou hast as it were manifested pity thus even on enemies!

## \|\| 81.21 \|\|

*durvṛttavṛttaśamanaṃ tava devi śīlaṃ*  
*rūpaṃ tathaitadavicintyamatulyamanyaiḥ \|*  
*vīryaṃ ca hantṛ hṛtadevaparākramāṇāṃ*  
*vairiṣvapi prakaṭitaiva dayā tvayettham \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. To what my this thy prowess be compared? And whereto thy form most charming, which strikes fear among foes? Compassion in mind and relentlessness in battle are seen In thee, O goddess, who bestowest boons even on the three worlds!

## \|\| 81.22 \|\|

*kenopamā bhavatu te 'sya parākramasya*  
*rūpaṃ ca śatrubhayakāryatihāri kutra \|*  
*citte kṛpā samaraniṣṭhuratā ca dṛṣṭā*  
*tvayyeva devi varade bhuvanatraye 'pi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Through the destruction of the foes, these three worlds entire Have been saved by thee. Having slain them in the battle-front Thou hast led even those hosts of foes to heaven, and dispelled the fear Which beset us from the frenzied foes of the gods. Reverence to thee!

## \|\| 81.23 \|\|

*trailokyametadakhilaṃ ripunāśanena*  
*trātaṃ tvayā samaramūrdhani te 'pi hatvā \|*  
*nītā divaṃ ripugaṇā bhayamapyapāstam*  
*asmākamunmadasurāribhavaṃ namaste \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With thy spear protect us, O goddess! Protect us with thy sword also, OAmbiká! By the clanging of thy bell protect us, And by the twanging of the thong of thy bow!

## \|\| 81.24 \|\|

*śūlena pāhi no devi pāhi khaḍgena cāmbike \|*  
*ghaṇṭāsvanena naḥ pāhi cāpajyāniḥ svanena ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the east guard us, and in the west; O C'andiká, guard us in the south By the brandishing of thy spear, And also in the north, O goddess!

## \|\| 81.25 \|\|

*prācyāṃ rakṣa pratīcyāṃ ca caṇḍike rakṣa dakṣiṇe \|*  
*bhrāmaṇenātmaśūlasya uttarasyāṃ tatheśvari \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Whatever gentle forms of thee wander about in the three worlds, And whatever exceedingly terrible forms wander, by means of them guard us and the earth!

## \|\| 81.26 \|\|

*saumyāni yāni rūpāṇi trailokye vicaranti te \|*  
*yāni cātyarthaghorāṇi tai rakṣāsmāṃstathā bhuvam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thy sword and spear and club, and whatever other weapons, OAmbiká, Rest in thy pliant hand, with them guard us on every side!

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 81.27 \|\|

*khaḍgaśūlagadādīni yāni cāstrāṇi te 'mbike \|*  
*karapallavasaṅgīni tairasmān rakṣa sarvataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus was she, the Upholder of the worlds, hymned by the gods, and they paid honour to her with celestial flowers that blossomed in Nandana, and with perfumes and unguents.

## \|\| 81.28 \|\|

*ṛṣīruvāca*  
*evaṃ stutā surairdivyaiḥ kusumairnandanodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*arcitā jagatāṃ dhātrī tathā gandhānulepanaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Moreover all the thirty gods in faith censed her with heavenly incenses. Benignly sweet in countenance she spoke to all the prostrate gods.

The goddess spoke:

## \|\| 81.29 \|\|

*bhaktyā samastaistridaśārdivyairdhūpaistu dhūpitā \|*  
*prāha prasādasumukhī samastān praṇatān surān \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Choose, ye thirty all! whatever ye desire of me, for I grant it with pleasure, being highly honoured by these hymns.

The gods spoke:

## \|\| 81.30 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*vriyatāṃ tridaśāḥ sarve yadasmatto 'bhivāñchitam \|*  
*dadāmyahamatiprītyā stavairebhiḥ supūjitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thou, O adorable lady, hast accomplished all, nought remains undone, in that thisAsura Mahisha, our foe has

## \|\| 81.31 \|\|

*kartavyamaparaṃ yacca duṣkaraṃ tanna vidmahe \|*  
*ityākarṇye vaco devyāḥ pratyūcuste divaukasaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. been slain. Yet if thou must grant us a boon, O goddess great! whenever we call thee, call thee to mind, do thou

## \|\| 81.32 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*

32\. away with our direst calamities!And whatever mortal shall praise thee with these hymns, O lady of spotless countenance, to prosper him in wealth and wife and other blessings by means of riches, success and power do thou incline always, O Ambiká, who art propitious to us!

The rishi spoke:

## \|\| 81.33 \|\|

*yadi cāpi varo deyastvayāsmākaṃ maheśvari \|*  
*saṃsmṛtā saṃsmṛtā tvaṃ no hiṃsethāḥ paramāpadaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Being thus propitiated by the gods for the good of the world and on their own behalf, "Be it so!" said she, Bhadrakálí; and vanished from their sight, O king.

## \|\| 81.34 \|\|

*yaśca martyaḥ stavairebhistvāṃ stoṣyatyamalānane \|*

34\. Thus I have narrated this, O king, how the goddess came into being of yore from out of the gods' bodies, she who desires the

## \|\| 81.35 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*iti prasāditā devairjagator'the tathā'tmanaḥ \|*

35\. good of all the three worlds. And again she came into existence having the body of Gaurí, just as she did before, in order

36\. to slay the wicked Daityas and S'umbha and Nisumbha, and to preserve the worlds, as benefactress of the gods. Hearken then to what I have declared to thee. I have truly told it thee.

## Chapter 82

## \|\| 82.1 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*purā śumbhaniśumbhābhyāmasurābhyāṃ śacīpateḥ \|*  
*trailokyaṃ yajñabhāgāśca hṛtā madabalāśrayāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Asuras S’umbha and Nisumbha conquered the gods and drove them from heaven. -The gods invoked C'andiká at Himavat in a hymn, appealing to her by all her attributes to help them. -Párvatí came there and C'andiká sprang forth from her body. -The servants of S’umbha and Nisumbha saw her and extolled her perfect beauty to S’umbha. -He sent a messenger to invite her to marry him. -She explained that by a vow she could marry no one who did not conquer her in fight.

The rishi spoke:

1\. Of yore the Asuras S'umbha and Nisumbha, trusting in their pride and strength, robbed S’ac’i’s lord of the three

## \|\| 82.2 \|\|

*tāveva sūryatāṃ tadvadadhikāraṃ tathaindavam \|*  
*kauberamatha yāmyaṃ ca cakrāte varuṇasya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. worlds and of his portions of the sacrifices; they both usurped likewise the sun's dignity and the moon's dominion,

## \|\| 82.3 \|\|

*tāveva pavanardhi ca cakraturvahnikarma ca \|*  
*anyeṣāñcādhikārān sa svayamevādhitiṣṭhati \|*  
*tato devā vinirdhūtā bhraṣṭarājyāḥ parājitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. and Kuvera's and Yama's and Varuna's; and they both exercised Váyu's authority and Agni's sphere of action. Thereby the gods were scattered, deprived of their

## \|\| 82.4 \|\|

*hṛtādhikārāstridaśāstābhyāṃ sarve nirākṛtāḥ \|*  
*mahāsurābhyāṃ tāṃ devīṃ saṃsmarantyaparājitām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. sovereignties and put to rout. The thirty gods, bereft of their dominion and set at nought by those two greatAsuras, all

## \|\| 82.5 \|\|

*tayāsmākaṃ varo datto yathā'patsu smṛtākhilāḥ \|*  
*bhavatāṃ nāśayiṣyāmi tatkṣaṇāt paramāpadaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. recall to mind that never-vanquished goddess, -"Thou didst grant us the boon, 'As ye when in calamities shall call me to mind, that very moment will I put an end to all your direst

## \|\| 82.6 \|\|

*iti kṛtvā matiṃ devā himavantaṃ nageśvaram \|*  
*jagmustatra tato devīṃ viṣṇumāyāṃ pratuṣṭuvuḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. calamities.' " Making this resolve the gods went to Himavat, lord among mountains, and there raised their hymn to the goddess, who isVishnu's illusive power.

The gods spoke:

## \|\| 82.7 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*namo devyai mahādevyai śivāyai satataṃ namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ prakṛtyai bhadrāyai niyatāḥ praṇatāḥ sma tām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Reverence to the goddess, to the great goddess! To her who is auspicious reverence perpetually! Reverence to Prakriti the good! Submissive we fall prostrate before her!

## \|\| 82.8 \|\|

*raudrāyai namo nityāyau gauryai dhātryai namo namaḥ \|*  
*namo jagatpratiṣṭhāyai devyai kṛtyai namo namaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Reverence to her who is terrible, to her who is constant! To Gaurí, to Dhátri reverence, yea reverence! And to the Moon-light, to her who has the moon's form, To her who is happy, reverence continually!

## \|\| 82.9 \|\|

*dyotstrāyai cendurūpiṇyai sukhāyai satataṃ namaḥ \|*  
*kalyāṇyai praṇatāṃ vṛddhyai siddhyai kurmo namo namaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Falling prostrate, to her who is propitious, to Prosperity, To Perfection let us pay reverence, yea reverence! To Nirriti, to the goddess of Good-Fortune of kings, To thee, Sarvání, reverence, yea reverence!

## \|\| 82.10 \|\|

*nairṛtyai bhūbhṛtāṃ lakṣmyai śarvāṇyai te namo namaḥ \|*

*khyātyai tathaiva kṛṣṇāyai dhūmrāyai satataṃ namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. To Durgá, to her who is a further shore difficult to be reached, To her who is essential, to her who works all things, And to Fame also, to her who is blue-black, To her who is smoke-dark reverence continually!

## \|\| 82.11 \|\|

*atisaumyātiraudrāyai natāstasyai namo namaḥ \|*  
*mano jagatpratiṣṭhāyai devyai kṛtyai namo namaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Before her who is at once most gentle and most harsh We fall prostrate; to her reverence, yea reverence! Reverence to her who is the foundation of the world! To the goddess who isAction reverence, yea reverence!

## \|\| 82.12 \|\|

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu viṣṇumāyeti śabditā \|*  
*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. To the goddess who among all created things Is called Vishnu's illusive power, Reverence to her, yea reverence to her! Reverence to her, reverence, yea reverence!

## \|\| 82.13 \|\|

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu cetanetyabhidhīyate \|*  
*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. To the goddess who among all created beings Bears the name Consciousness, Reverence to her, yea reverence to her! Reverence to her, reverence, yea reverence!

*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu dayārūpeṇa saṃsthitā \|*  
*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu nītirūpeṇaṃ saṃsthitā \|*  
*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu tuṣṭirūpeṇa saṃsthitā \|*  
*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

## \|\| 82.34 \|\|

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu mātṛrūpeṇa saṃsthitā \|*  
*namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. To her who exists pervading this entire World with the form of Thinking Mind, Reverence to her, yea reverence to her! Reverence to her, reverence, yea reverence!

## \|\| 82.35 \|\|

*yā devī sarvabhūteṣu bhrāntirūpeṇa saṃsthitā \|*

## Chapter 88

The gods offered a hymn of praise to the goddess. -She granted them the boon that she will always become incarnate and deliver the world whenever it is oppressed by demons.

The rishi spoke:

1\. When the great lord of the Asuras was slain there by the goddess, Indra and the other gods led byAgni offered praise to her, Kátyáyaní, because they had gained their desire; and their faces shone forth, and their hopes became manifest.

*prasīda viśveśvari pāhi viśvaṃ*  
*tvamīśvarī devi carācarasya \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. "O goddess, who removest the sufferings of thy suppliants, be gracious! Be gracious, O mother of the whole world! Be gracious, O queen of the universe! safeguard the universe! Thou, O goddess, art queen of all that is moveable and immoveable!

## \|\| 88.3 \|\|

*ādhārabhūtā jagatastvamekā*

## \|\| 88.5 \|\|

*vidyāḥ samastāstava devi bhedāḥ*

## Chapter 89

## \|\| 89.1 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*ebhiḥ stavaiśca māṃ nityaṃ stoṣyate yaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ sakalāṃ bādhāṃ nāśayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

The goddess descants on the merits of this poem and the beneficent results of reading and listening to it. - The gods regained their rights and the Daityas departed to Pátála. -Her attributes and beneficence are extolled.

The goddess spoke:

## Chapter 90

## \|\| 90.1 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*etatte kathitaṃ bhūpa devīmāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*evaṃprabhāvā sā devī yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat \|\| 1 \|\|*

After hearing this poem, king Su-ratha and the vaisya practised austerities and worshipped the goddess. C'andiká appeared to them and gave the king the boon that he should be Manu Sávarni in a future life, and bestowed knowledge on the vaisya.

The rishi spoke:

1\. I have now related to thee, O king, this sublime poem the Deví-máhátmya. Such majestic power has the goddess, by

## \|\| 90.2 \|\|

*vidyā tathaiva kriyate bhagavadviṣṇumāyayā \|*  
*tathā tvameṣa vaiśyaśca tathaivānye vivekinaḥ \|*  
*mohyante mohitāścaiva mohameṣyanti cāpare \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. whom this world is upheld. Moreover knowledge is conferred by her who is the adorable "Vishnu's Illusive power. By her thou and this vaisya and other men of discrimination, and

## \|\| 90.3 \|\|

*tāmupaihi mahārāja śaraṇaṃ parameśvarīm \|*  
*ārādhitā saiva nṛṇāṃ bhogasvargāpavargadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. celebrated men are bewitched; and others shall become bewitched. Go unto her, the supreme queen, as to a place of refuge, O great king. She indeed, when propitiated by men, bestows enjoyment, Svarga and final emancipation from existence.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 90.4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā surathaḥ sa narādhipaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya mahābhāgaṃ tamṛṣiṃ śaṃsitavratam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Having heard this his speech, king Su-ratha fell prostrate before the illustrious rishi who performed severe penances,

## \|\| 90.5 \|\|

*nirviṇṇo 'timamatvena rājyāpaharaṇena ca \|*  
*jagama sadyastapase sa ca vaiśyo mahāmune \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. and being down-cast by his excessive regard for self and by the deprivation of his kingdom, went forthwith to perform

## \|\| 90.6 \|\|

*saṃdarśanārthamambāyā nadīpulinasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*sa ca vaiśyastapastepe devīsūktaṃ paraṃ japan \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. austerities; and the vaisya, O great muni, in order to get a vision of Ambá, took up his station on a sand-bank

## \|\| 90.7 \|\|

*tau tasmin piline devyāḥ kṛtvā mūrti mahīmayīm \|*  
*arhaṇāṃ cakratustasyāḥ puṣpadhūpāgnitarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. in a river; and the vaisya practised austerities, muttering the sublime hymn to the goddess. They both made an earthen image of the goddess on that sand-bank, and paid worship

## \|\| 90.8 \|\|

*nirāhārau yatātmānau tanmanaskau samāhitau \|*  
*dadatustau baliṃ caiva nijagātrāsṛgukṣitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. to it with flowers, incense, fire and libations of water. Abstaining from food, restricting their food, concentrating their minds on her, keeping their thoughts composed, they both

## \|\| 90.9 \|\|

*evaṃ samārādhayatostribhirvarṣairyatātmanoḥ \|*  
*parituṣṭā jagaddhātrī pratyakṣaṃ prāha caṇḍikā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. offered the bali offering also sprinkled with blood drawn from their own limbs. When they continued with subdued souls to propitiate her thus for three years, C'andiká, who upholds the world, well-pleased spoke in visible shape.

The goddess spoke:

## \|\| 90.10 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca*  
*yatprārthyate tvayā bhūpa tvayā ca kulanandana \|*  
*mattastatprāpyatāṃ sarvaṃ parituṣṭā dadāmi tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. What thou dost solicit, O king, and thou O rejoicer of thy family, receive ye all that from me; well-pleased I bestow it.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 90.11 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tato vavre nṛpo rājyamavibhraṃśyanyajanmani \|*  
*atraiva ca nijaṃ rājyaṃ hataśatrubalaṃ balāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the king chose a kingdom that should not perish in another life, and in this life his own kingdom wherein the

## \|\| 90.12 \|\|

*so 'pi vaiśyastato jñānaṃ vavre nirviṇṇamānasaḥ \|*  
*mametyahamiti prājñaḥ saṅgavicyutikārakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. power of his enemies should be destroyed by force. Then the vaisya also, whose mind was down-cast, chose knowledge, -to be wise, knowing 'what is mine,' and 'what I am,' knowledge that causes the downfall of worldly attachments.

The goddess spoke:

## \|\| 90.13 \|\|

*śrīdevyuvāca*  
*svalpairahobhirnṛpate svaṃ rājyaṃ prāpsyate bhavān \|*  
*hatvā ripūnaskhalitaṃ tava tatra bhaviṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O king, thou shalt obtain thine own kingdom in a very few days, after slaying thine enemies; it shall be steadfast for

## \|\| 90.14 \|\|

*mṛtaśca bhūyaḥ samprāpya janma devādvivasvataḥ \|*  
*sāvarṇiko nāma manurbhavān bhuvi bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. thee there; and when dead thou shalt gain another life from the god "Vivasvat, and shalt be a Manu on earth, by name

## \|\| 90.15 \|\|

*vaiśyavarya tvayā yaśca varo 'smatto 'bhivāñchataḥ \|*  
*taṃ prayacchāmi saṃsiddhyai tava jñānaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sávarnika. And O excellent vaisya, I bestow on thee the boon which thou hast besought of me; knowledge shall be thine unto full perfection.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 90.16 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*iti dattvā tayordevī yathābhilaṣitaṃ varam \|*  
*babhūvāntarhitā sadyo bhaktyā tābhyāmabhiṣṭutā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Having thus given them both the boon that each desired, the goddess vanished forthwith, while extolled by them both in faith.

## \|\| 90.17 \|\|

*evaṃ devyā varaṃ labdhvā surathaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ \|*  
*sūryājjanma samāsādya sāvarṇirbhavitā manuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Having thus gained the boon from the goddess, Su-ratha the noble kshatriya shall obtain a new birth through the Sun, and shall be the Manu Sávarni.

## Chapter 91

## \|\| 91.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sāvarṇikamidaṃ samyakproktaṃ manvantaraṃ tava \| tathaiva devīmāhātmye mahiṣāsuraghātanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya mentions briefly the succeeding Manus, the ninth to the thirteenth, and declares what shall be the names of the gods, rishis and kings in their several periods.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. I have duly declared unto thee this account of the Sávarnika Manvantara, and also the Deví-máhátmya which tells of the

## \|\| 91.2 \|\|

*utpattayaśca yā devyā mātṝṇāṃ ca mahāhave \| tathaiva sambhavo devyāścāmuṇḍāyā yathā bhavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. slaughter of the Asura Mahisha. And the origins of the Mothers also which were from the goddess in the great battle,

## \|\| 91.3 \|\|

3\. and the origin as well as the life of the goddess C'ámundá, and the majesty of S'iva-dútí, the slaying of S'umbha and Nisumbha, and the killing of Rakta-víja -all this has been narrated to thee.

## \|\| 91.4 \|\|

## \|\| 91.5 \|\|

*kathayāmi manostasya ye devā munayo nṛpāḥ \| pārā marīcibhargāśca sudharmāṇastathā surāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

6\. and the Bhargas and the Su-dharmans shall be the gods; these shall be in threes; they shall be twelve groups in all; now

## \|\| 91.7 \|\|

7\. their lord shall be Sahasráksha, great in power. He, who is at presentAgni's six-faced son Kárttikeya, shall be the Indra,

*medhātithirvasuḥ satyo jyotiṣmāndyutimāṃstathā \| saptarṣayo'nyaḥ sabalastathānyo havyavāhanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dhṛṣṭaketurbarhaketuḥ khaḍgahasto nirāmayaḥ \| pṛthuśravāstathārciṣmānbhūridyumno bṛhadbhayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. váhana another -these shall be the seven rishis. Dhrishtaketu, Varha-ketu, Panc'a-hasta, Nir-ámaya, Prithu-s'ravas, and

*ete nṛpasutāstasya dattaputrasya vai nṛpāḥ \|*

10\. Arc'ish-mat, Bhúri-dyumna, Vrihad-bhaya -these shall be the royal sons of that son of Daksha, yea the kings. Now hear, O bráhman, about the next Manvantara, that of the

*manvantare ca daśame brahmaputrasya dhīmataḥ \| sukhāsīnā niruddhāśca dviprakārāḥ surāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śatasaṃkhyā hi te devā bhaviṣyā bhāvino manoḥ \| yatputrāṇāṃ śataṃ bhāvi taddevānāṃ tadā śatam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śāntirindrastathā bhāvī sarvairindraguṇairyutaḥ \| saptarṣīṃstānnibodha tvaṃ ye bhaviṣyanti vai tadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. so shall there be a hundred gods then. And Sánti shall be the Indra, endowed with all Indra's good qualities. Hear thou

## \|\| 91.14 \|\|

*āpomūtirhaviṣmāṃśca sukṛtī satya eva ca \| nābhāgo'pratimaścaiva vāsiṣṭhaścaiva saptamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. who shall indeed be the seven rishis then; Apo-múrtti and Havish-mat, Su-kritin and Satya, Nábhága and A-pratima,

## \|\| 91.15 \|\|

*sukṣetraścottamaujāśca bhūriṣeṇaśca vīryavān \| śatānīko'tha vṛṣabho hyanamitro jayadrathaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*bhūridyumnaḥ suparvā ca tasyaite tanayā manoḥ \| bhaviṣyā dharmaputrasya sāvarṇasyāntaraṃ śṛṇu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. amitra, Jayad-ratha, Bhúri-dyumna, and Su-parvan -these shall be that Manu's sons.

## \|\| 91.17 \|\|

*vihaṅgamāḥ kāmagāśca nirmāṇaratayastathā \| triḥprakārā bhaviṣyanti ekaikastriṃśako gaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hear about the period of Dharma's son Sávarna. TheVihangamas, and the Káma-gas and the Nirmána-ratis shall be the gods of three kinds; each shall be a group of thirty.

## \|\| 91.18 \|\|

*māsartudivasā ye tu nirmāṇapatayastu te \| vihaṅgamā rātrayo'tha mauhūrttāḥ kāmagā gaṇāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Now the Nirmána-ratis shall be those who preside over the months, seasons and days; and the Vihan-gamas shall be those who preside over the nights; the groups of Káma-gas

## \|\| 91.19 \|\|

*indro vṛṣākhyo bhavitā teṣāṃ prakhyātavikramaḥ \| haviṣmāṃśca variṣṭhaśca ṛṣṭiranyastathāruṇiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. shall be those who preside over the moments. Their Indra shall be namedVrisha, celebrated for valour. And Havish

## \|\| 91.20 \|\|

*niścaraścānaghaścaiva viṣṭiścānyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*saptarṣayo'ntare tasminnagnitejāśca saptamaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. mat, and Varishtha, and another rishi Aruni, and Nis'-c'ara and An-agha, and another great muni Vishti, and Agni-deva the seventh, - these shall be the seven rishis in that period.

## \|\| 91.21 \|\|

*sarvatragaḥ suśarmā ca devānīkaḥ purūdvahaḥ \| hemadhanvā dṛḍhāyuśca bhāvinastatsutā nṛpāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

## \|\| 91.22 \|\|

*dvādaśe rudraputrasya prāpte manvantare manoḥ \| sāvarṇākhyāśca ye devā munayaśca śṛṇuṣva tān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When the twelfth Manvantara of Rudra's son, the Manu named Sávarna, shall have arrived, who shall be the gods

## \|\| 91.23 \|\|

*sudharmāṇaḥ sumanaso harito rohitastathā \| suvarṇāśca surāstatra pañcaite daśakā gaṇāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. and munis, -hear about them. The Su-dharmans, the Sumanases, the Haritas and the Rohitas and the Su-varnas shall be the gods therein; these five shall be ten-fold groups.

## \|\| 91.24 \|\|

*teṣāmindrastu vijñeya ṛtadhāmā mahābalaḥ \| sarvairindraguṇairyuktāḥ saptarṣīnapi me śṛṇu \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Now their Indra shall be known as Rita-dháman, great in power, endowed with all Indra's good qualities. Hear from

## \|\| 91.25 \|\|

*dyutistapasvī sutapāstapomūrtistaponidhiḥ \| taporatistathaivānyaḥ saptamastu tapodhṛtiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. me the seven rishis also -Dyuti, Tapas-vin, Su-tapas, Tapomúrtti, Tapo-nidhi, andTapo-rati another, andTapo-dhriti

*devavānupadevaśca devaśreṣṭho vidūrathaḥ \| mitravānmitravindaśca bhāvinastatsutā nṛpāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

## \|\| 91.27 \|\|

*trayodaśasya paryāye raucyākhyasya manoḥ surān \| saptarṣīṃśca nṛpāñścaiva gadato me niśāmaya \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Listen while I tell thee of the Manu's sons and of the seven rishis and of the kings in the turn of the thirteenth

## \|\| 91.28 \|\|

*sudharmāṇaḥ surāstatra sukarmāṇastathāpare \| suśarmāṇaḥ surā hyete samastā munisattama \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Manu named Rauc'ya. The gods therein shall be the Sudharmans, the Su-karmans, and the Su-s'armans the others;

## \|\| 91.29 \|\|

*mahābalo mahāvīryasteṣāmindro divaspatiḥ \| bhaviṣyānatha saptarṣīngadato me niśāmaya \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nirmohaḥ sutapāścānyo niṣprakampaśca saptamaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Now hear while I tell thee of the seven rishis who shall be then - Dhriti-mat, andA-vyaya, Tattva-dars'in, Nir-utsuka, Nirmoha, and Su-tapas another, and Nish-prakampa the

## \|\| 91.31 \|\|

## Chapter 92

## \|\| 92.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ruciḥ prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ nirmamo nirahaṃkṛtaḥ \| yatrāstamitaśāyī ca cacāra pṛthivīmimām \|\| 1 \|\|*

A Prajá-pati named Ruc'i formerly lived in solitary discomfort -His forefathers appeared to him and urged him to marry -He demurred and they insisted on the importance of marriage.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. A Prajá-pati Ruc'i, who was devoid of self, free from pride, fearless and moderate in sleeping, formerly roamed this earth.

## \|\| 92.2 \|\|

*anagnimaniketaṃ tamekāhāramanāśramam \| vimuktasaṅgaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā procustatpitaro munim \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Seeing that he was destitute of fire, had no habitation, that he ate but once a day, had no hermitage, and was cut off from all attachments, his ancestors spoke to him, the muni.

The Pitris spoke:

## \|\| 92.3 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ vatsa kasmāttvayā puṇyo na kṛto dārasaṃgrahaḥ \| svargāpavargahatutvādbandhastenāniśaṃ vinā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Dear son, wherefore hast thou not done the sacred deed of taking a wife, since that is the cause of gaining Svarga and final emancipation from existence? without that there is

## \|\| 92.4 \|\|

*gṛhī samastadevānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca tathārhaṇām \| ṛṣīṇāmatithīnāṃ ca kurvaṃllokānupāśnute \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. bondage perpetually. A house-holder by paying worship to all the gods and the Pitris likewise, to rishis and guests, gains

## \|\| 92.5 \|\|

*svāhoccāraṇato devānsvadhoccāraṇataḥ pitṝn \| vibhajatyannadānena bhūtādyānatithīnapi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. the heavenly worlds. He apportions the gods their share by uttering 'sváhá' aloud, the Pitris by uttering 'svadhá' aloud,

## \|\| 92.6 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ daivādṛṇādbandhaṃ bandhamasmadṛṇādapi \| avāpnoṣi manuṣyarṣibhūtebhyaśca dinedine \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. created beings and other guests by the giving of food. Being such a negligent one, thou dost incur bondage by reason of the debt due to the gods, bondage by reason of the debt due to us also, bondage unto men and created beings day by day,

## \|\| 92.7 \|\|

*anutpādya sutāndevānasantarpya pitṝṃstathā \| bhūtādīṃśca kathaṃ mauḍhyātsugatiṃ gantumicchasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. by not begetting sons, by not satisfying the gods and Pitris. And how, by not fulfilling these duties through folly, dost thou

## \|\| 92.8 \|\|

*kleśamevaihikaṃ putra manyāmo'tra bhavettava \| mṛtasya narakaṃ tadvatkleśamevānyajanmani \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. hope to go the good way? We think affliction, one affliction after another, may be for thee in this world, O son; hell likewise when thou art dead, and affliction in sooth in another birth.

Ruc'i spoke:

## \|\| 92.9 \|\|

*ruciruvāca parigraho'tiduḥkhāya pāpāyādhogatestathā \| bhavatyato mayā pūrvaṃ na kṛto dārasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Wedlock tends to excessive suffering, and is a downward

## \|\| 92.10 \|\|

*ātmanaḥ saṃyamo yo'yaṃ kriyate'kṣaniyantraṇāt \|*  
*sa muktiheturna bhavatyāsāvapi parigrahāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. course toward sin; hence I took no wife hitherto. Control which is gained over one's self, this is effected by firm suppression; it is the cause of final emancipation from existence; that emancipation

## \|\| 92.11 \|\|

*prakṣālyate'nudivasaṃ yadātmā niṣparigrahaiḥ \| mamatvapaṅkadigdho'pi cittāmbhobhirvaraṃ hi tat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. verily comes not from wedlock. That the soul, though besmirched with the mire of selfishness, be washed clean day by day by those who have no family ties with the waters of

## \|\| 92.12 \|\|

*anekabhavasaṃbhūtakarmapaṅkāṃkito budhaiḥ \| ātmā sadvāsanātoyaiḥ prakṣālyo niyatendriyaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. thought -better verily is this! The soul, which is marked with the mire of actions that have developed during many existences, must be washed clean with the waters of good perceptions by wise men who keep their bodily organs under control.

The Pitris spoke:

## \|\| 92.13 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ yuktaṃ prakṣālanaṃ kartumātmano niyatendriyaiḥ \| kintu lepāya mārgo'yaṃ yatra tvaṃ putra vartase \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Fitting it is that those who have their organs under control should cleanse their soul; but does this path, wherein thou wendest, O son, tend to final emancipation from existence?

## \|\| 92.14 \|\|

*pañcarṇadīnairaśubhaṃ nudyate'nabhisandhitaiḥ \| phalaistathopabhogaiśca pūrvakarmaśubhāśubhaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Moreover evil is driven away by means of disinterested gifts, and by results and enjoyments which are good or ill according

## \|\| 92.15 \|\|

*evaṃ na bandho bhavati kurvataḥ kāraṇātmakaḥ \| na ca bandhāya tatkarma bhavatyanabhisandhitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. to former actions. Thus no bondage befalls him who acts with a tender heart, and such action being disinterested tends

## \|\| 92.16 \|\|

*pūrvakarma kṛtaṃ bhogaiḥ kṣīyate'harniśaṃ tathā \| sukhaduḥkhātmakairvatsa puṇyāpuṇyātmakairnṛṇām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. not to bondage. Thus a former action done, which consists of merit and demerit, is diminished day and night by enjoyments which consist of pleasure and pain, O son, among mankind.

## \|\| 92.17 \|\|

*evaṃ prakṣālyate prājñairātmā bandhācca rakṣyate \| na tvevamavivekena pāpapaṅkena lipyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus wise men cleanse their soul and guard it from bonds; thus, on the other hand, indiscrimination, which is the mire of sin, does not lay hold of it.

Ruc'i spoke:

## \|\| 92.18 \|\|

*ruciruvāca avidyā paṭhyate vedaḥ karmamārgaḥ pitāmahāḥ \| tatkathaṃ karmaṇo mārge bhavanto yojayanti mām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It is declared in the Veda, ignorance is the path of action, O my forefathers. How then do ye, sirs, despatch me on the path of action?

The Pitris spoke:

## \|\| 92.19 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ avidyā satyamevaitatkarma naitanmṛṣāvacaḥ \| kintu vidyā pariprāptau hetu karma na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Ignorance in very truth is this action thou mentioned -this maxim is not erroneous; nevertheless action is the cause

## \|\| 92.20 \|\|

*vihitākaraṇātpuṃbhirasadbhiḥ kriyate tu yaḥ \|*  
*saṃyamo muktaye nāsau pratyutā'dhogatipradaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. undoubtedly of full acquisition of knowledge. On that view the restraint, which bad men observe because they do not perform what is enjoined, should tend ultimately to final emancipation from existence; on the contrary it produces a downward

## \|\| 92.21 \|\|

*prakṣālayāmīti bhavānvatsātmānaṃ tu manyate \| vihitākaraṇodbhūtaiḥ pāpaistvaṃ tu vilipyase \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. course. But thou thinkest, O son, 'I will cleanse my soul'; yet thou art burnt up by sins which arise from not performing what

## \|\| 92.22 \|\|

*avidyāpyupakārāya viṣavajjāyate nṛṇām \| anuṣṭhitābhyupāyena bandhāyānyāyato hi sā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. is enjoined. Even Ignorance exists for the benefit of men, just as poison does; although it is different, it does not in truth tend to bondage by reason of the means which are put into

## \|\| 92.23 \|\|

*tasmādvatsa kuruṣva tvaṃ vidhivaddārasaṃgraham \| māṃ janma viphalaṃ te'stu asamprāpya tu laukikam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. practice. Therefore, O son, do thou take a wife according to precept; let not thy birth be unprofitable by thy not observing the business of ordinary life fully.

Ruc'i spoke:

## \|\| 92.24 \|\|

*ruciruvāca vṛddho'haṃ sāmprataṃ ko me pitaraḥ sampradāsyati \| bhāryāṃ tathā daridrasya duṣkaro dārasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I am now aged; who will bestow a wife on me, O my forefathers? Moreover it is hard for a poor man to take a wife.

The Pitris spoke:

## \|\| 92.25 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ asmākaṃ patanaṃ vatsa bhavataścāpyadhogatiḥ \| nūnaṃ bhāvi bhavitrī ca nābhinandasi no vacaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Our downfall will assuredly come to pass, O son, and so also will thy downward course; thou dost not welcome our speech.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 92.26 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityuktvā pitarastasya paśyato munisattama \| babhūvuḥ sahasā'dṛśyā dīpā vātāhatā iva \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Having spoken thus, the Pitris suddenly vanished from sight while he beheld them, O best of munis, just as lights when blown by the wind.

## Chapter 93

## \|\| 93.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sa tena pitṛvākyena bhṛśamudvignamānasaḥ \| kanyābhilāṣī viprarṣiḥ paribabhrāma medinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

Perturbed by his forefathers' admonition Ruc'i offered worship Brahmá, and Brahmá promised he should gain his desire with the Pitris' help -Ruc'i poured forth therefore a long hymn and prayer to the Pitris.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. The bráhman rishi Ruc'i, being greatly agitated in mind at that his forefathers' counsel, wandered about the earth,

## \|\| 93.2 \|\|

*kanyāmalabhamāno'sau pitṛvākyāgnidīpitaḥ \| cintāmavāpa mahatīmatīvodvignamānasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. desirous to find a maiden. Failing to obtain a maiden he, illuminated by the fire of his forefathers' counsel, fell into deep

## \|\| 93.3 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ me dārasaṃgrahaḥ \| kṣipraṃ bhavetpitṝṇāṃ yo mamābhyudayakārakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. thought, while his mind was exceedingly agitated -"What can I do? Where am I going? How am I to take a wife? May that come to pass quickly, which will effect my fore

## \|\| 93.4 \|\|

*iti cintayatastasya matirjātā mahātmanaḥ \| tapasārādhayāmyenaṃ brahmāṇaṃ kamalodbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. fathers' advancement!" While the high-souled muni pondered thus, a thought occurred to him - "I will propitiate

## \|\| 93.5 \|\|

*tato varṣaśataṃ divyaṃ tapastepe sa vedhasam \| didṛkṣuḥ suciraṃ kālaṃ paraṃ niyamamāsthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. lotus-born Brahmá with austerities." Thereupon he performed austerities to Brahmá for a hundred celestial years, and for the purpose of propitiating him engaged then in the

## \|\| 93.6 \|\|

*tataḥ svaṃ darśayāmāsa brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \| uvāca taṃ prasanno'smītyucyatāmabhivāñchitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. utmost self-mortification. Brahmá the forefather of the worlds thereupon showed himself and said to him - "I am

## \|\| 93.7 \|\|

*tato'sau praṇipatyāha brahmāṇaṃ jagato gatim \| pitṝṇāṃ vacanāttena yatkartumabhivāñchitam \| brahmā cāha ruciṃ vipraṃ śrutvā tasyābhivācchitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. well-pleased, declare thy earnest wish." He fell prostrate then before Brahmá, who is the origin of the world, and declared what he wished earnestly to do according to the counsel of his forefathers. And Brahmá hearing his earnest wish spoke to the bráhman Ruc'i.

Brahmá spoke:

## \|\| 93.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca prajāpatistvaṃ bhavitā sraṣṭavyā bhavatā prajāḥ \| sṛṣṭvā prajāḥ sutānvipra samutpādya kriyāstathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thou shalt be a Prajá-pati; thou shalt create human folk. After creating human folk, O bráhman, and begetting sons

## \|\| 93.9 \|\|

*kṛtvā kṛtādhikārastvaṃ tataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi \| sa tvaṃ yathoktaṃ pitṛbhiḥ kuru dāraparigraham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. and performing ceremonies, thou shalt then, after thy dominion shall be taken away, attain perfect felicity. Being such,

## \|\| 93.10 \|\|

*kāmaṃ cemamabhidhyāya kriyatāṃ pitṛpūjanam \|*  
*ta eva tuṣṭāḥ pitaraḥ pradāsyanti tavepsitān \|*  
*patnīṃ sutāṃśca santuṣṭāḥ kiṃ na dadyuḥ pitāmahāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. do thou take a wife as enjoined by thy forefathers; and after reflecting on this desire, perform worship to the Pitris those Pitris indeed being gratified shall bestow on thee the wife and sons desired. When satisfied what may thy ancestors not bestow?

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 93.11 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityṛṣervacanaṃ śrutyā brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \| nadyā vivikte puline cakāra pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The rishi on hearing this speech from Brahmá, whoso birth is inscrutable, performed worship to the Pitris on

## \|\| 93.12 \|\|

*tuṣṭāva ca pitṝnvipraḥ stavairebhistathādṛtaḥ \| ekāgraḥ prayato bhūtvā bhaktinamrātmakandharaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. a distant sand-bank in a river, and also gratified the Pitris, O bráhman, with these praises, respectfully, with single mind, subduing his body, and bending his neck in faith.

Ruc'i spoke:

## \|\| 93.13 \|\|

*ruciruvāca namasye'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhe ye vasantyadhidevatāḥ \| devairapi hi tarpyante ye ca śrāddhe svadhottaraiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I pay reverence unto the Pitris who dwell as presiding deities in the sráddha; and whom even the gods verily delight with invocations concluding with the word svadhá at the

## \|\| 93.14 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnsvarge ye tarpyante maharṣibhiḥ \| śrāddhairmanomayairbhaktyā bhuktimuktimabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. sráddha. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, whom maharshis, who desire to obtain enjoyment and final emancipation from existence, delight with mental sráddhas and with faith in

## \|\| 93.15 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnsvarge siddhāḥ santarpayanti yān \| śrāddheṣu divyaiḥ sakalairupahārairanuttamaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Svarga. I pay reverence Unto the Pitris, Whom the Siddhas delight with all hinds of incomparable heavenly offerings at the

## \|\| 93.16 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnbhaktyā ye'rcyante guhyakairapi \| tanmayatvena vāñchadbhirṛddhimātyantikīṃ parām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. sráddhas in Svarga. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, whom the Guhyakas also, who earnestly desire boundless sublime prosperity because they are absorbed therein, honour with faith.

## \|\| 93.17 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnmartyairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā \| śrāddheṣu śraddhayābhīṣṭalokaprāptipradāyinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, who are always honoured by mortals on the earth, and who grant unto men to attain unto

## \|\| 93.18 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnviprairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā \| vāñchitābhīṣṭālābhāya prājāpatyapradāyinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. the desired worlds by means of faith at the sráddhas. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, who are always honoured by brahmans on the earth, and who grant generative power for

## \|\| 93.19 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnye vai tarpyante'raṇyavāsibhiḥ \| vanyaiḥ śrāddhairyatāhāraistaponirdhūtakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. the obtaining of what they earnestly desire and long for. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, whom indeed forest-dwelling ascetics, who are restrained in their diet and whose stains have been washed away by austerities, delight with sráddhas performed

## \|\| 93.20 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnviprairnaiṣṭhikavratacāribhiḥ \|*  
*ye saṃyatātmabhirnityaṃ santarpyante samādhibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. in the forests. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, whom bráhmans, who practise the vow of perpetual celibate studentship and who have subdued their souls, delight with intense

## \|\| 93.21 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhai rājanyāstarpayanti yān \| kavyairaśeṣairvidhivallokatrayaphalapradān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. meditation continually. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, whom as being bestowers of benefits in the three worlds princes delight with sráddhas and all hinds of food-oblations

## \|\| 93.22 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝnvaiśyairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā \| svakarmābhiratairnityaṃ puṣpadhūpānnavāribhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. according to precept. I pay reverence unto the Pitris, whom vaisyas, who take pleasure in their own occupations, honour with flowers, incense, food and water continually on the earth.

## \|\| 93.23 \|\|

*namasye'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhairye śūdrairapi bhaktitaḥ \| santarpyante jagatyatra nāmnā khyātāḥ sukālinaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

## \|\| 95.1 \|\|

Kraushtuki spoke:

Márkandeya spoke:

18\. Clear sublime Knowledge, Light, Luminosity eternal and free, Perfect Isolation, Understanding, Visible Manifestation,

## \|\| 98.19 \|\|

*bodhaścāvagatiścaiva smṛtirvijñānameva ca \| ityetānīha rūpāṇi tasyārūpasya bhāsvataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tadbibheda tadantaḥstho bhagavānprapitāmahaḥ \| padmayoniḥ svayaṃ brahmā yaḥ sraṣṭā jagatāṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. into existence, an imperishable most potent cause. It split open; within it stood the adorable fore-father, lotus-born Brahmá himself, who is the creator of the worlds, the lord.

*tanmukhādomiti mahānabhūcchabdo mahāmune \| tato bhūstu bhuvastasmāttataśca svaranantaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Out of his mouth issued the great word "Om," O great muni; and then the Bhúr, after that the Bhuvas, and

## \|\| 98.24 \|\|

*etā vyāhṛtayastisraḥ svarūpaṃ tadvivasvataḥ \| omityasmātsvarūpāttu sūkṣmarūpaṃ raveḥ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. immediately thereafter the Svar. These three mystic words therefore express the essential property of the Sun. Now from this essential property indicated by "Om" comes the

## \|\| 98.25 \|\|

*tato mahariti sthūlaṃ janaṃ sthūlataraṃ tataḥ \| tatastapastataḥ satyamiti mūrttāni saptadhā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. subtle sublime form of the Sun. Next there issued the gross Mahar-loka, then the grosser Jana-loka, then the Tapo-loka, then the Satya-loka; - these are the seven-fold substantial

## \|\| 98.26 \|\|

*sthitāni tasya rūpāṇi bhavanti na bhavanti ca \| svabhāvabhāvayorbhāvaṃ yato gacchanti saṃśayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. forms. His permanent forms exist and do not exist, inasmuch as they assuredly come into existence in innate disposition, and in feeling,

*ādyantaṃ yatparaṃ sūkṣmamarūpaṃ paramaṃ sthitam \| omityuktaṃ mayā vipra tatparabrahma tadvapuḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The word "Om" which I have uttered, O bráhman, which has a beginning and an end, which is sublime, subtle, formless, most sublime, permanent -that is the Supreme Spirit, yea his body.

## Chapter 99

## \|\| 99.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tasmādaṇḍādvibhinnāttu brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \| ṛco babhūvuḥ prathamaṃ prathamādvadanānmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya says that from Brahmá's mouths issued the four Vedas and explains their peculiar qualities and transcendent merits -The gods and the Vedas are but manifestations of the Sun.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Now when that egg split open, out of the anterior mouth of Brahmá whose origin is inscrutable, O muni, came forth

## \|\| 99.2 \|\|

*japāpuṣpanibhāḥ sadyastejorūpā hyasaṃhatāḥ \| pṛthakpṛthagvibhinnāśca rajorūpavahāstataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. first the Ric' hymns, at once resplendent as the flowers of the China rose, glorious in form, but disconnected, and divided into separate portions, and therefore bearing the

## \|\| 99.3 \|\|

*yajūṃṣi dakṣiṇādvaktrādaniruddhāni kānicit \| yādṛgvarṇaṃ tathā varṇānyasaṃhatidharāṇi ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. form of passion. Out of his right month issued the Yajus hymns, unimpeded, coloured like the colour of gold, and

## \|\| 99.4 \|\|

*paścimaṃ yadvibhorvaktraṃ brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \| āvirbhūtāni sāmāni tattacchandāṃsi tānyatha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. disconnected. Out of the posterior mouth of the lord Brahmá, who is the highest of all, were revealed the Sáman

## \|\| 99.5 \|\|

*atharvaṇāmaśeṣaṃ ca bhṛṅgāñjanacayaprabham \| yāvaddhorasvarūpaṃ tadābhicārikaśāntikam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. hymns, and the C'handas hymns. And the entire Atharvan then, resplendent as a mass of black pigment or a cluster of bees, -that which has a nature as terrible as possible, which contains the magical rites and the rites for removing

## \|\| 99.6 \|\|

*uttarātprakaṭībhūtaṃ vadanāttasya vedhasaḥ \| sukhasattvatamaḥprāyaṃ saumyāsaumyasvarūpavat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. calamities, - became manifest out of the Creator's left mouth; it is composed chiefly of pleasure, goodness and darkness, and has the essential properties of gentleness and harshness.

## \|\| 99.7 \|\|

*ṛco rajoguṇāḥ sattvaṃ yajuṣāṃ ca guṇā mune \| tamoguṇāni sāmāni tamaḥsattvamatharvasu \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Ric' hymns have the quality of passion; and goodness is the quality of the Yajus hymns, O muni; the Sáman hymns have the quality of darkness; darkness and goodness

*etāni jvalamānāni tejasā'pratimena vai \| pṛthakpṛthagavasthānabhāñji pūrvamivābhavan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. exist in the Atharvan hymns. These emanations, blazing indeed with unrivalled glory, obtained each a separate station almost at first.

## \|\| 99.9 \|\|

*tatastadādyaṃ yatteja omityuktvābhiśabdyate \| tasya svabhāvādyattejastatsamāvṛtya saṃsthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

## \|\| 99.10 \|\|

*yathā yajurmayaṃ tejastadvatsāmnāṃ mahāmune \|*  
*ekatvamupayātāni pare tejasa saṃśraye \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. completely, remains fixed.As is the glory which consists of theYajus, such is that of the Sámans, O great muni; they have

## \|\| 99.11 \|\|

11\. grown into one in resorting to a supreme glory. Rites for the removal of calamities, and rites for promoting growth and magical rites also -these three things gained union with the threeVedas, the Ric' and the two others, O bráhman.

## \|\| 99.12 \|\|

*tato viśvamidaṃ sadyastamonāśātsunirmalam \| vibhāvanīyaṃ viprarṣe tiryagūrdhvamadhastathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This universe became most stainless then through the sudden destruction of darkness, and was to be developed horizontally,

## \|\| 99.13 \|\|

*tatastanmaṇḍalībhūtaṃ chāndasaṃ teja uttamam \| pareṇa tejasā brahmannekatvamupagamya tat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. upwards and downwards, O bráhman rishi. That excellent glory of the C'handas became then an orb, and grew into

## \|\| 99.14 \|\|

*prātarmadhyandine caiva tathā caivāparāhṇike \| trayī tapati sā kāle ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The triple Veda, which is named the Rid,Yajus and Sáman, gives warmth in the morning and at mid-day and in the

*śāntikamṛkṣu pūrvāhṇe yajuḥṣveva ca pauṣṭikam \| vinyastaṃ sāmni sāyāhne hyābhicārikamantataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

## \|\| 99.19 \|\|

*visṛṣṭau ṛṅmayo brahmā sthitau viṣṇuryajurmayaḥ \| rudraḥ sāmamayo'nte ca tasmāttasyāśucirdhvaniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the creation of the world is manifested Brahmá, who is composed of the Ric hymns; in its permanence Vishnu who is composed of the Yajus hymns; and Siva, who is composed of the Sáman, at the dissolution; therefore its

## \|\| 99.20 \|\|

*tadevaṃ bhagavānbhāsvānvedātmā vedasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*vedavidyātmakaścaiva paraḥ puruṣa ucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

21\. knowledge, is called the Supreme Soul.And he, the eternal, who is the cause of creation, permanence and dissolution, on taking recourse to passion, goodness and the other qualities, acquires the names of Brahmá,Vishnu and the other gods.

## \|\| 99.22 \|\|

*devaiḥ sadeḍyaḥ sa tu vedamūrtiramūrtirādyo'khilamartyamūrtiḥ \| viśvāśrayaṃ jyotiravedyadharmā vedāntagamyaḥ paramaḥ pareśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Now ever to be praised by the gods is he whose body is theVeda, Yet who has no body, who was in the beginning, who is embodied in all mortals; Who is the Light that is the refuge of the universe, who has righteousness that passes knowledge, Who is to be attained unto in theVedánta, supreme beyond things that are sublime!

## Chapter 100

## \|\| 100.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tasya santāpyamāne tu tejasordhvamadhasyathā \| sisṛkṣuścintayāmāsa padmayoniḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmá, finding the Sun's glory too great for creation, offered a hymn to the Sun. -The Sun contracted his glory, and Brahmá accomplished the creation.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Now when the egg was being heated by his glory above and beneath, the lotus-born Forefather, being desirous of

## \|\| 100.2 \|\|

*sṛṣṭiḥ kṛtāpi me nāśaṃ prayāsyatyabhitejasā \| bhāsvataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārasthitihetormahātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. creating, pondered -"My creation although accomplished will assuredly pass to destruction through the intense glory of the Sun, who is the cause of creation, dissolution and permanence,

## \|\| 100.3 \|\|

*aprāṇāḥ prāṇinaḥ sarva āpaḥ śuṣyanti tejasā \| na cāmbhasā vinā sṛṣṭirviśvasyāsya bhaviṣyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. great of soul. Breathing beings will all be bereft of breath, the waters will dry up through his glory, and

## \|\| 100.4 \|\|

4\. without water there will be no creation of this universe." Pondering thus the adorable Brahmá, Forefather of the world, becoming intent thereon, composed a hymn to the adorable Sun.

Brahmá spoke:

## \|\| 100.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca namasye yanmayaṃ sarvametatsarvamayaśca yaḥ \| viśvamūrtiḥ paraṃ jyotiryattaddhyāyanti yoginaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I pay reverence to thee of whom everything consists Here, and who consistest of everything; Whose body is the universe, who art the sublime Light Whereon religious devotees meditate; 6 Who art composed of the Ric' hymns, who art the repository of theYajus hymns, And who art the origin of the Sáman hymns; whose power passes thought; Who consistest of the threeVedas; who art half a short syllable as touching grossness Whose nature is sublime, who art worthy of the fullness of good qualities. 7 To thee, the cause of all, who art to be known as supremely worthy of praise, The supreme Light that was at the beginning, not in the form of fire And who art gross by reason that thy spirit is in the gods

\- to thee I pay reverence, The shining one, who wast in the beginning, the sublimest beyond the sublime! 8 Thine is the primeval power, in that urged on thereby I achieve this creation, which is in the forms of water, earth, wind and fire, Which has those elements, the gods and other beings for its objects, and which is complete with the word "Om" and other sounds - Not at my own wish; and that I effect its continuance and dissolution in the self-same manner. 9 Thou verily art fire. By reason of thy drying up of the water thou achievest The creation of the earth and the primeval completion of the worlds. Thou indeed, O lord, pervadest the very form of the sky. Thou, in five ways protectest all this world.

## \|\| 100.10 \|\|

*yajñairyajanti paramātmavido bhavantaṃ viṣṇusvarūpamakhileṣṭimayaṃ vivasvan \| dhyāyanti cāpi yatayo niyatātmacittāḥ sarveśvaraṃ paramamātmavimuktikāmā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They who know the Supreme Soul sacrifice with sacrifices to thee, Who hast the nature of Vishnu, who consistest of all sacrifices, O Sun! And self-subdued ascetics, who curb their souls and thoughts, meditate On thee, the lord of all, the supremest, while they desire final emancipation from existence for themselves. 11 Reverence to thee, whose form is divine; To thee, whose form is sacrifice, be reverence; Yea to thee who in thy very nature art the Supreme Spirit, Who art meditated upon by religious devotees! 12 Contract thy glory, since the abundance of thy glory Tends to obstruct creation, O lord, and I am ready to begin creation!

Márkandeya spoke:

13\. Being praised thus by the Creator Brahmá, the Sun contracted his supreme glory and retained but very little.

14\. And the lotus-born god accomplished the creation of the world. Thus in those intervals of the former kalpas

Brahmá finished the creation -He had a son Maríc'i, who had a son Kas'yapa -Kas'yapa married Daksha's thirteen daughters, and begot by them the gods, demons, mankind, animals, birds, &c. -The gods were subdued by the demons, and Aditi offered a hymn to the Sun, imploring his help.

35\. and afterwards as brilliant and burning, even so I behold thee here on earth a globe of glory. Be gracious; may I see thy form, O maker of day! O thou lord, who hast compassion on thy believers, I believe; protect my sons!

*sṛjasi kamalajanmā pālayasyacyutākhyaḥ kṣapayasi ca yugānte rudrarūpastvamekaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Thou createst it again also in unerring manifestations. Thou art reverenced by mortal beings that move, but art unapproachable by workers of iniquity.

## Chapter 102

## \|\| 102.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ svatejasastasmādāvirbhūto vibhāvasuḥ \| adṛśyata tadādityastaptatāmropamaprabhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Sun revealed himself to Aditi and became her son as Márttanda -This name is explained -Márttanda destroyed the demons and restored the gods to their sovereign positions.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Thereupon from out of that his own glory the Sun revealed himself; the lord, the Sun, appeared then, like unto

## \|\| 102.2 \|\|

3\. "Choose from me the coveted boon that thou desirest." And she, lying prostrate with her head on the ground and pressing the earth with her knees, answered the Sun who present in his very person offered her a boon: -

*deva prasīda putrāṇāṃ hṛtaṃ tribhuvanaṃ mama \| yajñabhāgāśca daityaiśca dānavaiśca balādhikaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

5\. Daityas and the Dánavas who excel them in strength. Do thou, O lord of the heavenly cattle, bestow on me favour for that purpose; with a portion of thyself enter thou into brotherhood

*yathā me tanayā bhūyo yajñabhāgabhujaḥ prabho \| bhaveyuradhipāścaiva trailokyasya divākara \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. with them and destroy their enemies. In order that my sons may again partake of the shares of the sacrifices, O lord,

Márkandeya spoke:

*ityuktvā bhagavānbhāsvānantarddhānamupāgamat \|*  
*nivṛttā sāpi tapasaḥ saṃtṛptākhilavāñchitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Having spoken thus the adorable Sun vanished from her sight; and she ceased from her austerities, having gained all

*tato raśmisahasrāttu sauṣumnākhyo raveḥ karaḥ \| viprāvatāraṃ saṃcakre devamāturathodare \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. her desire. Thereupon the Sun's ray called Sausumna from out of his thousand rays became incarnate in the womb of

## \|\| 102.12 \|\|

*tato yuddhāya daiteyānājuhāva śatakratuḥ \| saha devairmudā yukto dānavāśca samabhyayuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

25\. were reduced to ashes. Thereupon all the dwellers in heaven experienced unparalleled joy, and praised Márttanda

26\. the source of splendour and also Aditi; moreover they regained their own spheres of dominion and their shares of the sacrifices as before; and the adorable Márttanda also exercised

## Chapter 103

## \|\| 103.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atha tasmai dadau kanyāṃ saṃjñāṃ nāma vivasvate \| prasādya praṇato bhūtvā viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The Sun married Visva-karman's daughter Sanjná and had three children by her, Manu Vaivasvata, Yama and Yamuná -Sanjná could not endure the Sun's glory and leaving her shadow C'háyá departed -C'háyá-Sanjná took her place and had three children by the Sun -She cursed Yama for unfilial conduct, but the Sun minimised the curse and perceived the deception. -The Sun visited Visva-karman and the latter placing the Sun on his wheel pared down his glory -The world was thrown into chaos as the Sun was whirled around -The gods and celestial beings hymned the Sun.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Now the Prajá-pati Visva-karman, after falling prostrate and propitiating him, gave his daughter named Sanjná to

## \|\| 103.2 \|\|

*vaivasvatastu sambhūto manustasyāṃ vivasvataḥ \| pūrvameva tathākhyātaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. the Sun, Vivasvat. Manu Vaivasvata was begotten by Vivasvat of her then, and his nature has been already indeed

## \|\| 103.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca trīṇyapatyānyasau tasyāṃ janayāmāsa gopatiḥ \| dvau putrau sumahābhāgo kanyāṃ ca yamunāṃ mune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. declared particularly. He, Vivasvat, lord of the heavenly cattle, begot three children of her, two most illustrious sons

## \|\| 103.5 \|\|

5\. then were bornYama andYamí as twins. With the exceeding splendour that Márttanda Vivasvat possessed, he scorched the three worlds and the moveable and immoveable things

*golākāraṃ tu taddṛṣṭvā saṃjñārūpaṃ vivasvataḥ \| asahantī mahattejaḥ svāṃ chāyāṃ prekṣya sā'bravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. therein very grievously. But Sanjná saw Vivasvat's globelike form and, being impatient of his great splendour, gazed at her own shadow C'háyá and spoke: -

Sanjná spoke:

## \|\| 103.7 \|\|

*saṃjñovāca ahaṃ yāsyāmi bhadraṃ te svameva bhavanaṃ pituḥ \| nirvikāraṃ tvayāpyatra stheyaṃ macchāsanācchubhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Fare thee well! I will go to my father's very own abode. Yet thou must stay here without change at my command, O

## \|\| 103.8 \|\|

*imau ca bālakau mahyaṃ kanyā ca varavarṇinī \| sambhāvyau naiva cākhyeyamidaṃ bhagavate tvayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. fair one; and thou must show honour to these two boys for me and to this daughter who is of noble rank; and thou must not declare this at all to the god.

C'háyá the Shadow spoke:

## \|\| 103.9 \|\|

*chāyovāca ākeśagrahaṇāddevi āśapannaiva karhicit \| ākhyāsyāmi mataṃ tubhyaṃ gamyatāṃ yatra vāñchitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. "Unto enduring the seizing of my hair, unto undergoing curses, O goddess, I will never declare thy intention; go where thou wishest."

## \|\| 103.10 \|\|

*ityuktā chāyayā saṃjñā jagāma pitṛmandiram \|*  
*tatrāvasatpiturgehe kañcitkālaṃ śubhekṣaṇā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Being addressed thus by C'háyá, Sanjná went to her father's dwelling; and there she, the beautiful of eyes,

## \|\| 103.11 \|\|

C'háyá spoke:

*chāyovāca*  
*padā tarjayase yasmātpitṛbhāryāṃ garīyasīm \|*  
*tasmāttavaiva caraṇaḥ patiṣyati na saṃśaya \|\| 20 \|\|*

15\. And the second was "Yama" because of the curse, and he was "The Righteous-eyed" because of his father's favour. Now he was calledYama as having been greatly afflicted in

## \|\| 105.21 \|\|

*evamapyāha ca tato bhagavāṃllokabhāvitaḥ \| tvamapyaśeṣalokasya pūjyo vatsa bhaviṣyasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yavīyasī tu yā kanyā''dityasyābhūddvijottama \| abhavatsā saricchreṣṭhā tapatī lokapāvanī \|\| 26 \|\|*

29\. of the Sun's majesty, may obtain deliverance when he falls into calamity and may gain great fame. This story of the majesty of the primeval god, the high-souled Márttanda, when listened to, quells the sin that has been committed by day or night.

## Chapter 106

## \|\| 106.1 \|\|

*krauṣṭukiruvāca bhagavankathitaḥ samyagbhānoḥ santatisambhavaḥ \| māhātmyamādidevasya svarūpaṃ cātivistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya tells the story of king Rájya-vardhana. After the king had reigned many years, his queen sorrowed over finding a grey hair in his head -He comforted her add resolved to depart to the forest -His vassals and subjects tried to dissuade him and in vain - They performed many austerities in order to propitiate the Sun and went to Káma-rúpa and continued their worship -At length the Sun appeared to them in bodily shape.

Kraushtuki spoke:

1\. Adorable Sir! thou hast well declared the birth of the Sun's offspring, the majesty of the primeval god and his nature

## \|\| 106.2 \|\|

*bhūyo'pi bhāsvataḥ samyaṅmāhātmyaṃ munisattama \| śrotumicchāmyahaṃ tanme prasanno vaktumarhasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. at very full length. Nevertheless I desire, O best of munis, to hear more about the Sun's majesty comprehensively; deign therefore with favour to tell me of it.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 106.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca śrūyatāmādidevasya māhātmyaṃ kathayāmi te \| vivasvato yaccakāra pūrvamārādhito janaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Be it heard then! I tell thee of the majesty of the primeval god, Vivasvat, what he did formerly when worshipped by mankind.

## \|\| 106.4 \|\|

*damasya putro vikhyāto rājābhūdrājyavardhanaḥ \| sa samyakpālanaṃ cakre pṛthivyā pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was a famous king, Dama's son, named Rájya-vardhana; he, lord of the earth, kept the earth well protected.

## \|\| 106.5 \|\|

*dharmataḥ pālyamānaṃ tu tena rāṣṭraṃ mahātmanā \| vavṛdhe'nudinaṃ vipra janena ca dhanena ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Now the realm, being protected by that high-souled monarch in righteousness, increased day by day in people and wealth, O

## \|\| 106.6 \|\|

*hṛṣṭapuṣṭamatīvāsīttasminrājanyaśeṣataḥ \| nirbhayaḥ sakalaścorvyāṃ paurajānapado janaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. bráhman. And joyous and thriving exceedingly were all the subordinate kings on the earth without exception, while he was king; and so also were his people, both town and country

## \|\| 106.7 \|\|

*nopasargo na ca vyādhirna ca vyālodbhavaṃ bhayam \| na cāvṛṣṭibhayaṃ tatra damaputre mahīpatau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. folk. No portent visited them, nor sickness, nor the fear that comes from serpents, nor was there fear of drought there,

## \|\| 106.8 \|\|

*sa īje ca mahāyajñairdadau dānāni cārthinām \| sudharmasyāvirodhena bubhuje viṣayānapi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. while Dama's son was king. And he offered up great sacrifices, and gave gifts to those who asked; he enjoyed even the pleasures of sense without hindrance to true righteousness.

## \|\| 106.9 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ kurvato rājyaṃ samyakpālayataḥ prajāḥ \| sapta varṣasahasrāṇi jagmurekamaharyathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. While he ruled the kingdom thus and protected his people duly, seven thousand years passed away as if a single day.

## \|\| 106.10 \|\|

*vidūrathasya tanayā dākṣiṇātyasya bhūbhṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya patnī babhūvātha māninī nāma māninī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Now the daughter of Vidúratha, king of the South, was his

## \|\| 106.11 \|\|

*kadācittasya sā subhruḥ śiraso'bhyañjanādṛtā \| paśyato rājalokasya mumocāśrūṇi māninī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. queen, Mániní by name and high-spirited indeed. One day she, the fine-browed noble lady, shed tears when his head had not been dressed with ointment, in the sight of the king's

## \|\| 106.12 \|\|

*tadaśrubindavo gātre yadā tasya mahīpateḥ \| tadā vīkṣyāśruvadanāṃ tāmapṛcchata māninīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. folk. When her tear-drops fell on the king's body, he saw Mániní was of tearful countenance then and questioned her.

## \|\| 106.13 \|\|

*niḥśabdamaśrumokṣeṇa rudantīṃ tāṃ vilokya vai \| kimetaditi papraccha māninīṃ rājyavardhanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In sooth beholding her weeping and shedding tears silently,

## \|\| 106.14 \|\|

*pṛṣṭā sā tu tatastena bhartrā prāha manasvinī \| na kiñciditi tāṃ bhūyaḥ papraccha sa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Rájya-vardhana asked Mániní, "Why is this?" But she, being prudent, when questioned by her husband, replied then,

## \|\| 106.15 \|\|

*bahuśaḥ pṛcchatastasya bhūbhṛtaḥ sā sumadhyamā \| (na kiñciditi hovāca sā bhūyo rājyavardhanam \| kimetaditi papraccha māninīṃ pārthivaḥ punaḥ \| bahuśaḥ preritā tena sā bhartrā tatra bhāminī \|) darśayāmāsa palitaṃ keśabhārāntarodbhavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. "It is nothing." The king questioned her again. And after the king had questioned her often, she, the slender-waisted lady, showed him a grey hair growing among his abundant

## \|\| 106.16 \|\|

*etatpaśyeti bhūpāla kimanyanmanyukāraṇam \| mamātimandabhāgyāyā jahāsātha nṛpastataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. locks. "Look at this, O king; is this a cause of vexation to me, most luckless that I am?" And the king laughed thereat.

## \|\| 106.17 \|\|

*sa vihasyāha tāṃ patnīṃ śṛṇvatāṃ sarvabhūbhṛtām \| paurāṇāṃ ca mahīpālā ye tatrāsansamāvṛtāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With a smile quoth he to his wife -while listened all the kings and citizens, and the kings who were assembled there -

## \|\| 106.18 \|\|

*śokenālaṃ viśālākṣi roditavyaṃ na te śubhe \| janmarddhipariṇāmādyā vikārāḥ sarvajantuṣu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. "Away with grief, O wide-eyed lady! thou must not weep, pretty one! Birth, growth, decline of life and other changes

## \|\| 106.19 \|\|

*adhītāḥ sakalā vedā iṣṭā yajñāḥ sahasraśaḥ \| dattaṃ dvijānāṃ putrāśca samutpannā varānane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. befall all living beings. I have studied all the Vedas; I have offered sacrifices by thousands; I have given alms to bráhmans; and I have begotten sons, O lady of finest countenance;

*bhuktā bhogastvayā sārddhaṃ ye martyairatidurlabhāḥ \|*  
*sabhyañca pālitā pṛthvī śauryaṃ yuddheṣvanuṣṭhitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I have enjoyed along with thee pleasures which are very hardly attainable by mortals; and I have protected the earth

## \|\| 106.21 \|\|

*mitraiḥ saheṣṭairhasitaṃ vihṛtaṃ ca vanāntare \| kimanyatra kṛtaṃ bhadre palitebhyo bibheṣi yat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. well; I have borne myself ably in battles; I have laughed with my beloved friends; and I have sported in the heart of the woods. What else is there which I have not done,

## \|\| 106.22 \|\|

*bhavantu keśāḥ palitā valayaḥ santu me śubhe \| śaithilyametu me kāyaḥ kṛtakṛtyo'smi mānini \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. that thou art frightened at grey hairs, O lady? Let my hair become grey; let wrinkles come to me, O beauteous one; let my body pass into weakness; for I have been successful, O

## \|\| 106.23 \|\|

*mūrdhni yaddarśitaṃ bhadre bhavatyā palitaṃ mama \| cikitsāmeva tasyāhaṃ karomi vanasaṃśrayāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Mániní! Because thou hast shown me a grey hair on my head, O lady, here then I take medical treatment therefore

## \|\| 106.24 \|\|

*bālye bālakriyāpūrvaṃ tadvatkaumārake ca yā \| yauvane cāpi yā yogyā vārddhake vanasaṃśrayā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. through resorting to the forest. First in childhood there is childhood's action; similarly there is action which is natural in youth; and also such as is fitting in early manhood; in old

## \|\| 106.25 \|\|

*evaṃ matpūrvajairbhadre kṛtaṃ tvatpūrvajaiśca yat \| ato na te'śrupātasya kiñcitpaśyāmi kāraṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. age there is resort to the forest. Since those who lived before me did so, lady, and also those who lived before them, I see no reason whatever then for thee to shed tears.Away

## \|\| 106.26 \|\|

*alaṃ te manyunā bhadre nanvabhyudayakāri me \| darśanaṃ palitasyāsya mā rodīrniṣprayojanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. with thy vexation! Does not the sight of this grey hair cause me elevation?Weep not; it is futile."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 106.27 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ praṇamya taṃ bhūpāḥ paurāścaiva samīpagāḥ \| sāmnā procurmahīpālā maharṣe rājyavardhanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the kings and citizens who were in his presence did him reverence, and the kings addressed Rájya-vardhana with conciliatory words, O great rishi: -

## \|\| 106.28 \|\|

*na roditavyamanayā tava patnyā narādhipa \| roditavyamihāsmābhirathavā sarvajantubhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. "It is not for thee to weep with this thy wife, O king; it is

## \|\| 106.29 \|\|

*tvaṃ bravīṣi yathā nātha vanavāsāśritaṃ vacaḥ \| patanti tena naḥ prāṇā lālitānāṃ tvayā nṛpa \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. we who must weep here, or rather all living beings. Since thou, O master, speakest the word indicating that thou wilt dwell in the forest, life falls therefore from us who have been

## \|\| 106.30 \|\|

*sarve yāsyāmahe bhūpa yadi yāti bhavānvanam \|*  
*tato'śeṣakriyāhāniḥ sarvapṛthvīnivāsinām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. tenderly cherished by thee, O king. We will all go, O king, if thou goest to the forest. All the inhabitants of the earth

## \|\| 106.31 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati na sandehastvayi nātha vanāśrame \| sā ca dharmopaghātāya yadi tatpravimucyatām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. will thereby suffer loss in all their ceremonies without doubt, when thou, O master, shalt take up thy abode in the forest; and if that loss tends to injure righteousness, let that course

*sapta varṣasahasrāṇi tvayeyaṃ pālitā mahī \| tatsamutthaṃ mahāpuṇyamālokaya narādhipa \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. he discarded. Seven thousand years this earth has been guarded by thee; have regard, O king, to the great merit that

## \|\| 106.33 \|\|

*vane vasanmahārāja tvaṃ kariṣyasi yattapaḥ \| tanmahīpālanasyāsya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. has accrued therefrom! The austerities, which thou, O great king, wilt perform while dwelling in the forest, are not worth the sixteenth part of this thy guardianship over the earth!"

The king spoke:

## \|\| 106.34 \|\|

*rājovāca sapta varṣasahasrāṇi mayeyaṃ pālitā mahī \| idānīṃ vanavāsasya mama kālo'yamāgataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. "Seven thousand years I have protected this earth; now

## \|\| 106.35 \|\|

*mamāpatyāni jātāni dṛṣṭvā me'patyasantatīḥ \| svalpairevamahobhirme hyantako na sahiṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. this my time has come to dwell in the forest. I have begotten children. Now that I have seen my children and their descendants, Death truly will not allow me a very few days.

## \|\| 106.36 \|\|

*yadetatpalitaṃ mūrdhni tadvijānīta nāgarāḥ \| dūtabhūtamanāryasya mṛtyoratyugrakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Understand, O citizens, that this grey hair on my head has become a messenger from ignoble Death, who is very sharp

## \|\| 106.37 \|\|

*so'haṃ rājye sutaṃ kṛtvā bhogāṃstyaktvā vanāśrayaḥ \| tapastapsye samāyānti na yāvadyamasainikāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. in his actions. Being such, I will place my son in my kingdom, and abandon Worldly pleasures, and will, as a dweller in the forest, perform austerities until Yama's troops arrive for me."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 106.38 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato yiyāsuḥ sa vanaṃ daivajñānavanīpatiḥ \| putrarājyā'bhiṣekāya dinalagnānyapṛcchata \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Being desirous of departing to the forest the king then enquired of the astrologers about the best days and moments for

## \|\| 106.39 \|\|

*śrutvā ca te tu nṛpatervaco vyākulacetasaḥ \| dinaṃ lagnaṃ ca horāśca na viduḥ śāstradṛṣṭayaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. anointing his son in the kingdom.And on hearing the king's speech they became confused in mind; they who were skilled in the scriptures knew not the day nor moment nor the hours.

## \|\| 106.40 \|\|

*ūcuśca taṃ mahīpālaṃ daivajñā bāṣpagadgadam \|*  
*jñānāni naḥ praṇaṣṭāni śrutvaitatte vaco nṛpa \|\| 40 \|\|*

## \|\| 106.41 \|\|

*tato'nyanagarebhyaśca bhṛtyai rāṣṭrebhya eva ca \| tatastasmācca nagarātprācuryeṇābhyupāgaman \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then people came in a multitude both from other cities and also from dependent countries, and next from that city.

## \|\| 106.42 \|\|

*samutpatya mahīpālaṃ taṃ yiyāsuṃ mune vanam \| prakampiśiraso bhūtvā procurbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Springing up, O muni, the most eminent bráhmans, their heads' quivering with emotion, addressed the king who desired to

## \|\| 106.43 \|\|

*prasīda pāhi no rājanpālitāḥ sma yathā purā \| sīdiṣyatyakhilo lokastvayi bhūpa vanāśraye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. depart to the forest; -"Be gracious! Protect us, O king, as we have been protected a long time past. The whole world will sink down, when thou, O king, hast betaken thyself to

## \|\| 106.44 \|\|

44\. the forest. Do thou then so act, O king, that the world sink not. And while we, such as we cure, live our very short time, O hero, we desire not to see the regal throne deprived of thee, O lord."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 106.45 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityevaṃ taistathānyaiśca dvijaiḥ paurapuraḥsaraiḥ \| bhūpairbhṛtyairamātyaiśca rājā proktaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus both they and other dvijas heading the citizens, and kings, dependants and ministers appealed to him, and appealed

## \|\| 106.46 \|\|

*vanavāsavinirbandhaṃ nopasaṃharate yadā \| kṣamiṣyatyantako neti dadau sa ca tadottaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. again and again; but when he does not withdraw his determination to take up his abode in the forest, and returns them

## \|\| 106.47 \|\|

*tato'mātyāśca bhūpāśca pauravṛddhāstathā dvijāḥ \| sametya mantrayāmāsuḥ kimatra kriyatāmiti \|\| 47 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ mantrayatāṃ vipra niścayo'yamajāyata \| anurāgavatāṃ tatra mahīpāle'tidhārmike \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. here?" While they took counsel, O bráhman, this resolution developed there among those who were devotedly attached

## \|\| 106.49 \|\|

## \|\| 106.50 \|\|

*tatraikaniścayāḥ kārye kecidgehe ca bhāskaram \|*  
*samyagarghopacārādyairupahārairapūjayan \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Being all resolved alike there on that object, some of them, paid adoration to the Sun with their own bodies, by presenting to him the argha offering and presents and other oblations in due

## \|\| 106.51 \|\|

*apare maunino bhūtvā ṛgjāpena tathāpare \| yajuṣāmatha sāmnāṃ ca toṣayāñcakrire ravim \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. course; others gratified the Sun by maintaining silence; and

## \|\| 106.52 \|\|

*apare ca nirāhārā nadīpulinaśāyinaḥ \| tapāṃsi cakruricchaṃto bhāskarārādhanaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*
