## \|\| 106.53 \|\|

*agnihotraparāścānye ravisūktānyaharniśam \| jepustatrāpare tasthurbhāskare nyastadṛṣṭayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. and others, applying themselves to the oblation to Fire, day and night repeated hymns composed to the Sun; others

## \|\| 106.54 \|\|

*ityevamatinirbandhaṃ bhāskarārādhanaṃ prati \| bahuprakāraṃ cakruste taṃ taṃ vidhimupāśritāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. casting their eyes on the Sun remained standing there. Even thus, applying themselves to those several rites, did they work in manifold ways with exceeding determination in order to propitiate the Sun.

## Chapter 107

## \|\| 107.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ prasanno bhagavānbhānurāhākhilāñjanān \| vriyatāṃ yadabhipretaṃ mattaḥ prāptuṃ dvijādayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

King Rájya-vardhana's subjects besought of the Sun that the king might reign ten thousand years more, and the Sun granted it -But the king, distressed that the boon did not include all his family and subjects, went and propitiated the Sun, and at length gained his desire - This story is commented on and its merits are extolled.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Well-pleased then, the adorable Sun said to all the populace " Choose, O ye dvijas and other people, what ye have wished to obtain from me!"

## \|\| 107.2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataste praṇipatyocurviprakṣatrādayo janāḥ \| sasādhvasamaśītāṃśumavalokya puraḥ sthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Thereupon those bráhmans and other people gazing in fear on the fiery-rayed Sun, as he stood before them, prostrated themselves and said, O bráhman: -

The people spoke:

## \|\| 107.3 \|\|

*prajā ūcuḥ bhagavanyadi no bhaktyā prasannastimirāpaha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Prostrating themselves they said then to the lord of the world who proffered them a boon - "O adorable Dispeller of

## \|\| 107.4 \|\|

*daśa varṣasahasrāṇi tato no jīvatāṃ nṛpaḥ \| nirāmayo jitārātiḥ sukośaḥ sthirayauvanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. darkness, if thou art pleased with our faith, then let our king live ten thousand years, free from sickness, victorious over his enemies, rich in his treasury, and with firmly-enduring youth! May Rájya-vardhana live ten thousand years!"

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 107.5 \|\|

## \|\| 107.6 \|\|

## \|\| 107.43 \|\|

*suvarṇaśṛṅgīmatiśobhanāṅgīṃ payasvinīṃ gāṃ pradadāti yo hi \| śṛṇoti caitattryahamātmavānnaraḥ samaṃ tayoḥ puṇyaphalaṃ dvijāgrya \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. sublime majesty in thy mind and must mutter it over. Verily he who makes a gift of a milch cow with gilded horns and most handsome body, and the man who self-possessed listens to this poem for three days -equal are the merit and reward of them both, O bráhman!

## Chapter 108

## \|\| 108.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evaṃprabhāvo bhagavānanādinidhano raviḥ \| yasya tvaṃ krauṣṭuke bhaktyā māhātmyaṃ paripṛcchasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Manu had seven sons, whose names are mentioned and also a child, who was born as a daughter named Ilá, and afterwards became a man by name Su-dyumna -This child as Ilá had a son Purúravas, who reigned at Pratishthána, and as Su-dyumna had three sons.

Márkandeya spoke:

2\. dost ask me in faith. He is the Supreme Soul among religious devotees who meditate deeply on the dissolution of their intellects; he is the Conscious Soul among those who apply the Sánkhya doctrine to the knowledge of spirit; and he is the Lord of sacrifice among those who are sacrificers:

## \|\| 108.3 \|\|

*sūryādhikāraṃ vahato viṣṇorīśasya vedhasaḥ \| manustasyābhavatputraśchinnasarvārthasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

## \|\| 108.5 \|\|

5\. and prowess -and Narishyanta, Nábhága, Púshadhra and Dhrishta; these were that Manu's sons, each the guardian of

*vikhyātakīrttayaḥ sarve sarve śastrāstrapāragāḥ \| viśiṣṭataramanvicchanmanuḥ putraṃ tathā punaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. a separate kingdom. All were celebrated in fame, all had the utmost skill in arms and weapons. Seeking yet again for a son who should be more distinguished,

## \|\| 108.7 \|\|

*mitrāvaruṇayoriṣṭiṃ cakāra kṛtināṃ varaḥ \| yatra cāpahute hoturapacārānmahāmune \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Manu, best of the skilful ones, offered a sacrifice to Mitra and Varuna; in which sacrifice moreover when the offering was perversely made through the improper conduct of the priest,

*ilā nāma samutpannā manoḥ kanyā sumadhyamā \| tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyakāṃ tatra samutpannāṃ tato manuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O great muni, a daughter was born to Manu named Ilá, slender of waist. On seeing that daughter born there, Manu

\- "When I made the sacrifice with the prayer, 'Through 10 your favour may I obtain a distinguished son,' a daughter was born to me who am wise. If ye being gracious grant me a

14\. her a son named Pururavas who was a mighty universal monarch. When that son was born, Su-dyumna again

*puruṣatvamanuprāptaḥ sudyumnaḥ pārthivo'bhavat \| sudyumnasya trayaḥ putrā utkalo vinayo gayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

18\. during his womanhood, got no share of the earth, because he was Budha's son. Thereupon at Vasishtha's word Pratishthána, an excellent city, was given to him; he became king in that exceedingly charming city.

## Chapter 109

## \|\| 109.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca pṛṣadhrākhyo manoḥ putro mṛgayāmagamadvanam \| tatra caṃkramamāṇo'sau vipine nirjane vane \|\| 1 \|\|*

Manu's son Púshadhra while hunting accidentally killed a bráhman's cow -The bráhman's son fell into a rage and cursed him -The bráhman reproved his son or his passionate conduct, but the curse could not be altered and Púshadhra became a súdra.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Manu's son who was named Púshadhra went a-hunting to a forest. While walking about in that dense lonely forest he

## \|\| 109.2 \|\|

*nāsasāda mṛgaṃ kañcidbhānudīdhititāpitaḥ \| kṣuttṛṭtāpaparītāṅgaḥ itaścetaśca caṃkraman \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. lighted upon no deer at all, he was scorched by the sun's rays, and his body was seized with hunger, thirst and heat as he

## \|\| 109.3 \|\|

*sa dadarśa tadā tatra homadhenuṃ manoharām \| latāntardehachinnārdhāṃ brāhmaṇasyāgnihotriṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. walked hither and thither. Then he saw there a beautiful cow which yielded milk for sacrifice, belonging to a bráhman who maintained the sacrificial fire, half the body of which was

## \|\| 109.4 \|\|

*sa manyamāno gavayamiṣuṇā tāmatāḍayat \| papāta sāpi tadbāṇavibhinnahṛdayā bhuvi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. hidden among creepers. Thinking she was a gayál, he shot her with an arrow, and she fell to the earth, pierced to the heart

## \|\| 109.5 \|\|

*tato'gnihotriṇaḥ putro brahmacārī taporatiḥ \| śaptavānsa piturdṛṣṭvā homadhenuṃ nipātitām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. with the arrow. Thereupon the sacrificial priest's son Taporati, who was a religious student, on seeing his father's

## \|\| 109.6 \|\|

*gopālaḥ preṣitaḥ putro bābhravyo nāma nāmataḥ \| kopāmarṣaparādhīnacittavṛttistato mune \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. sacrificial cow stricken down cursed him; and sent forward his son named Vábhravya who tended the cow, Then, O muni, his

## \|\| 109.7 \|\|

*cukopa vigalatsvedajalalolāvilekṣaṇaḥ \| taṃ kruddhaṃ prekṣya sa nṛpaḥ pṛṣadhro munidārakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. mental feelings were overcome by wrath and resentment, and he fell into a rage, while his eyes rolled and were blurred with drops of perspiration that trickled down. The king Púshadhra seeing

## \|\| 109.8 \|\|

*prasīdeti jagau kasmācchūdravatkuruṣe ruṣam \| na kṣatriyo na vā vaiśya evaṃ krodhamupaiti vai \| yathā tvaṃ śūdravajjāto viśiṣṭe brahmaṇaḥ kule \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. that muni's son enraged said, -"Be gracious, wherefore dost thou give way to anger like a súdra. No kshatriya, no vaisya in truth indulges so in wrath as thou dost like a súdra, thou who art born in the noble family of a bráhman."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 109.9 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca iti nirbhatsitastena sa rājñā maulinaḥ sutaḥ \| śaśāpa taṃ durātmānaṃ śūdra eva bhaviṣyasi \|\| 9 \|\|*

9.When that son of a pre-eminent bráhman was upbraided thus by the king, he cursed the evil-souled king, saying: "Thou

## \|\| 109.10 \|\|

*prayāsyati kṣayaṃ brahmanyatte'dhītaṃ gurormukhāt \|*  
*homadhenurmama guroryadiyaṃ hiṃsitā tvayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. shalt become a súdra indeed! Whatever sacred lore thou hast learnt from thy guru's mouth shall waste away, because thou hast hurt this my guru's sacrificial cow."

## \|\| 109.11 \|\|

*evaṃ śapto nṛpaḥ kruddhastacchāpaparipīḍitaḥ \| pratiśāpaparo vipra toyaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When cursed thus the king became angry, yet he was tormented greatly by that curse. He took water up in his hand,

## \|\| 109.12 \|\|

*so'pi rājño vināśāya kopaṃ cakre dvijottamaḥ \| tamabhyetya tvarāyukto vārayāmāsa vai pitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. intent on cursing the other in retaliation, O bráhman. That bráhman also gave way to wrath in order to destroy the king. His father approached him hastily and forbad him in sooth, saying -

## \|\| 109.13 \|\|

*vatsālamalamatyarthaṃ kopenātīva vairiṇā \| aihikāmuṣmikahitaḥ śama eva dvijanmanām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. "My son, enough, more than enough, of wrath which does not counteract hostility! Verily calmness is beneficial to the twice-born in things of this world and of the next

## \|\| 109.14 \|\|

*kopastapo nāśayati kruddho bhraśyatyathāyuṣaḥ \| kruddhasya galate jñānaṃ kruddhaścārthācca hīyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. world. Anger destroys austerities; and the angry man falls away from long life; the angry man's knowledge melts away,

## \|\| 109.15 \|\|

*na dharmaḥ krodhaśīlasya nārthaṃ cāpnoti roṣaṇaḥ \| nālaṃ sukhāya kāmāsti kopenāviṣṭacetasām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. and the angry man fails of his object also. There is no righteousness in the man of angry disposition; and the passionate man obtains not his object; nor among those whose minds are possessed by wrath is the obtaining of their wishes enough for

## \|\| 109.16 \|\|

*yadi rājñā hatā dhenuriyaṃ vijñāninā satā \| yuktamatra dayāṃ kartumātmano hitabodhinā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. happiness. If the king has killed this cow with his full knowledge, it is right for one, who perceives what is for his own

## \|\| 109.17 \|\|

*athavā'jānatā dhenuriyaṃ vyāpāditā mama \| tatkathaṃ śāpayogyo'yaṃ duṣṭaṃ nāsya mano yataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. benefit, to extend pardon here. Or if he has slain this my cow in ignorance, how then is he worthy of a curse, since his

## \|\| 109.18 \|\|

*ātmano hitamanvicchanbādhate yo'paraṃ naraḥ \| kartavyā mūḍhavijñāne dayā tatra dayālubhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. mind was not evil? Whatever man, while seeking his own good, harasses another - merciful men should shew pardon to

## \|\| 109.19 \|\|

*ajñānataḥ kṛte daṇḍaṃ pātayanti budhā yadi \| budhebhyastamahaṃ manye varamajñānino narāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. that man in the knowledge that he is benighted. If wise men inflict punishment for what is done by a man in ignorance, I esteem him more than the wise men; better are the men

## \|\| 109.20 \|\|

*nādya śāpastvayā deyaḥ pārthivasyāsya putraka \|*  
*svakarmaṇaiva patitā gaureṣā duḥkhamṛtyunā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. who are ignorant. Invoke thou no curse now on this king, my son; by her own action indeed this cow has fallen in a painful death."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 109.21 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca pṛṣadhro'pi muneḥ putraṃ praṇamyānamrakandharaḥ \| prasīdeti jagādoccairajñānādghātiteti ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Púshadhra also, prostrating himself with bowed neck before the muni's son, exclaimed aloud, "Be gracious!" and "She

## \|\| 109.22 \|\|

*mayā gavayabuddhyā gauravadhyā ghātitā mune \| ajñānāddhomadhenuste prasīda tvaṃ ca no mune \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. was slain by me in ignorance, for I thought she was a gayál; a cow must not be killed; through ignorance, O muni, I slew thy sacrificial cow. Be thou also gracious to me, O muni!"

The rishi's son spoke:

## \|\| 109.23 \|\|

*ṛṣiputra uvāca ājanmano mahīpāla na mayā vyāhataṃ mṛṣā \| krodhaścādya mahābhāga nānyathā me kadācana \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Since my birth, O king, I have uttered nothing in vain, and my anger this day can never be altered, illustrious sir.

## \|\| 109.24 \|\|

*tannāhamenaṃ śaknomi śāpaṃ kartuṃ nṛpānnyathā \| yaste samudyataḥ śāpo dvitīyaḥ sa nivartitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Therefore I cannot make this curse otherwise, O king; but the second curse which was prepared for thee is averted.

## \|\| 109.25 \|\|

*ityuktavantaṃ taṃ bālamādāya sa pitā tataḥ \| jagāma svāśramaṃ so'pi pṛṣadhraḥ śūdratāmagāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The father then took the son who had spoken thus and went to his own hermitage. And Púshadhra in sooth became a súdra.

## Chapter 110

## \|\| 110.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca kāruṣāḥ kṣatriyāḥ śūrāḥ karuṣasyābhavansutāḥ \| te tu saptaśataṃ vīrāstebhyaścānye sahasraśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Karusha's descendants were the Kárushas -Dishta's son was Nábhága; Nábhága wanted to marry a vaisya maiden -Her father referred the matter to the king Dishta, and the king consulted the rishis -They declared the prince might marry her, provided he first married a kshatriya maiden -He spurned that and took her -The king tried to vanquish him by force, but was caused by a bráhman to desist, on the ground that the prince had degenerated into a vaisya.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Karusha's sons were the Kárushas, who were kshatriyas and warriors. Now they were seven hundred valiant men; and from them descended others in thousands.

## \|\| 110.2 \|\|

*diṣṭaputrastu nābhāgaḥ sthitaḥ prathamayauvane \| dadarśa vaiśyatanayāmatīva sumanoharām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now Dishta's son was Nábhága; he continued in the bloom of youthfulness. He saw a most surpassingly charming

## \|\| 110.3 \|\|

*tasyāṃ saṃdṛṣṭamātrāyāṃ madanākṣiptamānasaḥ \| babhūva bhūpatanayo niḥśvāsākṣepatatparaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. vaisya maiden. As soon as he beheld her, the prince was stricken in mind with love; he became absorbed in sighs and

## \|\| 110.4 \|\|

4\. reproaches. He went to her father and asked for the vaisya maiden in marriage; and then to the prince, whose mental

5\. feelings were under the dominion of the god of love, spoke her father -to the king's son spoke he, joining his hands respectfully, being afraid of the prince's father, this speech as he

## \|\| 110.6 \|\|

*bhavanto bhūbhujo bhṛtyā vayaṃ vaḥ karadāyakāḥ \| kathaṃ sambandhamasamairasmābhirabhivācchasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. bowed with deference, O bráhman -"Nobles of thy class are the enjoyers of the earth; dependants are we, paying tax to you. Why dost thou earnestly desire connexion with us who are not thy equals?"

The prince spoke:

## \|\| 110.7 \|\|

*rājaputra uvāca sāmyaṃ mānuṣadehasya kāmamohādibhiḥ kṛtam \| tathāpi kāle taireva yojyate mānuṣaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Equality of the human body is wrought by love, folly and other feelings. So indeed the human body is endowed with

## \|\| 110.8 \|\|

*tathaiva copakārāya jāyante tasya tānyapi \| anyāni cānye jīvanti bhinnajātimatāṃ satām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. those very feelings at the appropriate time, and thus in truth those feelings also come into existence for its benefit. And different feelings, different persons exist when folk exist of

## \|\| 110.9 \|\|

*tathānyānyapyayogyāni yogyatāṃ yānti kālataḥ \| yogyānyayogyatāṃ yānti kālavaśyā hi yogyatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. separate castes. Moreover, other feelings also that are inappropriate become proper according to season, and likewise appropriate feelings become inappropriate; for propriety depends

## \|\| 110.10 \|\|

*āpyāyyate yaccharīramāhārādibhirīpsitaiḥ \|*  
*kālaṃ jñātvā tathā bhuktaṃ tadeva pariśiṣyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. upon season. As the body is fattened by food and other things that are longed for, so that same body when used with

## \|\| 110.11 \|\|

*itthaṃ mamaiṣābhimatā tanayā dīyatāṃ tvayā \| anyathā maccharīrasya vipattirupalakṣyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. due regard to season is well regulated. Do thou accordingly bestow this thy highly esteemed daughter on me; otherwise calamity will be beheld in my body.

The vaisya spoke:

## \|\| 110.12 \|\|

*vaiśya uvāca paratantrā vayaṃ tvaṃ ca paratantro mahībhujaḥ \| pitrā tenābhyanujñātastvaṃ gṛhāṇa dadāmyaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. We are under another's authority, and thou art under another's authority, namely the king's. When he thy father permits thee, take thou her; I will give her.

The prince spoke:

## \|\| 110.13 \|\|

*rājaputra uvāca praṣṭavyā sarvakāryeṣu guravo guruvartibhiḥ \| na tvīdṛśeṣvakāryeṣu gurūṇāṃ vākyagocaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Those who treat gurus with respect should consult their gurus in all things that must be done; but not in such things as this, things which are not to be done, do the words of

## \|\| 110.14 \|\|

*kva manmatha kathālāpo gurūṇāṃ śravaṇaṃ kva ca \| viruddhametadanyatra praṣṭavyā guravo nṛbhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. gurus have scope. What has Love's conversation to do with listening to gurus? This is incompatible. In other things men should consult their gurus.

The vaisya spoke:

## \|\| 110.15 \|\|

*vaiśya uvāca evametatsmarālāpastavāyaṃ pṛccha mā gurum \| ahaṃ pṛcchāmi nālāpo mama kāmakathāśrayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Such, even this, is Love's talk! I, I here, will ask the guru, thine, the suitor's. My talk is not based on the speech of love.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 110.16 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityuktaḥ so'bhavanmaunī rājaputraḥ sa cāpi tat \| tatpitre sarvamācaṣṭa rājaputrasya yanmatam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When addressed thus the prince became silent. And he, the vaisya, related to that prince's father all that the prince

## \|\| 110.17 \|\|

*tatastasya pitā viprānṛcīkādīndvijottamān \| praveśya rājaputraṃ ca yathākhyānaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. thought. Thereupon his father summoned, before him the chief dvijas, Ric'ika and the other bráhmans, and the prince; and he made known the matter as it had been announced to

## \|\| 110.18 \|\|

*nivedya ca tataḥ prāha munīnevaṃ vyavasthite \| yatkartavyaṃ tadādeṣṭumarhanti dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. him; and after making it known he, being so situated in the matter, said to the munis, - "The best of dvijas deign to declare what ought to be done."

The rishis spoke:

## \|\| 110.19 \|\|

*ṛṣayaḥ ūcu rājaputrānurāgaste yadyasyāṃ vaiśyasantatau \| tadastu dharma evaiṣa kiṃ tu nyāyakrameṇa saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O prince, if thou hast love for this vaisya's child, then let this ordinance of righteousness verily be observed, but let it

## \|\| 110.20 \|\|

*mūrdhābhiṣiktatanayāpāṇigrāhotsavaḥ purā \|*  
*bhavatvanantaraṃ ceyaṃ tava bhāryā bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. be observed in the order enjoined bylaw. Marriage was enjoined for princes in the first place with the daughter of one who had been royally anointed. Be it so now first in thy case; and immediately afterwards this maiden also shall become thy wife.

## \|\| 110.21 \|\|

*evaṃ na doṣo bhavati tathemāmupabhuñjataḥ \| anyathā'bhyeti te jātirutkṛṣṭā bālakānayāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In this way no wickedness will attach to thee when thou enjoyest her thus; otherwise it does accrue: thy high rank comes from marriage with exalted maidens.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 110.22 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityuktastadapāsyeva vacasteṣāṃ mahātmanām \| viniṣkramya gṛhītvā tāmudyatāsirathābravīt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When admonished thus, he flung aside altogether that speech of those high-souled munis; and going outside he

## \|\| 110.23 \|\|

*rākṣasena vivāhena mayā vaiśyasutā hṛtā \| yasya sāmarthyamatrāsti sa etāṃ mocayatviti \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. seized her, and raising his sword aloft exclaimed, -"I have carried off the vaisya's daughter by the Rákshasa form of marriage; let him who has power here rescue her!"

## \|\| 110.24 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vaiśyastāṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhītāṃ tanayāṃ drutam \| trāhīti pitaraṃ tasya prayayau śaraṇaṃ dvija \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the vaisya seeing his daughter seized, O bráhman, hastened to that prince's father for help, exclaiming "Save

Nábhága declined the kingdom and Bhanandana became king -He had a son Vatsa-prí -A Daitya king Kujrimbha, who had a magic club called Sunanda, opened a great hole near king Vidúratha's city and carried the princess Mudávatí down to Pátála -Her brothers failed to rescue her and were made captive

Vatsa-prí killed the Daitya, after she destroyed the club's magic power, and rescued her and her brothers -She was named Sunanda after the club, and Vatsa-prí married her.

15\. Thus grieving in heart, king Khanitra being desirous of

## \|\| 115.16 \|\|

*abhiṣicya sutaṃ rājye kṣupasaṃjñaṃ mahīpatiḥ \| bhāryābhistisṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ tapase sa vanaṃ yayau \|\| 16 \|\|*

## \|\| 115.17 \|\|

## \|\| 115.18 \|\|

## Chapter 116

## \|\| 116.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca kṣupaḥ khanitraputrastu prāpya rājyaṃ yathā pitā \| tathaiva pālayāmāsa prajādharmeṇa rañjayan \|\| 1 \|\|*

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Now Khanitra's son Kshupa on receiving the kingdom protected his people, while delighting them in righteousness, even

## \|\| 116.2 \|\|

*ekadā sa mahīpālo nijasthānagato mune \| sūtairukto yathā pūrvaṃ kṣupo rājā tathā'bhavat \|\| 3 \|\|*

The king spoke:

The king spoke:

8\. of exalted exploits! Hear then the promise which I now

## \|\| 116.9 \|\|

*trīṃstrīnyajñānkariṣyāmi sasyāpāte gatāgate \| pṛthivyāṃ caturantāyāṃ pratijñeyaṃ kṛtā mayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. make -I will imitate the great king Kshupa's exploits. I will perform sacrifices three and three on the present and future gathering of the harvests on the earth which has four

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca iti pratijñāya vacaḥ kṣupastatkṛtavāṃstathā \| sasyāpāte sa yajñāṃstrīnayajadyajatāṃvaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasya putro'bhavadvīraḥ pramathāyāmaninditaḥ \| yasya pratāpaśauryābhyāṃ kṛtā vaśyā mahībhṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

15\. WhileVivimsa was ruling the earth, as a king of great

*tatpratāpena ripavo bhayamāpurmahāmune \| svāsthyaṃ janaḥ suhṛdvargo mudamāpa supūjitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

## \|\| 116.19 \|\|

## Chapter 117

## \|\| 117.1 \|\|

Vivimsa was succeeded by his son Khanínetra, who was a great sacrificer -Being son-less he went hunting to kill a deer for a sacrifice, and two deer came, one having no offspring and the other many -Each pressed his claim to be killed, but the king refused to kill either.

1\. His son was Khanínetra, great in strength and prowess, at whose sacrifices sang the Gandharvas, filled with astonishment,

## \|\| 117.3 \|\|

## \|\| 117.7 \|\|

## \|\| 117.8 \|\|

*mṛga uvāca*

Márkandeya spoke:

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca athābhyetya mṛgaḥ prāha tamanyo vasudhādhipam \| mṛgasya tasya pratyakṣamalametena pārthiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

14\. means of the flesh of this other son-less deer?As is the rite that is to be performed, such is the thing one should offer. Knowledge of the odours of sweetly-odorous things is not ascertained by means of ill-odorous things.

## \|\| 117.15 \|\|

*rājovāca vairāgyakāraṇaṃ proktamanenāputratā mama \| kathyatāṃ prāṇasaṃtyāge yatte vairāgyakāraṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

The deer spoke:

## \|\| 117.17 \|\|

17\. flames of a raging conflagration. O king, this most weakly deer-tribe is to be mastered by every one, and I have excessive self-interest in those my children - therefore I am distressed.

## \|\| 117.18 \|\|

*manuṣyasiṃhaśārdūlavṛkādibhyo bibhemyaham \| vihīnātsarvasattvebhyaḥ śvaśṛgālādapi prabho \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I am in fear of men, lions, tigers, wolves, and other ravenous beasts, but not of a feeble animal, nor of all good creatures, nor

## \|\| 117.19 \|\|

*so'haṃ nimittaṃ bandhūnāmimāṃ śūnyāṃ vasundharām \| nṛsiṃhādibhayātsarvāmicchāmi sunṛśaṃsakṛt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. even of a dog or jackal, my lord. Being such, I desire most earnestly for the sake of my kindred, that all this earth may be free for once from the fear of men, lions, and other beasts.

## \|\| 117.20 \|\|

*tṛṇānyanye'pi khādanti go'jāvituragādikāḥ \|*  
*tāṃsteṣāṃ poṣaṇāyāhamicchāmi nidhanaṃ gatān \|\| 20 \|\|*

## \|\| 117.21 \|\|

*niṣkrānteṣu tatasteṣu mamāpatyeṣu vai pṛthak \| bhavanti cintāḥ śataśo mamatvāvṛtacetasaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

## \|\| 117.22 \|\|

*kiṃ kūṭapāśaṃ kiṃ vajraṃ vāgurāṃ kiṃ suto mama \| prāptaścaranvane kiṃ vā nṛsiṃhādivaśaṃ gataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. to me whose mind is enveloped by self-interest, such as ' Has a son of mine while browsing in the forest encountered a crafty trap, or a thunderbolt, or a noose? or has he fallen into the power of a man, or lion or other dangerous creature?

## \|\| 117.23 \|\|

*prāpto'yamekaḥ samprāptāste'vasthāṃ kīdṛśīṃ mama \| sāmprataṃ te cirāyante ye gatāḥ sumahāvanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. What condition has this one reached? what condition have those sons of mine reached, who while actually grazing

## \|\| 117.24 \|\|

*dṛṣṭavā prāptānmamābhyāśamahaṃ tānātmajānnṛpa \| īṣaduchravasitaḥ kṣemamicchāmi rajanīṃ punaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. have now gone to the very great forest?' On seeing that those my sons have reached my presence, O king, I, panting somewhat, wish for night however as security

## \|\| 117.25 \|\|

*prabhāte divasaṃ kṣemamastage'rke niśāmapi \| vāñchāmyahaṃ kadā kṣemaṃ sarvakālaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. At dawn I desire day earnestly as security, and when the sun has set I desire again the night earnestly - when

## \|\| 117.26 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ bhūpa mahodvegasya kāraṇam \| ataḥ prasādaṃ kuru me bāṇo'yaṃ pātyatāṃ mayi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. will there be safety at every time? This I have declared to thee, O king, is the cause of my anxiety. Be gracious to me therefore - let this thy arrow be discharged at me!

## \|\| 117.27 \|\|

*iti duḥkhaśatāviṣṭaḥ prāṇānnāhaṃ tyajāmi yat \| tatkāraṇaṃ nibodha tvaṃ bruvato mama pārthiva \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. That is the cause why pierced by hundreds of sufferings I thus forsake even my life; hearken thou as I speak, O king!

## \|\| 117.28 \|\|

*asūryā nāma te lokā yāngacchantyātmaghātakāḥ \| yajñopayuktāḥ paśavaḥ samprayāntyucchritīḥ prabho \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Named 'The Sun-less' are the worlds, to which those who kill themselves go; but cattle that are suitable for sacrifice attain

## \|\| 117.29 \|\|

*agniḥ paśurabhūtpūrvaṃ paśurāsījjalādhipaḥ \| bhāsvānathocchritīḥ prāptā yajñe niṣṭhāmupāgatāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. thus to exalted stations, O lord. Agni was a domestic animal formerly; the lord of the waters was a domestic animal; and so was the Sun, who gained exalted stations and reached his

The first deer spoke:

## \|\| 117.31 \|\|

The second deer spoke:

*uttaramṛga uvāca ekadehabhayaṃ yasya duḥkhaṃ dhanyaḥ sa vai bhavān \| bahūni yasya dehāni tasya duḥkhānyanekadhā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Happy in troth art thou, sir deer, being such a one for whom suffering exists in a single body! He who has many bodies has

## \|\| 117.33 \|\|

## \|\| 117.34 \|\|

*yadājātānyapatyāni tadā yāvanti tāni vai \| tāvaccharīrabhūmīni mama duḥkhānyathābhavan \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When children were born, then as many as they were, so many

## \|\| 117.35 \|\|

*na kṛtārtho bhavāmyasya nātiduḥkhāya sambhavaḥ \| iha duḥkhāya matsūtiḥparatra ca virodhinī \|\| 35 \|\|*

## \|\| 117.36 \|\|

*yato rakṣaṇapoṣārthamapatyānāṃ karomi tat \| cintayāmi ca sambhūtistena me narake dhruvam \|\| 36 \|\|*

The king spoke:

## \|\| 117.37 \|\|

*rājovāca na vedmi kiṃ santatimāndhanyo'putro'tra kiṃ mṛga \| putrārthaścāyamārambho mama dolāyate manaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. I know not, O deer, whether he who has offspring is happy in this world, or he who has no son; and this undertaking of

## \|\| 117.38 \|\|

38\. mine in order to obtain a son makes my mind vacillate. Offspring verily tend then to cause suffering both in this world and in the other world; nevertheless, debts come upon those

## \|\| 117.39 \|\|

39\. who have no son -so have I heard. I being such will strive to obtain a son, without the slaughter of breathing beings, O deer, even with very arduous austerities, as did a king of yore.

## Chapter 118

## \|\| 118.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ sa nṛpatirgatvā gomatīṃ pāpanāśinīm \| tatra tuṣṭāva niyato bhūtvā devaṃ purandaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Khanínetra propitiated Indra and obtained the gift of a son, Balásva -King Balásva was besieged by his rebellious vassal kings and was delivered by an army which issued from his hands that shook with distress - Hence he was named Karandhama.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Thereupon the king went to the sin-destroying river Go-matí, and, practising self-restraint, gratified the god Purandara

## \|\| 118.2 \|\|

*tapyamānastapaścograṃ yatavākkāyamānasaḥ \| tuṣṭāva prayataḥ śakramapatyārthaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. there. And assiduously practising severe austerities, subduing his voice, body and mind, and controlling himself,

## \|\| 118.3 \|\|

*tasya stotreṇa tapasā bhaktyā cāpi sureśvaraḥ \| tutoṣa bhagavānindraḥ prāha cainaṃ mahāmune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. the king gratified Indra in order to obtain a son. The adorable Indra, lord of the gods, was gratified with his praise,

## \|\| 118.4 \|\|

*anena tapasā bhaktyā stotreṇoccāritena ca \| parituṣṭo'smi te bhūpa vriyatāṃ bhavatā varaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. austerities and faith, and said to him, O great muni, -"By reason of these austerities, faith and praise uttered by thee, I am well satisfied with thee, O king; choose a boon, sir!"

The king spoke:

## \|\| 118.5 \|\|

*rājovāca aputrasya suto me'stu sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \| sadā cāvyāhataiśvaryo dharmakṛddharmavitkṛtī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. May I who am son-less obtain a son, who shall be chief among all who bear arms, and always unrepulsed in his sovereignty, a doer of righteousness, a knower of righteousness, and skilful.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 118.6 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tatheti coktaḥ śakreṇa rājā prāptamanorathaḥ \| prajāḥ pālayituṃ bhūpa ājagāma nijaṃ puram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. And when Indra said to him, "Be it so!" the king gained his desire. The king returned to his own city to protect his

## \|\| 118.7 \|\|

*tatrāsya kurvato yajñaṃ samyakpālayataḥ prajāḥ \| ajāyata suto vipra tadā śakraprasādataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. people. As he was performing sacrifice there, as he was duly protecting his people, a son was born to him then through

## \|\| 118.8 \|\|

*tasya nāma pitā cakre balāśva iti bhūpatiḥ \| astragrāmamaśeṣaṃ ca grāhayāmāsa taṃ sutam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indra's favour, O bráhman.The king, his father, gave him the name Balásva, and caused the son to acquire skill in every

## \|\| 118.9 \|\|

*pitaryuparate vipra so'dhirājye sthito nṛpaḥ \| sa balāśvo vaśaṃ ninye bhuvi sarvamahīkṣitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. kind of weapon. When his father died, O bráhman, he stood as king in the supreme sovereignty. Balásva brought all

## \|\| 118.10 \|\|

*karaṃ ca dāpayāmāsa sāragrahaṇapūrvakam \|*  
*sa sarvabhūmipānrājā pālayāmāsa ca prajāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. kings on the earth into subjection; and the king after first taking away their choicest property, made all the kings pay him tribute; and he protected his people.

## \|\| 118.11 \|\|

*athākhilanarendrāste dāyādāstasya durmadāḥ \| na cābhyutthāya satataṃ ta cāsmai pradaduḥ karān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Now all those kings as claimants were furious against him; and at all times they neither rose up before him nor paid him tribute.

## \|\| 118.12 \|\|

*vyutthitāḥ sveṣu rāṣṭreṣu na santoṣaparāstataḥ \| bhuvaṃ tasya narendrasya jagṛhuste narādhipāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They stood up then in their own countries; disregarding contentment as the chief good, those kings seized that king's territory.

## \|\| 118.13 \|\|

*sa gṛhītvā svakaṃ rājyaṃ pṛthivīśo balānmune \| tasthau svanagare bhūpairvirodho bahubhiḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. That king held fast his own kingdom by force, O muni, and made his stand in his own city. Many kings besieged him.

## \|\| 118.14 \|\|

*sametya sumahāvīryāḥ sasādhanadhanāstataḥ \| rurudhustaṃ mahīpālaṃ pure tatra nareśvarāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Kings, very great in valour, possessing military apparatus and riches, assembled then and besieged that king in that city.

## \|\| 118.15 \|\|

*purarodhena tenātha kupitaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \| svalpakośo'lpadaṇḍaśca vaiklavyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Now the king was enraged at that siege of his city, but, having very little treasure and a small army, fell into the utmost

## \|\| 118.16 \|\|

*apaśyamānaḥ śaraṇaṃ sabalo dvijasattama \| karau mukhāgrataḥ kṛtvā niśaśvāsārtamānasaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. distress. Beholding no succour though possessing an army, O best of dvijas, he put his hands before his face and sighed

## \|\| 118.17 \|\|

*tato'sya hastavivarānmukhānilasamāhatāḥ \| nirjagmuḥ śataśo yodhā rathanāgaturaṅgamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. in mental suffering. Then compacted together by the breath from his mouth, which issued through the interstice between his hands, there went forth in hundreds warriors

## \|\| 118.18 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣaṇena tatsarvaṃ nagaraṃ tasya bhūpateḥ \| vyāptamāsīdbalaughena sāreṇātibalānmune \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. accompanied by chariots, elephants and horses. Thereby in a moment all that city of that king was pervaded by a host of forces, choice by reason of their extreme strength, O muni.

## \|\| 118.19 \|\|

*atha so'tibalaughena mahatā tena saṃvṛtaḥ \| nirmathyanagarāttasmāttānvijigye narādhipaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Surrounded then by that exceeding great host of forces, the king sallied forth from that city and conquered those foes.

## \|\| 118.20 \|\|

*jitvā ca vaśamānīya cakāra karadānpunaḥ \|*  
*yathāpūrvaṃ mahābhāga mahābhāgyo nareśvaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. And after vanquishing them the king, having great good fortune, brought them into subjection and made them pay

## \|\| 118.21 \|\|

*dhutayoḥ karayorjajñe yatastasyāridāhadam \| balaṃ karandhamastasmātsa balāśvo'bhidhīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. tribute again as before, illustrious sir. Because from his agitated hands was produced an army which burnt up his

## \|\| 118.22 \|\|

*sa dharmātmā mahātmā ca sa maitraḥ sarvajantuṣu \| karandhamo'bhavadbhūpastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. foes, Balásva is thence called Karandhama. He was righteous of soul and great of soul; he was benevolent to all living creatures. King Karandhama was celebrated in the three

## \|\| 118.23 \|\|

*samprāstasya parāmārttiṃ dadāvarivināśanam \| balaṃ dharmeṇa cākṣiptamabhyupetya svayaṃ nṛpam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. worlds. And Power, which is denounced by Righteousness itself approaching the king, who had undergone intense suffering, granted him the destruction of his enemies.

## Chapter 119

## \|\| 119.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca vīryacandrasutā subhūrvīrā nāma śubhavratā \| svayaṃvare sā jagṛhe mahārājaṃ karandhamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Karandhama had a son Avíkshita, who was so called because benign planets looked upon his birth -Avíkshita was a great prince; he was chosen by many princesses and he also carried off others at their svayam-varas -He carried off Vaisáliní princess of Vidisá, and other kings arrayed themselves against him.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Virya-c'andra's beautiful-browed daughter was named Vírá; she was noble in her vows. She chose the great king

## \|\| 119.2 \|\|

*tasyāṃ putraṃ sa rājendro janayāmāsa vīryavān \| avikṣitamiti khyātimupetaṃ jagatītale \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Karandhama for her husband at her svayam-vara. That valiant king of kings begat of her a son namedAvíkshita, who attained

## \|\| 119.3 \|\|

*jāte tasminsute rājā sa daivajñānapṛcchata \| kaccitpraśastanakṣatre śastalagne suto mama \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. fame on the face of the earth. When that son was born, the king asked the astrologers who could read fate -"I trust my son is born under an excellent constellation, at an excellent

## \|\| 119.4 \|\|

*kacciccālokitaṃ janma mama putrasya śobhanaiḥ \| grahaiḥ kaccinna duṣṭānāṃ grahāṇāṃ dṛkpathaṃ gatam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. conjuncture? And I trust that benignant planets have looked upon my son's birth; I trust it did not pass into the path of view of evil planets?"

## \|\| 119.5 \|\|

*ityuktāstena daivajñāstamūcurnṛpatiṃ tataḥ \| śaste muhūrte nakṣatre lagne caiva sutastava \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When addressed thus by him, the astrologers spake then to the king - "When the moment, the constellation and the

## \|\| 119.6 \|\|

*samutpanno mahāvīryo mahābhāgo mahābalaḥ \| bhaviṣyati mahārāja mahārājastavātmajaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. conjuncture have been excellent, thy son has been born to be great in valour, great in his parts, great in strength. O great king, thy

## \|\| 119.7 \|\|

*avaikṣatemaṃ devānāṃ guruḥ śukraśca saptamaḥ \| somaścaturthastanayaṃ tavainaṃ samavaikṣata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. son shall be a great king. The planet Jupiter, preceptor of the gods, has looked on him, and Venus which is the seventh; and the Moon the fourth planet has looked upon this thy son;

## \|\| 119.8 \|\|

*upāntasaṃsthitaścaiva somaputropyavaikṣata \| nāvaikṣatemaṃ savitā na bhaumo na śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. and Soma's son Mercury also, which is stationed at the edge,

## \|\| 119.9 \|\|

*tava putraṃ mahārāja dhanyo'yaṃ tanayastava \| sarvakalyāṇasampatti samaveto bhaviṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. has guarded him. The Sun has not looked on him; nor has Mars or Saturn looked on thy son, O great king. Happy is this thy son! he will be endowed with all good fortune and prosperity."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 119.10 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*iti daivajñavacanaṃ niśamya vasudhādhipaḥ \|*  
*harṣapūrṇamanāḥ prāha nijasthānagatastadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On hearing this the astrologers' speech, the king was filled with gladness in his mind, and going then to his own abode he said -

## \|\| 119.11 \|\|

*avaikṣatemaṃ devānāṃ guruḥ somaḥ sito budhaḥ \| nāvaikṣatainamādityo nārkasūnurna bhūmijaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. "The preceptor of the gods has looked on him, and so has Soma's son Mercury. The Sun has not looked on him, nor

## \|\| 119.12 \|\|

*avaikṣateti yatproktaṃ bhavadbhirbahuśo vacaḥ \| avikṣiteti tenāsya khyātaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. has the Sun's son nor Mars. This word 'Has looked upon' that ye, sirs, have uttered often, -celebrated by reason of it his name shall beAvíkshita."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 119.13 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca avikṣitaḥ sutastasya vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \| astragrāmamaśeṣaṃ sa kaṇvaputrādathāgrahīt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. His son Avíkshita learnt the whole of the Vedas and Vedángas. He acquired too from Kanva's son perfect skill in every

## \|\| 119.14 \|\|

*svarūpeṇātibhiṣajau devānāṃ pārthivātmajaḥ \| buddhyā vācaspatiṃ kāntyā śaśāṅkaṃ tejasā ravim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. weapon. The prince surpassed both the Physicians of the gods in figure,Vác'as-pati in intellect, the Moon in loveliness,

## \|\| 119.15 \|\|

*dhairyeṇābdhiṃ tayorvīṃ ca sahiṣṇutvena vīryavān \| śauryeṇa na samastasya kaścidāsīnmahātmanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. the Sun in splendour, the Ocean in steadfastness, and the Earth in endurance, full of valour as he was. In heroism no one was the equal of that high-souled prince.

## \|\| 119.16 \|\|

*svayaṃvare taṃ jagṛhe hemadharmātmajā varā \| sudevatanayā gaurī subhadrā balinaḥ sutā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At her svayam-vara Hema-dharma's daughter Vará chose him for her husband; so also did Sudeva's daughter Gaurí, Balin's

## \|\| 119.17 \|\|

*līlāvatī vīrasutā vīrabhadrasutā nibhā \| bhīmātmajā mānyavatī dambhaputrī kumudvatī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. daughter Su-bhadrá, Víra's daughter Lílávatí, Víra-bhadra's daughter Anibhá, Bhíma's daughter Mánya-vatí, Dambha's

*yāścainaṃ nābhinandanti svayaṃvarakṛtakṣaṇāḥ \| tāścāpi sa balādvīro jagrāha nṛpateḥ sutaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. daughter Kumud-vatí. And those maidens who, awaiting the precise moment at their svayam-varas, did not approve him

## \|\| 119.19 \|\|

*nirākṛtya nṛpānsarvāṃstāsāṃ pitṛkulāni ca \| svayaṃ hi vīryamāśritya balavānna baloddhataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. even them the hero prince took by force. Driving off all the kings and the fathers and families of those princesses and trusting in his own valour, the mighty prince was indeed proud of his strength.

## \|\| 119.20 \|\|

*ekadā tu viśālasya viśālādhipateḥ sutām \|*  
*vaiśālinīṃ sa sudatīṃ svayaṃvarakṛtakṣaṇām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Now one day he seized Vaisáliní of the beautiful teeth, daughter of theVaidisa king Visála, as she was waiting for

## \|\| 119.21 \|\|

*paribhūyākhilānbhūpānsvecchayā na vṛtastayā \| balājjagrāha viprarṣe yathānyā balagarvitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. the proper moment at her svayam-vara; after vanquishing all the kings he seized her by force, because in her own free fancy she chose him not, O bráhman-rishi, just as, proud of

*tataste bhūbhṛtaḥ sarve bahuśastena māninā \| nirākṛtāḥ sunirviṇṇāḥ procuranyonyamākulāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. his strength, he had seized other princesses. Then all those kings, being repeatedly driven off by that haughty prince and being sorely dejected, spoke to one another, all thronging

## \|\| 119.23 \|\|

*kṣamatāṃ vañcanāmetāmekasmādbalaśālinām \| bahūnāmekavarṇānāṃ janma dhigvo mahībhṛtām \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. together, - "Fie on the birth of you kings, who being endowed with strength submit to this defrauding deed at the hands of

## \|\| 119.24 \|\|

*kṣatriyo yaḥ kṣatāttrāṇaṃ vadhyamānasya durmadaiḥ \| karoti tasya tannāma vṛthaivānye hi bibhrati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. a single man, and who are many, of the same caste! A kshatriya is he who delivers from injury a man, who is being killed by ferocious men; that is the name of such a one; for

## \|\| 119.25 \|\|

*ātmano'pi kṣatatrāṇaṃ duṣṭādasmādakurvatām \| bhavatāṃ kṣatriyakule jātānāṃ kīdṛśī matiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. in vain verily do others bear that name! Of you, sirs, who, though born of kshatriya lineage, cannot save even your own selves from injury at the hands of this scoundrel, what is

## \|\| 119.26 \|\|

*uccāryate stutiryā vaḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ \| sā satyā mā vṛthā vīrā bhavatvarivināśanāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. your resolution like? Let the praise, which is poured forth to you by bards and minstrels and heralds, be true -let it not bee in vain - O heroes, by reason of the destruction of your

## \|\| 119.27 \|\|

*caratāṃ sā tathaivaiṣā bhūpāścārairdigantare \| pauruṣāśrayiṇaḥ sarve viśiṣṭakulasambhavāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. foes! Let not this story vainly spread itself about by messengers belonging to other regions, O kings!Ye all rely on your manhood, ye are sprung from exalted families. Who fears

## \|\| 119.28 \|\|

28\. not death? Who is immortal without battling? With these thoughts ye whose profession is arms must not abandon your manhood."

## \|\| 119.29 \|\|

*etanniśamya te bhūpā vispaṣṭāmarṣapūritāḥ \| ūcuḥ parasparaṃ sarve samuttasthuśca sāyudhāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

30\. their weapons. Some mounted chariots, some elephants and others horses; others overpowered with wrath advanced on foot against him.

## Chapter 120

## \|\| 120.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca iti saṃgrāmasajjāste bhūpā bhūpasutastathā \| nirākṛtāḥ subahuśastatkālaṃ cāpyavikṣitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

The kings had a great battle with Avíkshita and conquered and captured him. -The svayam-vara was reopened, but the princess would not choose any husband, and the wedding was postponed.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Thus were prepared for battle those kings and princes, who had been beaten off repeatedly and yet were not destroyed at

## \|\| 120.2 \|\|

*tato babhūva saṃgrāmastasya taiḥ saha dāruṇaḥ \| ekasya bahubhirbhūpairbhūpaputravarairmune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. that time. Then began a terrible battle between him and them, between the prince single-handed and many kings and noble

## \|\| 120.3 \|\|

*te'siśaktigadābāṇapāṇayastaṃ sudurmadāḥ \| abhighnanto yuyudhire taiḥ samastairasāvapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. princes, O muni. In great ferocity they fought, assailing him with their swords, spears, clubs, arrows, and hands; and he

## \|\| 120.4 \|\|

*sa tāñcharaśatairugrairbibheda nṛpanandanaḥ \| kṛtāstro balavānbāṇaiste ca taṃ bibhiduḥ śitaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. fought with them all. The prince mighty and skilled in weapons pierced them with hundreds of fierce arrows; and they

## \|\| 120.5 \|\|

*kasyaciccicchide bāhumanyasya ca śirodharām \| hṛdi vivyādha caivānyamanyaṃ vakṣasyatāḍayat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. pierced him with sharp arrows. He cut off the arm of one, and the neck of another; and pierced another in the heart,

## \|\| 120.6 \|\|

*karaṃ ciccheda kariṇasturagasya tathā śiraḥ \| rathasyeṣāṃ tathaivāśvānrathasyānyasya sārathim \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. and smote another in the breast. He cut off the trunk of an elephant and the head of a horse, and wounded the horses of the chariot of these foes and the driver of the chariot of

## \|\| 120.7 \|\|

*bāṇānāpatataścakre dvidhā bāṇaistathā dviṣām \| cicchedānyasya khaḍgaṃ ca dhanuranyasya lāghavāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. another. And he split in two with his own arrows his enemies' arrows which were falling on him, and in his agility cracked

## \|\| 120.8 \|\|

*tanutre'pahṛte tena nanāśānyo nṛpātmajaḥ \| avikṣitāhataścānyaḥ padātiḥ prajahau raṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

## \|\| 120.9 \|\|

*ityākulīkṛte tasminsamagre rājamaṇḍale \| tasthuḥ saptaśataṃ vīrā maraṇe kṛtaniścayāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When that entire band of kings was thus thrown into confusion, seven hundred warriors stood forth resolute unto death,

## \|\| 120.10 \|\|

*ābhijātyavayaḥśauryalajjābhārasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*nirjite sakale sainye palāyanaparāyaṇe \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. who were nobly born, in the flower of their age, heroic, valiant, and modest, after all the army was defeated and was in a panic of

*taiḥ sametya mahīpālaiḥ sa tu putro mahībhṛtaḥ \| yuyudhe dharmayuddhena tena taṃ nātikopitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*cchinnāsicarmā jagrāha sa gadāṃ gadināṃ varaḥ \| tāmapyanyaḥ kṣurapreṇa ciccheda kṛtahastavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When his sword and shield were broken, he best of clubwielders grasped his club; and another, like a dexterous man, split

## \|\| 120.18 \|\|

*anye śarasahasreṇa śatenānye narādhipāḥ \| vivyadhuḥ koṣṭhakīkṛtya dharmayuddhaparāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. it with a sharp curved-headed arrow. The kings, turning their faces away from righteously conducted combat, surrounded him and pierced him, some with a thousand arrows, some

*sa vihvalaḥ papātorvyāmeko bahubhirarditaḥ \| rājaputrā mahābhāgā babandhuste ca taṃ tataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

## Chapter 121

## \|\| 121.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ śuśrāva taṃ baddhaṃ tanayaṃ sa karandhamaḥ \| tasya patnī tathā vīrā anye cāpi mahībhṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Avíkshita's mother Virá roused up his father and allied kings to rescue Avíkshita, and they defeated Visála and his confederates -Avíkshita was set free, but refused to marry the princess as she had seen him overpowered, although she praised him and his father entreated him - She vowed to marry no one else, and departed to the forest and wore herself away with austerities -The gods in compassion sent a messenger to her and promised that she should have a son who should be a universal monarch -She then regained her health.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Karandhama heard then that his son had been captured; and

## \|\| 121.2 \|\|

*tamadharmeṇa tanayaṃ baddhaṃ śrutvā mahīpatiḥ \| samantaiḥ pṛthivīpālaiściraṃ dadhyau mahāmune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. his wife Vírá and other kings also heard it. On hearing that his son had been captured unrighteously, the king pondered a long time in company with the neighbouring kings, O

## \|\| 121.3 \|\|

*kecidūcurmahīpālā vadhyāḥ sarve mahībhṛtaḥ \| yairekaḥ saṃyuge baddhaḥ samastaistairadharmataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. great muni. Some of the kings said, - "All those kings should be slain, who banding themselves all together captured him

## \|\| 121.4 \|\|

*yujyatāṃ vāhinī śīghramūcuranye kimāsyate \| viśālo badhyatāṃ duṣṭastatra ye'nye samāgatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. single-handed unrighteously in fight." "Let the army be made ready; why sit the others still? Let wicked Visála be

## \|\| 121.5 \|\|

*anye tathocurdharmo'tra tyaktaḥ pūrvamahīkṣitā \| anyāyena balādyena gṛhītā tamavācchatī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. slain!" said others who were assembled there. And others said, -"Righteousness was first discarded in this affair by Avíkshit, who acting unjustly forcibly seized the princess who

## \|\| 121.6 \|\|

*svayaṃvareṣvaśeṣeṣu tena rājasutāstadā \| khilīkṛtāstataḥ sarve sametya sa vaśīkṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. did not desire him. In all svayam-varas then he has reduced all the princes to ruin at once; when they combined, he was subdued."

## \|\| 121.7 \|\|

*teṣāmetadvacaḥ śrutvā vīrā vīraprajāvatī \| vīragotrasamudbhūtā vīrapatnī praharṣitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

## \|\| 121.8 \|\|

*uvāca bharttuḥ pratyakṣamanyeṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām \| bhadraṃ kṛtaṃ bhadrabhujā mama putreṇa pārthivāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. race of heroes, and wife of a hero, rejoiced and spoke in view of her husband and of the other kings, - "A noble

*gṛhītā yadbalātkanyā jitvā sarvamahīkṣitaḥ \| tadarthaṃ yudhyamāno'yaṃ baddha eko na dharmataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. deed, O kings, has my son who feasts on noble deeds done, in that vanquishing all the kings he seized the maiden by force. While fighting for that object single-handed he was captured

*tadapyasmatsutasyājau manye nāpacayapradam \|*  
*etadevahi pauruṣyaṃ yadamarṣavaśānnaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. unrighteously. Even that I reckon entails no deterioration on my son in battle. For this in truth is manliness, that a

## \|\| 121.11 \|\|

*nītiṃ na gaṇayatyevaṃ jighāṃsuriva kesarī \| svayaṃvarāya vinyastā mama putreṇa kanyakā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*balādeva samādatte kṣatriyo balināṃ puraḥ \| lohaśṛṃkhalabaddhā vā na vaśaṃ yānti kātarāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

## \|\| 121.64 \|\|

*atraiva kānane tiṣṭha tanuṃ kṣīṇāṃ ca poṣaya \| tapaḥprabhāvādetatte sarvaṃ sādhu bhaviṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Remain in this very forest and nourish up thy emaciated body. Through the power of austerities all this shall be well for thee.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 121.65 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityuktvā devadūto'sau yathāgatamagacchata \| cakārānudinaṃ subhrūḥ sāpyātmatanupoṣaṇam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. After speaking thus, the messenger of the gods went away as he had come. And the beautiful-browed lady nourished up her body day by day.

## Chapter 122

## \|\| 122.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atha sā'vikṣito mātā vīrā vīra prajāvatī \| puṇye'hani samāhūya prāha putramavikṣitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Avíkshita's mother induced him to engage in the 'Whatwant- ye?' penance, in which he declared he would bestow on any one who asked whatever he wanted -His father Karandhama, being entreated by his ministers, pressed Avíkshita to forgo his religious continence and beget a son -Avíkshita though very loth was obliged to promise compliance.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Now Avíkshita's mother Vírá, mother of a hero, called her son Avíkshita on a sacred day and said: -

## \|\| 122.2 \|\|

*putrāhamabhyanujñātā tava pitrā mahātmanā \| upavāsaṃ kariṣyāmi duṣkaro'yaṃ kimicchakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. "My son, permitted by thy high-souled father, I will engage in a fast; it is this difficult penance, the 'What-want-ye?'

## \|\| 122.3 \|\|

*sa cāyattastava pitustvayā sādhyo mayāpi ca \| pratijñāte tvayā putra tatastatra yatāmyaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. And it depends on thy father, and must be achieved by thee and by me also. When thou hast consented, my son.

## \|\| 122.4 \|\|

*dravyasyārddhaṃ mahākośāttava dāsyāmyahaṃ pituḥ \| dhanaṃ te piturāyattamanujñātā'smi tena ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I will then give my endeavours thereto. I will give thee half the riches from thy father's great treasury; thy riches

## \|\| 122.5 \|\|

*kleśasādhyo madāyattaḥ sa hi śreyo bhaviṣyati \| sādhyo bhavedvā yadi te kaścidbalaparākramaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. depend on thy father, and I have his permission. To be achieved through affliction is the part of the penance that depends upon me; it will indeed be a noble thing. If, on the other hand, any part of it may be achievable by thee

## \|\| 122.6 \|\|

*sa te'sādhyo hyanyathā vā duḥkhasādhyo bhaviṣyati \| tattvaṃ pratijñāṃ kuruṣe yadi putrātra caiva te \| tadaitadahamāvāpsye kathyatāṃ yanmataṃ tava \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. through strength and prowess, that will indeed be unachievable by thee otherwise, or will be achievable with difficulty. If then thou givest me a promise, my son, I also will pledge thee here the very same thing. Tell me what thou thinkest."

Avíkshita spoke:

## \|\| 122.7 \|\|

*avikṣiduvāca vittaṃ me piturāyattaṃ matsvāmitvaṃ na tatra vai \| yanmaccharīraniṣpādyaṃ tatkariṣye tvayoditam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Riches depend on my. father; I indeed have no ownership therein. I will perform what can be accomplished by my

## \|\| 122.8 \|\|

*kimicchakaṃ vrataṃ mātarniścintā bhava nirvyathā \| rājñā pitrā'bhyanujñātaṃ yadi vitteśvareṇa me \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. body, as thou hast said, even the 'What-want-ye?' penance, O mother -cease then from anxiety and distress -if it has been approved for me by the king, my father, the master of the riches.

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 122.9 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ sā rājamahiṣī tadvrataṃ samupoṣitā \| yathoktaṃ sā'karotpūjāṃ rājarājasya saṃyatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then the queen applied herself wholly to that penance. She performed the worship of the king of kings as directed,

## \|\| 122.10 \|\|

*nidhīnāmapyaśeṣāṇāṃ nidhipālagaṇasya ca \|*  
*lakṣmyāśca parayā bhaktyā yatavākkāyamānasā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. with self subdued, and the worship of all the Nidhis and of the band of Nidhi-guardians and of Lakshmí, with profound faith, with voice, body and mind restrained.

## \|\| 122.11 \|\|

*vivikte tu gṛhastho'yamatha rājā karandhamaḥ \| āsīna uktaḥ sacivairnītiśāstraviśāradaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Now this king Karandhama dwelt in his house in a sequestered part. As he sat there, his ministers, learned in the books of Good Policy, addressed him.

The ministers spoke:

## \|\| 122.12 \|\|

*sacivā ūcuḥ rājanvayaḥ pariṇataṃ tavaitacchāsato mahīm \| ekaste tanayo'vikṣittyaktadāraparigrahaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O king, this thy time of life has reached its decline, while thou art ruling the earth. Thy only son Avíkshit has forsworn

## \|\| 122.13 \|\|

*aputraḥ sa ca te niṣṭhāṃ yadā bhūpa gamiṣyati \| tadāripakṣaṃ pṛthivī niścitaṃ tava yāsyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. possession of his wives; and he has no son. When he shall reach thy condition, O king, thy territory will

## \|\| 122.14 \|\|

*vaṃśakṣayaste bhavitā pitṛpiṇḍodakakṣayaḥ \| etanmahatte'ribhayaṃ kriyāhānyā bhaviṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. assuredly pass to thy enemies then. There will be ruin to thy family, and ruin to the cakes and water offered to the pitris; thou wilt have this great dread of enemies with

## \|\| 122.15 \|\|

*tasmātkuru tathā bhūpa yathā te tanayaḥ punaḥ \| karoti satataṃ buddhiṃ pitṝṇāmupakāriṇīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. loss of sacrifices. Contrive therefore, O king, so that thy son shall again steadfastly apply his mind so as to benefit the pitris!

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 122.16 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca etasminnantare śabdaṃ śuśrāva jagatīpatiḥ \| purohitasya vīrāyā gadato hyarthinaṃ prati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At this moment the king heard the sound of Vírá's family priest speaking to some petitioner; -

## \|\| 122.17 \|\|

*kaḥ kimicchati duḥsādhyaṃ kasya kiṃ sādhyatāmiti \| karandhamasya mahiṣī kimicchikamupoṣitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. " 'Who wishes for what, that is hard to be achieved? Who must achieve what?' -this 'What-want-ye?' penance Karandhama's queen is intent upon!"

## \|\| 122.18 \|\|

*rājaputro'pyavikṣittu śrutvā paurohitaṃ vacaḥ \| pratyuvācārthinaḥ sarvānrājadvāramupāgatān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Now prince Avíkshit also heard the priest's speech and replied to all the petitioners who were assembled at the

## \|\| 122.19 \|\|

*mayā sādhyaṃ śarīreṇa yasya kiñjidbravītu saḥ \| mama mātā mahābhāgā kimicchikamupoṣitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. king's gate; -"Let him speak out, for whom I must accomplish anything with my body; my illustrious mother

## \|\| 122.20 \|\|

*śṛṇvantu me'rthinaḥ sarve pratijñātaṃ mayā tadā \|*  
*kimicchatha dadāmyeṣa kriyamāṇo kimicchike \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. is intent upon the 'What-want-ye?' penance. Let all petitioners hear me. I have promised then; what want ye? here I give it, while the 'What-want-ye?' penance is being' performed!"

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 122.21 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato rājā niśamyaitadvākyaṃ putramukhācchrutam \| samutpatyābravītputramahamarthī prayaccha me \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereupon the king, on hearing this speech that fell from his son's mouth, springing up said to his son, -"I have a petition; grant it me!"

Avíkshit spoke:

## \|\| 122.22 \|\|

*avikṣiduvāca dātavyaṃ yanmayā tāta bhavate tadbravīhi mām \| kartavyaṃ duṣkaraṃ vā te sādhyaṃ duḥsādhyameva vā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Tell me, dear father, what I must give to your highness; I must do it for thee, whether it be difficult, or readily accomplishable, or truly hard to be accomplished!

The king spoke:

## \|\| 122.23 \|\|

*rājovāca yadi satyapratijñastvaṃ dadāsi ca kimicchakam \| pautrasya darśaya mukhaṃ mamotsaṅgagatasya tat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If thou art true to thy word, and thou grantest the 'Whatwant- ye?' boon, show me then the face of a grandson lying upon my lap!

Avíkshit spoke:

## \|\| 122.24 \|\|

*avikṣiduvāca ahaṃ tavaikastanayo brahmacaryaṃ ca me nṛpa \| na me putro'sti pautrasya darśayāmi kathaṃ mukham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I am thy only son, and religious continence is my lot, O king; no son have I, how can I show thee a grandson's face?

The king spoke:

## \|\| 122.25 \|\|

*rājovāca pāpāya brahmacaryaṃ te yadidaṃ dhāryate tvayā \| tasmāttvaṃ mocayātmānaṃ mama pautraṃ ca darśaya \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thy religious continence tends to sin, if thou holdest to this. Therefore deliver thou thy own self and show me a grandson!

Avíkshit spoke:

## \|\| 122.26 \|\|

*avikṣiduvāca viṣamaṃ syānmahārāja yadanyattatsamādiśa \| vairāgyeṇa mayā tyaktaḥ strīsaṃbhogastathāstu saḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Any other thing that may he arduous, O great king, command me that. Intercourse with women has been eschewed by me, with passionlessness - let it be so still!

The king spoke:

## \|\| 122.27 \|\|

*rājovāca bahubhiryudhyamānānāṃ dṛṣṭo vai vairiṇāṃ jayaḥ \| tatrāpi yadi vairāgyamupaiṣi tadapaṇḍitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thou in sooth hast seen victory over enemies who were fighting against thee with numbers; yet, there if thou hast

## \|\| 122.28 \|\|

*kiṃ vā no bahunoktena brahmacaryaṃ parityaja \| mātustvamicchayā vaktra pautrasya mama darśaya \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. recourse to passionlessness, then thou art unwise. Yet what need have we of more talking? Abandon thy religious continence. At thy mother's desire show thou me a grandson's face!

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 122.29 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca yadā sa bahuśastena proktaḥ putreṇa pārthivaḥ \| nānyatprārthayate kiṃcittadā putro'bravītpunaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When the king, though accosted by the son in many words,

## \|\| 122.30 \|\|

*dattvā kimicchakaṃ tubhyaṃ prāpto'haṃ tāta saṅkaṭam \|*  
*tatkariṣyāmi nirlajjo bhūyo dāraparigraham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. makes no other request, the son then spoke again; -"By granting thee the 'What-want-ye?' boon, I am in a strait, dear father. I will therefore without shame wed a wife

## \|\| 122.31 \|\|

*striyāḥ samakṣaṃ vijitaḥ patito dharaṇītale \| strīpatirbhavitā bhūyastātaitadatiduṣkaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. again. He, who in a woman's sight has been vanquished and has fallen to the face of the earth, shall further be that woman's husband - this is exceedingly hard, dear father.

## \|\| 122.32 \|\|

*tathāpi kiṃ karomyeṣa satyapāśavaśaṅgataḥ \| kariṣyāmi yathā''ttha tvaṃ bhujyatāṃ nijaśāsanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Nevertheless what am I to do here, who have passed under the power of Truth's fetters? I will do as thou hast said; do thou enjoy thy prevailing in this matter!"

## Chapter 123

## \|\| 123.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca kadācidrājaputro'sau mṛgayāmacaradvane \| mṛgānvidhyanvarāhāṃśca śārdūlādīṃśca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Avíkshit while hunting found a Daitya had seized a maiden who called herself his (Avíkshit's) wife -He killed the Daitya -The gods appeared and offered him a boon -He asked for a son, and they said he should have a son, who would be a universal monarch, by her -She then explained to him she was king Visála's daughter, and told him her history.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. The prince went hunting in the forest one day, piercing deer and wild boars and tigers and other beasts and elephants.

## \|\| 123.2 \|\|

*śuśrāva sahasā śabdaṃ trāhitrāhīti yoṣitaḥ \| vikrośantyāḥ subahuśo bhayagadgadamuccakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suddenly he heard the cry, "Save me! Save me!" from a woman who was screaming aloud very often in a voice

## \|\| 123.3 \|\|

*mābhairmābhairiti vadanrājaputraḥ sa vegitaḥ \| codayāmāsa turagaṃ yataḥ śabdaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. inarticulate through terror. The prince exclaiming, "Fear not! fear not!" urged his horse in haste thither whence the sound

## \|\| 123.4 \|\|

*tataśca sāpi cukrośa kanyakā vijane vane \| gṛhītā danuputreṇa dṛḍhakeśena māninī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. proceeded. And the maiden then cried out, for seized by Danu's son Dridha-kes'a in the lonely forest was she, a highspirited lady: -

## \|\| 123.5 \|\|

*karandhamasutasyāhaṃ bhāryā cāhamavikṣitaḥ \| haratyanāryo vipine pṛthivīśasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. "I belong to Karandhama's son and I am Avíkshit's wife; a villain is carrying off into a thicket me, the wife of the

## \|\| 123.6 \|\|

*yasya sarve mahīpālāstathā gandharvaguhyakāḥ \| na samarthāḥ puraḥ sthātuṃ tasya bhāryā hatāsmyaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. wise king. I, wife of him, before whom all the kings with the Gandharvas and Guhyakas could not stand, am carried

## \|\| 123.7 \|\|

*yasya mṛtyoriva krodhaḥ śakrasyeva parākramaḥ \| karandhamasutasyaiṣā tasya bhāryā hṛtāsmyaham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. off! I here, wife of him, Karandhama's son, whose wrath is like that of Death, whose prowess is like Indra's, am carried off!"

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 123.8 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityākarṇya mahīpālatanayaḥ saśarāsanī \| cintayāmāsa kimidaṃ mama bhāryātra kānane \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing this, the king's son, bearer of the bow, reflected,

## \|\| 123.9 \|\|

*māyeyaṃ rakṣasāṃ nūnaṃ duṣṭānāṃ kānanaukasām \| athavā gata evāhaṃ sarvaṃ vetsyāmi kāraṇam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. "What is this? Have I a wife here in the forest? She is surely an illusion produced by the wicked Rákshasas who inhabit the forest. However I have certainly come; I will ascertain the whole cause."

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 123.10 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tvaritaḥ sa tato gatvā dadarśātimanoramām \|*  
*kānane kanyakāmekāṃ sarvālaṅkārabhūṣitām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hastening on then he beheld a surpassingly fascinating maiden alone in the forest, adorned with every hind of ornament,

## \|\| 123.11 \|\|

*gṛhītāṃ danuputreṇa dṛḍhakeśena daṇḍinā \| trāhitrāhīti karuṇaṃ vikrośantī punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. seized by Danu's son Dridha-kes'a who bore a staff, and screaming out pitifully "Save me! save me!" again and

## \|\| 123.12 \|\|

*mā bhairiti sa tāmāha hato'sīti ca taṃ vadan \| śāsatīmāṃ mahīṃ duṣṭaḥ ko dūyeta karandhame \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. again. "Fear not!" said he to her, and exclaiming "Thou art slain!" to him, he said - "What wicked man exercises rule over this earth while

## \|\| 123.13 \|\|

*yasya pratāpāvanatā bhuvi sarve mahīkṣitaḥ \| tatastamāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhītavarakārmukam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Karandhama is king here, before whose majesty all kings bow down to the earth?"

Seeing him at hand then, grasping his choice bow, the

## \|\| 123.14 \|\|

*māṃ trāhītyāha tanvaṅgī hṛtāsmyeṣeti cāsakṛt \| rājñaḥ karandhamasyāhaṃ snuṣā bhāryāpyavikṣitaḥ \| hṛtāsmyetena duṣṭena sanāthā'nāthavadvane \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. slender-limbed maiden exclaimed more than once -"Save me!" and - "Here I am carried off! I am king Karandhama's daughter-inlaw and Avíkshit's wife. I am carried off by this wicked demon in the forest, -I who belong to a master -as if I belong to no master."

Márkandeya spoke

## \|\| 123.15 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato vimamṛśe vākyamavikṣitsa tathoditam \| kathameṣā hi me bhāryā snuṣā tātasya vā katham \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereupon Avíkshit considered the speech so uttered, " How m truth is she my wife? or how is she my dear father's

## \|\| 123.16 \|\|

*athavā mocayāmyetāṃ tanvīṃ vetsyāmi tatpunaḥ \| kṣatriyairdhāryate śastramārtānāṃ trāṇakāraṇāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. daughter-in-law? However I will set her free, the slender maiden; I will find that out afterwards. Kshatriyas bear arms for the sake of delivering the afflicted."

## \|\| 123.17 \|\|

*tataḥ kuddho'bravīdvīro dānavaṃ taṃ sudurmatim \| jīvangaccha vimucyaināmanyathā na bhaviṣyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the angry hero addressed that most evil-minded Dánava, - "Release her and depart while alive; otherwise

## \|\| 123.18 \|\|

*tataḥ sa tāṃ vihāyoccairdaṇḍamutkṣipya dānavaḥ \| tamapyadhāvatso'pyenaṃ śaravarṣairavākirat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. thou shalt not live!" Quitting her then the Dánava raised his staff aloft and rushed at him; and he also, the prince,

## \|\| 123.19 \|\|

*sa vāryamāṇo bāṇaughairdānavo'timadānvitaḥ \| rājaputrāya cikṣepa daṇḍaṃ śaṃkuśatāvṛtam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. poured a shower of arrows on him. The Dánava, filled with exceeding frenzy, warded them off with a multitude of arrows, and hurled his staff that was studded with a

## \|\| 123.20 \|\|

*tamāpatantaṃ ciccheda śarairbhūpasutastataḥ \|*  
*so'pyāsannaṃ gṛhītvoccairdrumamājau vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. hundred spikes at the prince. The prince split it then, as it was rushing onwards, with arrows. And he, the Dánava, grasping aloft a tree that was near, stood firmly in the battle and

## \|\| 123.21 \|\|

*sṛjataḥ śaravarṣāṇi taṃ cikṣepa tato drumam \| sa ca taṃ tilaśaścaike bhallaiḥ kārmukamocitaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. then hurled that tree at the prince who was discharging clouds of arrows. And he shattered it into mall fragments with

## \|\| 123.22 \|\|

*tataścikṣepa ca śilāṃ rājaputrāya dānavaḥ \| sāpi moghā papātorvyāmujjhitā tena lāghavāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. crescent-headed arrows shot from his bow.And the Dánava next flung a piece of rock at the prince, and it fell vainly on the ground, for he avoided it by agility.

## \|\| 123.23 \|\|

*rājaputrāya kupito yadyaccikṣepa dānavaḥ \| tattacciccheda bāṇaughairbhūbhṛtsūnuḥ salīlayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Whatever the enraged Dánava flung at the prince, each thing the king's son playfully split with multitudes of arrows.

## \|\| 123.24 \|\|

*tato vicchinnadaṇḍo'sau vicchinnasakalāyudhaḥ \| muṣṭimudyamya sakrodho rājaputramadhāvata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then, his staff being shattered and all his weapons shattered, he raised his fist in anger and rushed upon the prince.

## \|\| 123.25 \|\|

*tasyāpatata evāsau karandhamasutaḥ śiraḥ \| chittvā vetasapatreṇa pātayāmāsa vai bhuvi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Karandhama's son struck off his head with a two-edged sword as he was in the act of falling upon him, and felled him to the very ground.

## \|\| 123.26 \|\|

*tasminvinihate devairdānave duṣṭaceṣṭite \| karandhamasutaḥ sarvaiḥ sādhusādhviti bhāṣitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When that Dánava, the evil doer, was slain, all the gods exclaimed to Karandhama's son, "Well done, well done!"

## \|\| 123.27 \|\|

*varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti tadā devairukto nṛpātmajaḥ \| vavre putraṃ mahāvīryaṃ pituḥ priyacikīrṣayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The gods said to the prince then, "Choose thee a boon!" and he replied by reason of his desire to benefit his father, "I choose a son, great in valour."

The gods spoke:

## \|\| 123.28 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ bhaviṣyati hi te putraścakravarttī mahābalaḥ \| asyāmeva hi kanyāyāṃ mokṣitāyāṃ tvayānagha \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Verily thou shalt have a son, who shall be a universal monarch great in valour, by this very maiden in sooth whom thou, O sinless one, hast delivered!

The prince spoke:

## \|\| 123.29 \|\|

*rājaputra uvāca pitrāhaṃ satyapāśena baddha icchāmyahaṃ sutam \| rājabhinirjitenājau tyakto me dārasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Being bound to my father by a bond of truthfulness I wish for a son, but having been vanquished by the kings in fight

## \|\| 123.30 \|\|

*sā ca me yāvatā tyaktā viśālanṛpateḥ sutā \|*  
*tayā ca matkṛte tyakto māmṛte narasaṅgamaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. I have discarded wedlock. And I have abandoned king Visála's daughter, who wanted me, and she has for my

## \|\| 123.31 \|\|

*tatkathaṃ tāmapāsyādya viśālatanayāmaham \| nṛśaṃsātmā kariṣyāmi anyanārīparigraham \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. sake abandoned union with any man but me. How then after discarding her, Visála's daughter, shall I with cruel son marry another woman now?

The gods spoke:

## \|\| 123.32 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ iyameva hi te bhāryā ślāghyate yā tvayā sadā \| viśālasya sutā subhrūstvatkṛte yā''śritā tapaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This very maiden is indeed thy wife, whom thou dost always extol, even Visála's beautiful-browed daughter, who has

## \|\| 123.33 \|\|

*asyāmutpatsyate vīraḥ saptadvīpaprasādhakaḥ \| yaṣṭā yajñasahasrāṇāṃ cakravarttī sutastava \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. devoted herself to austerities for thy sake. Of her shall he born to thee a son who shall be a hero, an embellisher of the seven continents, a sacrificer of a thousand sacrifices, a universal monarch.

Márkandeya spoke

## \|\| 123.34 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ityuccārya yayurdevāḥ karandhamasutaṃ dvija \| so'pyāha tāṃ tadā patnī kathyatāṃ bhīru kintvidam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After announcing this to Karandhama's son the gods departed, O bráhman; and he then addressed her who was

## \|\| 123.35 \|\|

*sā cāsmai kathayāmāsa tyaktāhaṃ bhavatā yadā \| tyaktabandhujanā'raṇyaṃ nirvedātsamupāgatā \|\| 35 \|\|*

## Chapter 124

## \|\| 124.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā smṛtvā pitṛvacaḥ śubham \| kimicchake pratijñāte yaduktaṃ tena bhūbhṛtā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Avíkshit agreed to marry the rescued maiden -The Gandharvas appeared then, and one of them explained she was his daughter and had been born as king Visála's daughter Bháviní because of Agastya's curse -They were married and lived in the Gandharvas' world -She gave birth to a son there -All the celestial beings came to the boy's birth ceremony, and because of the blessings invoked for him from the Maruts he was called Marutta.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. On hearing this her speech, he remembered his father's fine speech which the king had uttered upon the promise regarding

## \|\| 124.2 \|\|

2\. the "What-want-ye" penance, and prince Avíkshit replied to the maiden, he with mind full of love to the maiden who had also abandoned all enjoyments for his sake, -

## \|\| 124.3 \|\|

The maiden spoke:

The prince spoke:

Márkandeya spoke:

## \|\| 124.6 \|\|

## Chapter 125

## \|\| 125.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ sa rājaputrastamādāya dayitaṃ sutam \| patnīṃ cānugato vipra gandharvairāyayau puram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Avíkshit returned and presented his son to his father Karandhama, and there was great rejoicing -The boy grew up, learned in sacred lore and skilful with all weapons -Karandhama resigned the kingdom, but Avíkshit refused it because of the shame of his former captivity -Marutta was made king, and Karandhama retired to the forest.

Márkandeya spoke:

1\. Then the prince, taking that beloved son and followed by his wife and the bráhmans and Gandharvas, went to his

2\. city. Reaching his father's palace he extolled his father's feet with respect; and so did his slender-limbed wife, the bashful

*tathāha rājaputro'sau gṛhītvā bālakaṃ sutam \| dharmāsanagataṃ bhūpaṃ rājñāṃ madhye karandhamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. princess. And the prince holding his infant son addressed king Karandhama, who was seated on the throne of justice in

## \|\| 125.4 \|\|

*mukhaṃ pautrasya paśyaitadutsaṅgasthasya yanmayā \| kimicchake pratijñātaṃ tubhyaṃ mātuḥ kṛte purā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. the midst of kings, -"Behold this face of thy grandson who rests in my lap, as I promised formerly to thee for my mother's

5\. sake at the 'What-want-ye?' vow." So saying he laid that son then on his father's lap, and related to him everything as

## \|\| 125.6 \|\|

*sa pariṣvajya taṃ pautramānandāsrāvilekṣaṇaḥ \| sa bhāgyo'smītyathātmānaṃ praśaśaṃsa punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. it had occurred. The king embracing his grandson, while his eyes were beclouded with tears of joy, felicitated himself again

*tataḥ so'rghyādinā samyaggandharvānsamupāgatān \| sammānayāmāsa mudā vismṛtānyaprayojanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

9\. O great muni. In that glad and opulent city sportive courtesans of the prettiest forms danced an exquisite dance to the

## \|\| 125.10 \|\|

*rājā ca dvijamukhyebhyo ratnāni ca vasūni ca \|*

11\. The boy grew thenceforward, as the moon waxes in its bright fortnight. He was the source of pleasure to his parents, and

17\. Now the king Karandhama had attained his wishes, in that he had seen his son's son and had offered many sacrifices, and had

*sa yiyāsurvanaṃ putramavikṣitamabhāṣata \| putra vṛddho'smi gacchāmi vanaṃ rājyaṃ gṛhāṇa me \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. he was endowed with strength and intelligence. Being desirous of departing to the forest he addressed his son Avíkshit -"My son, I am old, I am going to the forest, take over the

## \|\| 125.20 \|\|

*kṛtakṛtyo'smi nāstyanyatkiñcittvadabhiṣecanāt \|*
